    3.2  istiod — The Control Plane (Deep Dive)
         - istiod is a single binary that replaced 4 separate components (v1.5+)
         - Old architecture: Pilot + Citadel + Galley + sidecar injector (separate pods)
         - New architecture: all merged into one istiod pod
         - What istiod contains:
           a) Pilot: reads Istio CRDs (VirtualService, DestinationRule), converts
              them to Envoy xDS configuration, pushes to all sidecar proxies
           b) Citadel (now: Certificate Authority): issues and rotates mTLS
              certificates for every service in the mesh (SPIFFE/X.509 certs)
           c) Galley (now: Config Validation): validates Istio YAML before applying,
              watches Kubernetes API for changes
           d) Sidecar injector: runs the Kubernetes mutating admission webhook
              that injects the istio-proxy container into new pods
         - istiod runs in istio-system namespace

         🔧 UNDER THE HOOD. Cert rotation never drops a live connection.
           Citadel signs jobpost-api's next cert well before the current
           one's ~24h TTL expires, then pushes it to istio-agent over SDS
           as a fresh "default" secret -- Envoy just presents the new one
           on the NEXT TLS handshake. Any connection already running on
           the old cert keeps going until it closes on its own -- no
           istio-proxy restart, and no request is ever dropped.
         [istiod INTERNALS DIAGRAM — what happens inside istiod]

         [istiod INTERNAL ARCHITECTURE — what lives inside the single binary]
         ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │                        istiod Pod                                 │
         │   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
         │   │   PILOT sub-component (Traffic Config Manager)           │    │
         │   │   • Watches Kubernetes API for:                          │    │
         │   │     - VirtualService changes → convert to Envoy RDS      │    │
         │   │     - DestinationRule changes → convert to Envoy CDS     │    │
         │   │     - Gateway changes → convert to Envoy LDS             │    │
         │   │     - Service/Endpoint changes → convert to Envoy EDS    │    │
         │   │   • Pushes config to Envoy proxies via gRPC/xDS stream   │    │
         │   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
         │   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
         │   │   CITADEL sub-component (Certificate Authority)          │    │
         │   │   • Issues SPIFFE X.509 certificates to every workload   │    │
         │   │   • Certificate identity: spiffe://cluster.local/        │    │
         │   │     ns/anihpj/sa/jobpost-api-service-account            │    │
         │   │   • Rotates certs automatically (default: 24h)           │    │
         │   │   • Stored as Kubernetes Secrets (auto-mounted)          │    │
         │   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
         │   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
         │   │   GALLEY sub-component (Config Validation)               │    │
         │   │   • Validates Istio YAML before it reaches Pilot         │    │
         │   │   • Runs as a Kubernetes Validating Admission Webhook     │    │
         │   │   • Rejects bad config (prevents misconfiguration)       │    │
         │   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
         │                                                                   │
         │   External interfaces:                                            │
         │   • Port 15010: xDS gRPC (plaintext, for mesh-internal only)     │
         │   • Port 15012: xDS gRPC (mTLS, for production)                  │
         │   • Port 15014: Control plane metrics (Prometheus scrape)         │
         │   • Port 443:   Webhook (sidecar injection requests)             │
         └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [ISTIOD EVOLUTION — old vs new architecture]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┐
         │  OLD (Istio < 1.5)               │  NEW (Istio 1.5+)                │
         ├──────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
         │  Pod: pilot (100m/256Mi)         │  Pod: istiod (single binary)     │
         │  Pod: citadel (50m/128Mi)        │  All four merged into one        │
         │  Pod: galley (50m/128Mi)         │  Simpler: 1 deployment to manage │
         │ Pod: sidecar-injector (50m/128Mi)│  Easier upgrades and scaling     │
         │  Total: 4 pods to manage         │  Total: 1 pod (or 3 for HA)      │
         │  Complex communication between   │  In-process calls (faster)       │
         │  them over gRPC                  │  Less failure modes              │
         └──────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┘

    3.3  The Envoy Proxy — Deep Dive
         - Envoy is not just a proxy — it is a "programmable" proxy
         - istiod configures Envoy via the xDS API (Discovery Services):
           • LDS (Listener Discovery Service): which ports to listen on
           • RDS (Route Discovery Service): how to route requests
           • CDS (Cluster Discovery Service): which upstream services exist
           • EDS (Endpoint Discovery Service): which pod IPs are behind a service
         - Envoy's capabilities used by Istio:
           • HTTP request/response manipulation
           • Automatic metrics generation (RED metrics: Rate, Errors, Duration)
           • Distributed tracing header injection (x-b3-traceid, etc.)
           • mTLS termination and origination
           • Circuit breaking and outlier detection
           • Request retries with backoff
           • Fault injection (delays, aborts)
         [xDS PROTOCOL DIAGRAM: istiod → xDS → Envoy configuration flow]

         [HOW istiod CONFIGURES ENVOY — xDS flow]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │                                                        │
         │  You apply YAML:                                       │
         │  kubectl apply -f virtual-service.yaml                 │
         │         │                                             │
         │         ▼                                             │
         │  Kubernetes API Server stores it in etcd              │
         │         │                                             │
         │         ▼                                             │
         │  istiod watches for CRD changes (via informers)       │
         │         │                                             │
         │         ▼                                             │
         │  istiod converts VirtualService → Envoy xDS config    │
         │         │                                             │
         │         ▼  (gRPC streaming, persistent connection)    │
         │  istiod PUSHES config to every affected Envoy proxy   │
         │         │                                             │
         │         ▼                                             │
         │  Envoy proxies update their routing tables in-memory  │
         │  ← No restart needed. Live config update! →           │
         │                                                        │
         │  Total time from kubectl apply to traffic routing:    │
         │  ~1-3 seconds 🚀                                      │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     VISUAL: A SINGLE REQUEST — FULL JOURNEY THROUGH THE ISTIO MESH
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
         ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  TRACE: User clicks "View Job #42" on anihpj website               │
         │                                                                     │
         │  STEP  TIME    COMPONENT              ACTION                       │
         │  ──── ─────── ────────────────────── ────────────────────────────  │
         │   ①    0ms     Browser                GET /jobs/42/                 │
         │                   │                                                │
         │   ②    2ms     Istio Gateway          TLS termination               │
         │                   │  Envoy matches Gateway CRD                     │
         │                   │  Routes to VirtualService                      │
         │                   ▼                                                │
         │   ③    4ms     jobpost-api Pod        Envoy inbound:               │
         │                   ┌─────────────────┐  • Verify mTLS (if internal) │
         │                   │ 🔷 Envoy Sidecar │  • Check AuthorizationPolicy │
         │                   │   (inbound)      │  • Start trace span          │
         │                   │   port 15006     │  • Record request count      │
         │                   └────────┬────────┘  • Forward to Django :8000   │
         │                            │                                       │
         │   ④    5ms     Django Container       views.get_job(id=42)          │
         │                   │  (port 8000)       • Django code runs           │
         │                   │                     • Calls: user-service,      │
         │                   │                       skills-service            │
         │                   ▼                                                │
         │   ⑤    8ms     Envoy Sidecar (out)    Django calls user-service:   │
         │                   ┌─────────────────┐  • iptables redirect → Envoy  │
         │                   │ 🔷 Envoy Sidecar │  • Envoy evaluates VS rules  │
         │                   │   (outbound)     │  • Selects pod via LB        │
         │                   │   port 15001     │  • Initiates mTLS handshake  │
         │                   └────────┬────────┘  • Adds x-b3-traceid header  │
         │                            │                                       │
         │                            │  🔒 mTLS encrypted tunnel             │
         │                            ▼                                       │
         │   ⑥   12ms    user-service Pod        Envoy inbound receives:       │
         │                   ┌─────────────────┐  • Terminates mTLS            │
         │                   │ 🔷 Envoy Sidecar │  • Verifies SPIFFE cert      │
         │                   │   (inbound)      │  • Records inbound span      │
         │                   └────────┬────────┘  • Forwards to Django :8000   │
         │                            │                                       │
         │   ⑦   15ms    Django Container       GET /api/users/42/             │
         │                   │                     • Returns author JSON       │
         │                   ▼                                                │
         │   ⑧   45ms    Response returns        • Envoy records: latency=33ms │
         │                   (back through both   • Status: 200 OK             │
         │                    Envoy proxies)       • Response size: 1.2KB      │
         │                                                                     │
         │   ⑨   50ms    Django (jobpost)        Now calls skills-service:     │
         │                   │                     • Same Envoy hop pattern     │
         │                   ▼                                                │
         │   ⑩   55ms    skills-service Pod      GET /api/skills/?ids=1,2,3   │
         │                   │                     • This service is slow ⚠️    │
         │                   │                     • DB query: 185ms!          │
         │                   ▼                                                │
         │   ⑪  245ms    Response returns         • Envoy records: latency=190ms│
         │                                                                     │
         │   ⑫  250ms    jobpost-api Pod          Django assembles response:   │
         │                   │                     • Merges user + skills data  │
         │                   ▼                                                │
         │   ⑬  255ms    Response → Browser       • Envoy records final span   │
         │                                         • Total: 255ms              │
         │                                         • Traces sent to Jaeger     │
         │                                                                     │
         │  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════    │
         │  KEY TAKEAWAYS FROM THIS TRACE:                                     │
         │                                                                     │
         │  🟢 Gateway + jobpost-api: 4ms overhead (negligible)               │
         │  🟢 user-service call: 33ms total (healthy)                        │
         │  🔴 skills-service call: 190ms (75% of total time!) ← bottleneck   │
         │                                                                     │
         │  Without Istio tracing: you'd only know "page took 255ms"          │
         │  With Istio: you know EXACTLY that skills-service DB is slow       │
         │                                                                     │
         │  Envoy adds ~3-5ms per hop. Business logic + DB = 240ms.           │
         │  Verdict: ~4% overhead for full encryption + observability ✅       │
         └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - Envoy actually speaks a fifth xDS API that the list above didn't
           cover — SDS (Secret Discovery Service), the channel istiod uses
           to stream mTLS certificates straight into Envoy's memory, with
           no cert ever touching disk. Here are all five discovery
           services side by side, one card each:

         [xDS API CARD ROW — the five discovery services, one job each]
         ┌────────────────────────┐  ┌────────────────────────┐  ┌────────────────────────┐
         │ 1. 📡 LDS              │  │ 2. 🧭 RDS              │  │ 3. 🗄 CDS              │
         │ Listener Discovery     │  │ Route Discovery        │  │ Cluster Discovery      │
         │ Configures: listeners  │  │ Configures: route      │  │ Configures: upstream   │
         │ (ports & protocols)    │  │ tables (host/path)     │  │ clusters (LB, subsets) │
         │ Why it matters: no     │  │ Why it matters: VS     │  │ Why it matters: no     │
         │ listener = no traffic  │  │ edits apply live       │  │ cluster = 503 error    │
         └────────────────────────┘  └────────────────────────┘  └────────────────────────┘

         ┌────────────────────────┐  ┌────────────────────────┐
         │ 4. 📍 EDS              │  │ 5. 🔑 SDS              │
         │ Endpoint Discovery     │  │ Secret Discovery       │
         │ Configures: pod IPs    │  │ Configures: mTLS       │
         │ behind each cluster    │  │ certs & keys for Envoy │
         │ Why it matters: most   │  │ Why it matters: certs  │
         │ dynamic xDS API        │  │ never touch disk       │
         └────────────────────────┘  └────────────────────────┘

         - Strip away the acronyms and Envoy is really doing three jobs on
           every single packet: proxying it, policing it, and measuring
           it. anihpj's jobpost-api sidecar runs all three inside the same
           istio-proxy container, on the same request, every time:

         [ENVOY'S THREE ROLES — jobpost-api sidecar, one process, three jobs]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ ZONE 1 — TRAFFIC PROXY  (moves the bytes)                            │
         │                                                                      │
         │ - Intercepts ALL in/out traffic via iptables (:15006 in, :15001 out) │
         │ - Picks a healthy endpoint via EDS and load-balances the connection  │
         │ - Retries safe failures, enforces the route's per-try timeout        │
         │                                                                      │
         │ jobpost-api example: routes GET /jobs/42/ to Django on               │
         │   127.0.0.1:8000                                                     │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ ZONE 2 — POLICY ENFORCEMENT POINT  (guards the bytes)                │
         │                                                                      │
         │ - Originates/terminates mTLS on every hop, checking the SPIFFE cert  │
         │ - Evaluates AuthorizationPolicy: allow, or deny with an RBAC 403     │
         │ - Applies rate limits, circuit breaking, and outlier ejection        │
         │                                                                      │
         │ jobpost-api example: a caller with no valid SPIFFE identity is       │
         │   denied right here — Django never even sees the request             │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ ZONE 3 — TELEMETRY COLLECTOR  (measures the bytes)                   │
         │                                                                      │
         │ - Records RED metrics for every request (rate, errors, duration)     │
         │ - Writes access logs and stamps trace headers (x-b3-traceid)         │
         │ - Exposes /stats/prometheus on :15020 for Prometheus to scrape       │
         │                                                                      │
         │ jobpost-api example: the p99 = 234ms figure from section 9.2 came    │
         │   from THIS Envoy, not from Django instrumentation                   │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - None of these three roles is optional: a packet that skips
           policy enforcement never reaches telemetry, and one that isn't
           measured still gets proxied. All three run together, on the
           same istio-proxy binary, for every hop in the full-journey
           trace above.

    3.4  Automatic Sidecar Injection — How It Works
         - How Istio injects Envoy without changing your Deployment YAML
         - Kubernetes Mutating Admission Webhook: Istio registers a webhook
         - When a Pod is created, Kubernetes calls istiod's webhook FIRST
         - istiod modifies the Pod spec on the fly — adds the istio-proxy container
         - Also adds an init container (istio-init) that sets up iptables rules
         - iptables rules: redirect ALL inbound/outbound traffic through Envoy
         - Enable injection for a namespace: kubectl label namespace anihpj
           istio-injection=enabled
         - Or per-deployment: add annotation sidecar.istio.io/inject: "true"
         [INJECTION FLOW DIAGRAM: Pod creation → webhook → sidecar added]

         [SIDECAR INJECTION FLOW]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │                                                        │
         │  kubectl apply -f jobpost-deployment.yaml              │
         │                       │                               │
         │                       ▼                               │
         │         Kubernetes API Server                          │
         │                       │                               │
         │  "Before I create this Pod, call the Admission         │
         │   Webhooks registered in the cluster"                 │
         │                       │                               │
         │                       ▼                               │
         │  Istio Mutating Admission Webhook (istiod)             │
         │  "I see istio-injection=enabled on this namespace"     │
         │  "Let me modify the Pod spec..."                       │
         │                       │                               │
         │                       ▼                               │
         │  Modified Pod spec returned:                           │
         │  + initContainers: [istio-init]  ← sets iptables      │
         │  + containers: [istio-proxy]     ← Envoy sidecar      │
         │                       │                               │
         │                       ▼                               │
         │  Pod is created with sidecar already inside it        │
         │  Your original jobpost container: UNCHANGED ✅         │
         │                                                        │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    3.5  iptables — How Traffic Is Intercepted
         - iptables is a Linux firewall that redirects network packets
         - istio-init container runs as root to set iptables rules:
           • ALL outbound traffic → redirected to Envoy port 15001
           • ALL inbound traffic → redirected to Envoy port 15006
           • Envoy process itself is excluded (avoid infinite loop)
         - This is completely transparent to your Django app
         - Django thinks it's connecting directly to user-service:80
         - In reality: Django → iptables → Envoy → mTLS tunnel → remote Envoy → user-service

         🧠 ANALOGY. iptables interception is like a hotel's phone
           switchboard. A guest dials another room's extension normally
           and never learns an operator exists -- but every call is
           silently patched through the operator first, who logs it,
           times it, and can reroute it. Django "dials" user-service on
           port 80 the exact same way every time; iptables is the
           switchboard quietly connecting that call through Envoy instead.
         [IPTABLES REDIRECT DIAGRAM showing the invisible interception]

         [IPTABLES PACKET JOURNEY — step by step through the network stack]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  OUTBOUND (jobpost-api calling user-service):                      │
         │                                                                    │
         │  ① Django code:  requests.get("http://user-service/api/users/")   │
         │  ② OS resolves:  user-service → ClusterIP 10.96.45.23:80          │
         │  ③ Packet enters: Linux network stack, destination 10.96.45.23:80 │
         │  ④ iptables rule: "OUTPUT chain → redirect to 127.0.0.1:15001"   │
         │  ⑤ Envoy receives packet on port 15001 (outbound listener)        │
         │  ⑥ Envoy looks up: "who is 10.96.45.23?" → it is user-service    │
         │  ⑦ Envoy applies:  routing rules, timeout, retry, circuit breaker │
         │  ⑧ Envoy initiates mTLS: presents jobpost-api certificate         │
         │  ⑨ Packet sent to: user-service Pod IP:15006 (not :80!)           │
         │                                                                    │
         │  INBOUND (user-service receiving):                                 │
         │                                                                    │
         │  ① Packet arrives at user-service Pod:15006                       │
         │  ② iptables rule: "PREROUTING → redirect to 127.0.0.1:15006"     │
         │  ③ Envoy receives on port 15006 (inbound listener)                │
         │  ④ Envoy verifies: mTLS certificate from jobpost-api Envoy       │
         │  ⑤ Envoy checks:   AuthorizationPolicy (is jobpost-api allowed?)  │
         │  ⑥ Envoy records:  request metric (latency timer starts)          │
         │  ⑦ Envoy forwards: to 127.0.0.1:8000 (Django on localhost)        │
         │  ⑧ Django sees:    normal HTTP request, no TLS needed!            │
         │                                                                    │
         │  KEY INSIGHT: Django never sees TLS. Envoy handles it all.        │
         │  Django talks plain HTTP on localhost. Envoy handles encryption    │
         │  between pods. Your code changes: ZERO. ✅                         │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [IPTABLES RULES SET BY istio-init — the actual commands]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  # Rules added by istio-init container (simplified):               │
         │                                                                    │
         │  # Redirect ALL outbound traffic to Envoy port 15001               │
         │  iptables -t nat -A OUTPUT -p tcp \                                │
         │    ! --dport 15001 \                   ← skip Envoy's own traffic  │
         │    -m owner ! --uid-owner 1337 \       ← skip Envoy process (uid) │
         │    -j REDIRECT --to-ports 15001                                    │
         │                                                                    │
         │  # Redirect ALL inbound traffic to Envoy port 15006                │
         │  iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -p tcp \                            │
         │    -j REDIRECT --to-ports 15006                                    │
         │                                                                    │
         │  # Exception: do NOT redirect traffic from Envoy itself            │
         │  # (Envoy runs as UID 1337 — exempt from redirection)              │
         │  iptables -t nat -A OUTPUT -m owner \                              │
         │    --uid-owner 1337 -j RETURN                                      │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    3.6  Istio Components in the Cluster (What Pods Run)
         - istio-system namespace contains:
           • istiod — the control plane (1 deployment, 1-3 replicas for HA)
           • istio-ingressgateway — handles inbound traffic (LoadBalancer service)
           • istio-egressgateway — handles outbound traffic (optional)
           • Kiali — service mesh visualization dashboard
           • Prometheus — metrics scraping (can use existing)
           • Grafana — dashboards (can use existing)
           • Jaeger/Zipkin — distributed tracing
         [TABLE: Component | Namespace | Purpose | Resource usage]

         | Component             | Namespace    | Purpose                                |
         | ──────────────────────│──────────────│────────────────────────────────────── │
         | istiod                | istio-system | Control plane — configures all proxies  |
         | istio-ingressgateway  | istio-system | Ingress to the mesh (LoadBalancer)      |
         | istio-egressgateway   | istio-system | Controlled egress from mesh (optional)  |
         | kiali                 | istio-system | Mesh topology + traffic visualization   |
         | prometheus            | istio-system | Metrics collection from Envoy proxies   |
         | grafana               | istio-system | Metrics dashboards (pre-built for Istio)|
         | jaeger                | istio-system | Distributed tracing (trace spans)       |

    3.7  Sidecar Debugging Checklist — When Things Go Wrong
         - DEFINITION: sidecar debugging = a fixed, ordered routine that tells
           you WHY a pod is not meshed, not synced, or not routing traffic
         - Why it matters: most "Istio is broken" tickets on anihpj are one of
           six repeat symptoms → memorize the symptom-to-first-command mapping
         - How it works: every check reads LIVE state — either from the
           Kubernetes API (labels, webhook, events) or from Envoy itself
           (istioctl proxy-config reads the proxy's in-memory tables)
         - Golden order: INJECTION → SYNC → CONFIG → TRAFFIC
           → never start by editing YAML blindly; observe first, change second
         - The modern toolbox (Istio 1.22+) — commit these five to memory:
           • istioctl proxy-status               → is every proxy SYNCED?
           • istioctl x describe pod <pod>       → one-pod mesh summary
             (shows matching VirtualServices, DestinationRules, mTLS mode)
           • istioctl proxy-config <section> <pod> → Envoy's live config
             (sections: listener / route / cluster / endpoint / secret)
           • kubectl logs <pod> -c istio-proxy   → Envoy runtime errors
           • istioctl analyze -n anihpj          → static config lint
         - ⚠️ "istioctl authn tls-check" was REMOVED years ago — never answer
           with it; use istioctl x describe pod / proxy-config secret instead

         [SIDECAR SYMPTOM CHECKLIST — the six repeat offenders in anihpj]
         ┌────┬────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┐
         │ □  │ Symptom (what you see)         │ First command to run       │
         ├────┼────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
         │ □1 │ Pod READY 1/1 — no sidecar     │ kubectl get ns anihpj      │
         │    │ container was ever injected    │   --show-labels            │
         ├────┼────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
         │ □2 │ Pod 2/2 but follows OLD routes │ istioctl proxy-status      │
         │    │ minutes after kubectl apply    │   → any STALE / NOT SENT?  │
         ├────┼────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
         │ □3 │ Calls to a service return 503  │ istioctl proxy-config      │
         │    │ "no healthy upstream"          │   endpoint deploy/<name>   │
         ├────┼────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
         │ □4 │ Plaintext caller gets TCP      │ istioctl x describe pod    │
         │    │ connection RESET (not 403!)    │   <pod> → mTLS STRICT?     │
         ├────┼────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
         │ □5 │ istio-proxy CrashLoopBackOff   │ kubectl logs <pod>         │
         │    │ or pod never leaves Init state │   -c istio-proxy -n anihpj │
         ├────┼────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
         │ □6 │ mTLS errors: unknown identity, │ istioctl proxy-config      │
         │    │ certificate expired            │   secret deploy/<name>     │
         └────┴────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┘

         [QUICK-DEBUG COMMAND TABLE — exact commands for deploy/jobpost-api]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  # 1. Is every proxy in the mesh synced with istiod?             │
         │  istioctl proxy-status                                           │
         │     → want: CDS/LDS/EDS/RDS all "SYNCED" for every workload      │
         │                                                                  │

         │  istioctl proxy-config listener deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj     │

         │  istioctl proxy-config cluster  deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj     │
         │  istioctl proxy-config endpoint deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj     │
         │  istioctl proxy-config secret   deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj     │
         │                                                                  │
         │  # 4. Envoy runtime logs (rejected config, TLS handshake fails)  │
         │  kubectl logs deploy/jobpost-api -c istio-proxy -n anihpj        │
         │                                                                  │
         │  # 5. Static lint of all Istio config in the namespace           │

         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - REAL SCENARIO (anihpj, day 12): skills-service came back 1/1 after
           a node drain. Checklist □1 → namespace label was fine; □2 → the pod
           was missing from istioctl proxy-status entirely → it had been
           recreated WHILE the injection webhook was down during an istiod
           upgrade. Fix: kubectl delete pod → recreated 2/2, SYNCED in ~3s ✅

    3.8  Inside Envoy — Proxy Configuration Hierarchy
         - DEFINITION: Envoy stores its running config as four stacked tables —
           Listeners (LDS), Routes (RDS), Clusters (CDS), Endpoints (EDS)

         📖 KEY TERM. xDS = the umbrella name for the FOUR discovery
           protocols shown above -- LDS, RDS, CDS, and EDS. An exam prompt
           that says "trace it through the xDS pipeline" means this whole
           four-table stack, not just one API.
         - Why it matters: every istioctl proxy-config command reads exactly
           ONE of these tables — the hierarchy tells you WHICH one to read
         - How a request walks the hierarchy (top → bottom):
           • LDS: "a packet hit 15001/15006 — which listener owns it?"
           • RDS: "which route matches this Host header + path?"
           • CDS: "route points at a cluster — does that cluster exist?"
           • EDS: "which healthy pod IPs are members of that cluster?"
         - Istio CRD → xDS mapping (memorize):
           → Gateway → LDS   → VirtualService → RDS
           → DestinationRule → CDS   → Service/Endpoints → EDS
         - DEBUG BOTTOM-UP: endpoints first (no healthy pods = nothing else
           matters), then cluster, then route, then listener last

         [ENVOY CONFIG HIERARCHY — the four xDS tables inside every sidecar]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  REQUEST ENTERS ENVOY                                            │
         │      │                                                           │
         │      ▼                                                           │
         │  ┌─ 1. LDS — LISTENERS ─────────────────────────────────────┐    │
         │  │ "Which ports do I own?" → 15001, 15006, 15021, 15090     │    │
         │  │ Fed by: Gateway CRDs + mesh defaults                     │    │
         │  │ Read: istioctl proxy-config listener deploy/jobpost-api  │    │
         │  └────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘    │
         │                               ▼                                  │
         │  ┌─ 2. RDS — ROUTES ────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
         │  │ "Which rule matches Host + path?" (VirtualService)       │    │
         │  │ Fed by: VirtualService CRDs                              │    │
         │  │ Read: istioctl proxy-config route deploy/jobpost-api     │    │
         │  └────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘    │
         │                               ▼                                  │
         │  ┌─ 3. CDS — CLUSTERS ──────────────────────────────────────┐    │
         │  │ "Which upstream services and subsets exist?"             │    │
         │  │ Fed by: DestinationRule CRDs + Service registry          │    │
         │  │ Read: istioctl proxy-config cluster deploy/jobpost-api   │    │
         │  └────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘    │
         │                               ▼                                  │
         │  ┌─ 4. EDS — ENDPOINTS ─────────────────────────────────────┐    │
         │  │ "Which healthy pod IPs back that cluster?"               │    │
         │  │ Fed by: K8s Endpoints (istiod bypasses kube-proxy)       │    │
         │  │ Read: istioctl proxy-config endpoint deploy/jobpost-api  │    │
         │  └────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘    │
         │                               ▼                                  │
         │  PACKET LEAVES → mTLS to the chosen pod's Envoy on :15006        │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [BOTTOM-UP DEBUG ORDER — always start at EDS, finish at LDS]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  Symptom: calls to skills-service time out or return 503         │
         │                                                                  │
         │  STEP 1 — EDS (endpoints): are there healthy pod IPs?            │
         │    istioctl proxy-config endpoint deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj   │
         │    ❌ empty or UNHEALTHY → no ready pods / outlier ejection       │
         │       (skills-service at 8.1% errors gets ejected!) — STOP HERE  │
         │    ✅ healthy IPs listed → continue to STEP 2                     │
         │                                                                  │
         │  STEP 2 — CDS (clusters): does the target cluster exist?         │
         │    istioctl proxy-config cluster deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj    │
         │    ❌ no outbound|8090||skills-service... → DestinationRule /     │
         │       subset problem                                             │
         │                                                                  │
         │  STEP 3 — RDS (routes): is your VirtualService rule present?     │
         │    istioctl proxy-config route deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj      │
         │    ❌ rule missing → VS not applied, or host typo                 │
         │                                                                  │
         │  STEP 4 — LDS (listeners): is Envoy even listening?              │
         │    istioctl proxy-config listener deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj   │
         │    ❌ 15001/15006 missing → injection or iptables broken          │
         │                                                                  │
         │  All four ✅ but still failing? → kubectl logs -c istio-proxy     │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    3.9  Deep Dive — Envoy Filter Chain & Full Request Lifecycle
         - DEFINITION: a filter chain is Envoy's internal assembly line —
           every packet passes an ordered list of filters before it may leave
         - Why it matters: when an Istio feature "does nothing", the usual
           cause is that the packet never reached the filter implementing it
         - Three filter layers, in fixed order:
           • Listener filters → connection-level peeking (tls_inspector asks
             "TLS or plaintext?"; original_dst recovers the real destination
             address that iptables rewrote)
           • Network filters  → L4, run for ALL traffic (http_connection_
             manager for HTTP, tcp_proxy for raw TCP, rbac for authorization)
           • HTTP filters     → L7, ONLY when http_connection_manager runs
             (jwt_authn, cors, fault, stats, router — router is ALWAYS last)
         - → this is why TCP services get no retries/fault-injection: those
           live in HTTP filters that plain TCP traffic never reaches
         - The sidecar's port map (memorize for the exam):
           • 15001 outbound capture   • 15006 inbound capture
           • 15021 health/readiness   • 15090 raw Envoy stats
           • 15020 istio-agent — merged app + Envoy metrics; Prometheus
             scrapes THIS port, not 15090

         [ENVOY FILTER CHAIN — inbound packet through jobpost-api's sidecar]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  packet arrives on :15006 (iptables PREROUTING redirect)         │
         │        │                                                         │
         │        ▼                                                         │
         │  LISTENER FILTERS ("what is this connection?")                   │
         │   • tls_inspector → TLS or plaintext? (STRICT mTLS + plaintext   │
         │                     = TCP connection RESET, never an HTTP 403)   │
         │   • original_dst  → recover real destination iptables rewrote    │
         │        │                                                         │
         │        ▼                                                         │
         │  NETWORK FILTERS (L4 — run for ALL traffic)                      │
         │   • istio_authn             → verify SPIFFE peer certificate     │
         │   • rbac                    → enforce AuthorizationPolicy        │
         │   • http_connection_manager → hand HTTP traffic to L7 filters    │
         │     (tcp_proxy instead if raw TCP, e.g. PostgreSQL on 5432)      │
         │        │                                                         │
         │        ▼                                                         │
         │  HTTP FILTERS (L7 — HTTP/gRPC only)                              │
         │   • jwt_authn → validate JWT (RequestAuthentication)             │
         │   • cors      → cross-origin rules                               │
         │   • fault     → inject delays/aborts (VirtualService fault)      │
         │   • stats     → record RED metrics (rate/errors/duration)        │
         │   • router    → ALWAYS LAST: pick route → cluster → endpoint     │
         │        │                                                         │
         │        ▼                                                         │
         │  forward to 127.0.0.1:8000 (Django, plain HTTP on localhost)     │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [FULL REQUEST LIFECYCLE — browser → gateway → sidecar → Django]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  🌐 Browser: GET https://api.anihpj.com/jobs/42/                  │
         │        │  public TLS on :443                                     │
         │        ▼                                                         │
         │  [istio-ingressgateway]  (standalone Envoy, no app container)    │
         │    • LDS: listener bound by the Gateway CRD                      │
         │    • terminates public TLS, matches VirtualService route         │
         │    • RDS: /jobs/* → cluster outbound|8000||jobpost-api...        │
         │        │  🔒 mTLS: gateway cert ↔ jobpost-api sidecar cert        │
         │        ▼                                                         │
         │  [jobpost-api pod — INBOUND side]                                │
         │    • iptables PREROUTING → Envoy :15006                          │
         │    • filter chain: tls_inspector → istio_authn → rbac → HTTP     │
         │    • forwards to Django on 127.0.0.1:8000 (plain HTTP)           │
         │        │                                                         │
         │        ▼                                                         │
         │  Django view runs → needs the author → calls user-service        │
         │        │                                                         │
         │        ▼                                                         │
         │  [jobpost-api pod — OUTBOUND side]                               │
         │    • iptables OUTPUT (UID != 1337) → Envoy :15001                │
         │    • RDS route for user-service → CDS cluster → EDS pod IP       │
         │    • 🔒 new mTLS tunnel to user-service sidecar :15006            │
         │        │                                                         │
         │        ▼                                                         │
         │  [user-service pod] :15006 → filters → app on :8080              │
         │        │  response retraces the same path in reverse             │
         │        ▼                                                         │
         │  🌐 Browser receives 200 OK — every hop encrypted + measured      │
         │                                                                  │
         │  SIDE PORTS (never in the request path):                         │
         │   :15021 kubelet health probes    :15090 raw Envoy stats         │
         │   :15020 istio-agent merges app + Envoy metrics for Prometheus   │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - REAL SCENARIO (anihpj, day 19): a fault-injection rule "did
           nothing" for search-service traffic. Root cause: the Service port
           was named "tcp-search", so Envoy installed only tcp_proxy and the
           fault HTTP filter never saw a request. Renaming the port to
           "http-search" switched the chain to L7 — the fault fired instantly

     CHAPTER 3: DAILY WORK TAKEAWAYS
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    After this chapter, in your daily work you will:
      • Visualize the two planes: data plane (sidecars doing the work)
        and control plane (istiod configuring everything)
      • Know that istiod merged 4 components into 1 binary (simpler ops!)
      • Understand how xDS pushes config from istiod to Envoy in ~1-3 seconds
      • Know exactly what happens during sidecar injection (mutating webhook)
      • Understand iptables interception — your code thinks it talks directly
        to user-service:80, but Envoy intercepts and encrypts everything
      • Know what pods run in istio-system and what each one does
      • Be able to check proxy sync status: istioctl proxy-status

    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     CHAPTER 3: ICA EXAM TIPS & QUESTIONS
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    🎯 ICA EXAM FOCUS (Foundation — feeds all 5 domains):
      • "Check if all proxies are synced" = istioctl proxy-status
      • "What port does Envoy listen on for inbound traffic?" = 15006
      • "How does traffic get redirected to Envoy?" = iptables rules by istio-init
      • "What runs in istio-system namespace?" = istiod, ingressgateway, addons
      • "Traffic not routing — debug order?" = endpoint → cluster → route →
        listener (bottom-up through EDS / CDS / RDS / LDS)
      • "Verify a workload certificate" = istioctl proxy-config secret
        (istioctl authn tls-check was REMOVED — never pick it)
      • "Which port does Prometheus scrape?" = 15020 (istio-agent, merged
        app + Envoy metrics; 15090 is the raw Envoy stats port)

    Q1: What command checks if all Envoy proxies are synchronized with istiod?
    A1: istioctl proxy-status

    Q2: What are the four sub-components merged into the single istiod binary?
    A2: Pilot (traffic config), Citadel (certificates/mTLS), Galley (config
        validation), and the sidecar injector (mutating admission webhook)

    Q3: How does the istio-init container redirect traffic to Envoy?
    A3: By setting iptables rules: outbound → port 15001, inbound → port 15006.
        Envoy's own traffic (UID 1337) is exempt from redirection.

    Q4: New pods in the anihpj namespace suddenly come up 1/1 with no sidecar,
        although the namespace still carries istio-injection=enabled. What do
        you check first, and how do you prove injection works end-to-end?
    A4: Check the webhook object: kubectl get mutatingwebhookconfiguration
        istio-sidecar-injector. If it is missing or its CA bundle is broken,
        the API server never calls istiod, so Pods are persisted unmodified.
        Prove it end-to-end with a server-side dry run:
        kubectl apply --dry-run=server -o yaml -f pod.yaml | grep istio-proxy
        → the output must contain the injected istio-proxy container.
        Why: injection happens ONLY at Pod creation, inside the admission
        chain — if the webhook is gone, nothing else can add the sidecar.

    Q5: Why do the iptables rules written by istio-init exempt traffic owned
        by UID 1337, and what exactly would break without that exemption?
    A5: UID 1337 is the user the istio-proxy (Envoy) container runs as. The
        rule "-m owner ! --uid-owner 1337 -j REDIRECT --to-ports 15001"
        redirects everyone EXCEPT Envoy. Without it, Envoy's own outbound
        packets would be redirected back into Envoy on :15001 → an infinite
        redirect loop; no packet would ever leave the pod. Verify with:
        kubectl exec deploy/jobpost-api -c istio-proxy -n anihpj -- id
        → uid=1337(istio-proxy).

    Q6: You applied a VirtualService 10 minutes ago, but one jobpost-api pod
        still routes with the old rules. istioctl proxy-status marks that
        proxy STALE. What does STALE mean and how do you recover?
    A6: STALE = the proxy is connected but has not acknowledged istiod's
        latest xDS push (SYNCED = ACKed latest; NOT SENT = istiod could not
        deliver at all). Normal propagation is ~1-3s, so minutes = a stuck
        stream. Recover: confirm the pod can reach istiod on port 15012, then
        force a reconnect — kubectl exec <pod> -c istio-proxy -n anihpj --
        curl -X POST localhost:15000/quitquitquit (Envoy restarts and
        re-subscribes to xDS) — or simply kubectl delete pod <pod> -n anihpj.

    Q7: Prove that the jobpost-api workload really holds a valid SPIFFE
        identity certificate, and state the exact SPIFFE URI you expect.
    A7: Dump what Envoy is serving: istioctl proxy-config secret
        deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj -o json, base64-decode the "default"
        cert and read it with openssl x509 -noout -text — the URI SAN must be
        spiffe://cluster.local/ns/anihpj/sa/jobpost-api (trust domain /
        namespace / service account). istioctl x describe pod <pod> confirms
        the effective mTLS mode. Never answer "istioctl authn tls-check" —
        that command was removed years ago.

    Q8: What does istioctl proxy-config secret deploy/user-service -n anihpj
        show, and how do you read certificate health from its output?
    A8: It lists the workload's SDS secrets: "default" (the workload cert)
        and "ROOTCA", with STATUS, SERIAL NUMBER, NOT BEFORE / NOT AFTER.
        Healthy = STATUS "VALID CERT" with NOT AFTER within ~24h (istiod
        rotates workload certs daily). "CERT NOT FOUND" or an expired window
        means the SDS stream from istio-agent to istiod is broken → check
        kubectl logs <pod> -c istio-proxy for SDS/CA errors.

    Q9: A VirtualService fault-injection rule (HTTP 500 abort) has no effect
        on notification-service, though the identical pattern works for
        jobpost-api. The Service port is named "tcp-notify". Why, and what
        is the fix?
    A9: The port name tells Istio the protocol. "tcp-*" → Envoy installs only
        the tcp_proxy network filter, so the HTTP filter chain (fault, cors,
        jwt_authn, router) NEVER runs — L4 traffic cannot use L7 features.
        Fix: rename the port to "http-notify" (or set appProtocol: http) and
        re-apply; the listener then uses http_connection_manager and the
        fault filter fires.

    Q10: jobpost-api gets 503 "no healthy upstream" when calling
         skills-service. Give the bottom-up istioctl sequence you would run
         and what each step rules out.
    A10: Walk the xDS hierarchy from the bottom:
         ① istioctl proxy-config endpoint deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj —
           empty/UNHEALTHY → no ready pods or outlier ejection (likely here:
           skills-service degraded at 8.1% errors / 1240ms gets ejected)
         ② istioctl proxy-config cluster deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj —
           outbound|8090||skills-service... missing → DestinationRule/subset
         ③ istioctl proxy-config route deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj —
           rule absent → VirtualService not applied, or host typo
         ④ istioctl proxy-config listener deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj —
           15001/15006 missing → injection or iptables broken
         Why bottom-up: if EDS is empty nothing above it matters — this
         ordering finds the root cause in the fewest commands.

         - Pulling the filter-chain detail back out to the full journey, a
           request crosses exactly six waypoints between the browser and
           the Django code that finally handles it:

         [REQUEST LIFECYCLE — 6 WAYPOINTS AT A GLANCE]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ REQUEST LIFECYCLE — 6 WAYPOINTS AT A GLANCE  (jobpost-api)                 │
         │                                                                            │
         │ 1. CLIENT — browser/caller issues the request                              │
         │    GET https://api.anihpj.com/jobs/42/  (public TLS on :443)               │
         │                                                                            │
         │                                      ▼                                     │
         │                                                                            │
         │ 2. INGRESS GATEWAY ENVOY — standalone Envoy, no app container              │
         │    Terminates public TLS, matches the Gateway + VirtualService             │
         │                                                                            │
         │                                      ▼                                     │
         │                                                                            │
         │ 3. NETWORK FILTERS  (mTLS / authz) — L4 — run for ALL traffic              │
         │    tls_inspector checks TLS-or-plaintext, istio_authn verifies the         │
         │    SPIFFE peer cert, rbac enforces AuthorizationPolicy — all BEFORE        │
         │    any HTTP parsing happens                                                │
         │                                                                            │
         │                                      ▼                                     │
         │                                                                            │
         │ 4. HTTP FILTER CHAIN  (routing / retries) — L7 — HTTP/gRPC only            │
         │    jwt_authn, cors, fault, stats each run in order, then router —          │
         │    router is ALWAYS last: it picks the route to forward                    │
         │                                                                            │
         │                                      ▼                                     │
         │                                                                            │
         │ 5. UPSTREAM CLUSTER SELECTION — CDS + EDS + load balancing                 │
         │    CDS supplies the cluster, EDS supplies a healthy pod IP, the            │
         │    LB policy (e.g. ROUND_ROBIN, LEAST_REQUEST) picks the endpoint          │
         │                                                                            │
         │                                      ▼                                     │
         │                                                                            │
         │ 6. APPLICATION CONTAINER — Django on 127.0.0.1:8000                        │
         │    views.get_job(id=42) runs — Envoy never touches business logic,         │
         │    it only measured and secured the trip getting here                      │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - Every waypoint costs time. For a HEALTHY jobpost-api request
           (not the skills-service outlier from section 3.3's trace), here
           is where the canonical p99 budget of 234ms (section 9.2) is
           actually spent:

         [p99 LATENCY BUDGET — where jobpost-api's 234ms goes]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ jobpost-api GET /jobs/ — WHERE THE p99 BUDGET (234ms) GOES           │
         │                                                                      │
         │ Client → Gateway (network hop)      █░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░    2ms      │
         │ Gateway Envoy (TLS + route match)   █░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░    2ms      │
         │ mTLS handshake (sidecar ↔ sidecar)  █░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░    2ms      │
         │ Inbound filter chain (L4 + L7)      █░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░    2ms      │
         │ Django app + downstream calls       ████████████████████  224ms      │
         │ Outbound re-encrypt + return trip   █░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░    2ms      │
         │                                                                      │
         │ Mesh/Envoy overhead: 10ms of 234ms total ≈ 4%                        │
         │ (matches the ~4% overhead verdict from the full-journey trace above) │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - The mesh's own tax is tiny: ~10ms of 234ms, about 4% —
           matching the "~4% overhead" verdict from the full-journey trace
           in section 3.3. The other 96% was never Envoy's to save; it is
           Django, its downstream calls, and the database underneath them.


    3.10  The istio-cni Plugin — An Alternative to istio-init
         - DEFINITION: istio-cni is a chained CNI plugin that writes the
           SAME iptables redirect rules as the istio-init container (3.5),
           but from one privileged DaemonSet pod per node instead of a
           privileged init container inside every application Pod
         - Why it matters: istio-init needs the NET_ADMIN and NET_RAW
           capabilities on every injected Pod. Many clusters block that
           under the Kubernetes "restricted" Pod Security Admission level,
           or under org RBAC policy — istio-cni removes that requirement
           from application namespaces entirely
         - How it works:
           • enable at install time: components.cni.enabled: true in the
             IstioOperator spec (or --set pilot.cni.enabled=true in Helm)
           • istio-cni runs as the istio-cni-node DaemonSet, one Pod per
             node in istio-system — it chains AFTER the primary CNI
             (Calico, Flannel, etc.) during kubelet's pod-network setup
           • when a new Pod is scheduled, the chained plugin writes the
             outbound→15001 / inbound→15006 rules into that Pod's network
             namespace BEFORE any of its containers ever start
           • the Pod still gets the istio-proxy sidecar container from the
             mutating webhook (3.4) — it simply never gets an istio-init
             entry in its initContainers list
         - Verify it is active: kubectl get daemonset -n istio-system
           istio-cni-node → want DESIRED = CURRENT = READY = node count

         [ISTIO-INIT vs ISTIO-CNI — same iptables job, different privilege model]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┐
         │  istio-init (default)            │  istio-cni plugin                │
         ├──────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
         │  Runs in every Pod               │  Runs once per node              │
         │  Needs NET_ADMIN+NET_RAW         │  Only the node needs it          │
         │  Blocked by strict PSA           │  Works with restricted PSA       │
         │  Adds an initContainer           │  No initContainer added          │
         │  Default behavior                │  cni.enabled: true               │
         │  No extra DaemonSet              │  istio-cni-node DaemonSet        │
         └──────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┘

         [SIDECAR INJECTION WITH CNI — no istio-init in the Pod spec]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  kubectl apply -f jobpost-deployment.yaml                          │
         │  ▼                                                                 │
         │  Kubernetes API Server + istiod Mutating Webhook                   │
         │  adds ONLY the istio-proxy container (no istio-init this time)     │
         │  ▼                                                                 │
         │  kubelet creates the Pod's network namespace                       │
         │  ▼                                                                 │
         │  Primary CNI plugin (Calico / Flannel / etc.) wires up networking  │
         │  ▼                                                                 │
         │  istio-cni chained plugin runs next, in that SAME callback         │
         │  writes outbound→15001 / inbound→15006 iptables rules (3.5)        │
         │  ▼                                                                 │
         │  Pod starts already 2/2 — redirection was live before Envoy        │
         │  or Django ever executed a single line                             │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - REAL SCENARIO (anihpj, day 27): the platform-security team
           enforced Pod Security "restricted" cluster-wide, which silently
           blocked every new istio-init container (NET_ADMIN denied) and
           left new Pods running with NO sidecar and no error visible in
           kubectl describe. Fix: reinstalled with
           components.cni.enabled: true and re-rolled the Deployments —
           injection succeeded with zero changes to any Pod spec

    3.11  Inside the istio-proxy Container — pilot-agent + Envoy
         - DEFINITION: the istio-proxy container that injection adds (3.4)
           is not one process — it runs TWO: pilot-agent (also called
           istio-agent in the docs) and Envoy, started in that order
         - Why it matters: SDS certificates, Envoy's bootstrap config, the
           merged metrics endpoint (3.9's port 15020), and Pod readiness
           are ALL produced by pilot-agent, not Envoy — when one of those
           breaks, kubectl logs -c istio-proxy is showing a pilot-agent
           error, and 3.7's proxy-config commands go quiet because Envoy
           itself never finished starting
         - How it works, in start-up order:
           • pilot-agent generates Envoy's bootstrap config — istiod's
             address, node/cluster metadata, trust domain — and writes it
             to disk before Envoy ever runs
           • pilot-agent creates a private key + CSR, then sends the CSR
             to istiod's CA over gRPC for signing (3.2's Citadel duty)
           • pilot-agent execs Envoy as a child process, pointing it at
             that bootstrap file; Envoy then opens its own xDS stream
           • Envoy asks pilot-agent locally for the signed cert + root CA
             over the Secret Discovery Service (SDS) API — the "default"
             and "ROOTCA" secrets 3.7's proxy-config secret command shows
           • pilot-agent polls Envoy's own health endpoint, and only then
             lets the kubelet readiness probe on :15021 start succeeding
           • pilot-agent keeps running for the Pod's lifetime, serving the
             merged app+Envoy metrics endpoint on :15020 (3.9)
           • the istio-init container (3.5) runs pilot-agent's
             istio-iptables logic directly; istio-cni (3.10) reuses that
             same rule-writing logic from its node DaemonSet instead

         [INSIDE THE istio-proxy CONTAINER — pilot-agent starts Envoy]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  ① pilot-agent starts first inside the istio-proxy container       │
         │     builds Envoy bootstrap config: istiod address, node/cluster    │
         │     metadata, trust domain — written to disk before Envoy runs     │
         │                                                                    │
         │  ② pilot-agent creates a private key + CSR, sends the CSR to       │
         │     istiod for signing over gRPC (3.2's Citadel sub-component)     │
         │                                                                    │
         │  ③ pilot-agent execs Envoy as a child process, pointing it at      │
         │     that bootstrap file — Envoy then opens its own xDS stream      │
         │                                                                    │
         │  ④ Envoy asks pilot-agent locally for the signed cert + root CA    │
         │     via the Secret Discovery Service (SDS) API — the "default"     │
         │     and "ROOTCA" secrets 3.7's proxy-config secret command shows   │
         │                                                                    │
         │  ⑤ pilot-agent polls Envoy's health endpoint; only then does the   │
         │     kubelet readiness probe on :15021 start succeeding             │
         │                                                                    │
         │  ⑥ pilot-agent keeps serving the merged metrics endpoint on        │
         │     :15020 for as long as the Pod is alive (see 3.9)               │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [pilot-agent vs ENVOY AT A GLANCE]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┐
         │  pilot-agent (istio-agent)       │  Envoy                           │
         ├──────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
         │  Builds Envoy bootstrap config   │  Reads that config at startup    │
         │  Requests + rotates SPIFFE cert  │  Terminates/originates mTLS      │
         │  Serves certs to Envoy via SDS   │  Fetches certs over local SDS    │
         │  Runs istio-iptables (3.5,3.10)  │  Never touches iptables itself   │
         │  Polls Envoy for readiness       │  Answers kubelet on :15021       │
         │  Merged metrics on :15020        │  Raw Envoy stats on :15090       │
         │  Debug: pilot-agent request      │  Admin API on :15000             │
         └──────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┘

         - REAL SCENARIO (anihpj, day 33): istio-proxy sat in
           CrashLoopBackOff on a freshly drained node. kubectl logs
           -c istio-proxy showed a pilot-agent error, not an Envoy one —
           "failed to get certificate: rpc error: context deadline
           exceeded" — istiod itself was mid-rollout and unreachable on
           :15012 for about 40s. No proxy-config command could help,
           because Envoy had never started; the fix was simply waiting
           out the istiod rollout, confirmed once istioctl proxy-status
           listed the pod again

    🔧 UNDER THE HOOD — CAPSTONE: A CANARY RULE'S FULL JOURNEY, YAML TO PACKET
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ SCENARIO: you kubectl apply a VirtualService sending 10% of jobpost-api │
    │ traffic to the v2 subset. Here is EVERY section in this chapter, doing  │
    │ its one job, exactly once, on that single change:                       │
    │                                                                         │
    │ ① kubectl apply -f canary-vs.yaml -- API server persists it to etcd,    │
    │    before any Istio component has even noticed                          │
    │                                                                         │
    │ ② (3.2) istiod's Pilot sub-component's informer sees the new            │
    │    VirtualService -- Galley's webhook already rejected it here if the   │
    │    YAML were malformed, so Pilot only ever sees valid config            │
    │                                                                         │
    │ ③ (3.2-3.3) Pilot converts the CRD into an updated Envoy route table:   │
    │    one cluster becomes two, weighted 90/10                              │
    │                                                                         │
    │ ④ (3.3) istiod streams that new RDS config over the persistent xDS      │
    │    gRPC stream to every Envoy that routes to jobpost-api (~1-3s)        │
    │                                                                         │
    │ ⑤ (3.4-3.5, 3.10) each receiving Envoy exists only because, back at     │
    │    Pod creation, the mutating webhook added istio-proxy AND iptables    │
    │    (or the istio-cni DaemonSet) already redirected ports 15001/15006    │
    │    -- the canary push has nowhere to land without that one-time setup   │
    │                                                                         │
    │ ⑥ (3.11) none of ②-⑤ would have mattered if pilot-agent had never       │
    │    finished its own certificate handshake with istiod -- a sidecar      │
    │    still starting up cannot receive OR apply any xDS push, canary       │
    │    included                                                             │
    │                                                                         │
    │ ⑦ (3.9) the next real request to hit an updated sidecar walks the       │
    │    filter chain -- network filters check identity first, THEN the       │
    │    HTTP router filter (always last) now rolls the dice 90/10 between    │
    │    v1 and v2                                                            │
    │                                                                         │
    │ ⑧ (3.7-3.8) verify the whole chain in exactly two commands:             │
    │    istioctl proxy-status                    -- SYNCED, not STALE?       │
    │    istioctl proxy-config route deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj             │
    │                                              -- route shows the 90/10?  │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    Every one of this chapter's eleven sections is exactly one hop on this
    same road — a YAML edit goes in, enforced bytes come out — and 3.7/3.8's
    commands are simply how you inspect any single hop without guessing
    which one is lying to you.

    ⚡ SPEED TIPS
      ⚡ Triage in one glance: STALE/NOT SENT in istioctl proxy-status means
        an istiod (control-plane) problem; SYNCED-but-still-wrong means an
        Envoy (data-plane) problem — that split decides which half of the
        toolbox you open next
      ⚡ Debug the xDS hierarchy bottom-up — EDS → CDS → RDS → LDS (3.8) —
        never top-down; an empty endpoint list makes every table above it
        irrelevant
      ⚡ Run istioctl analyze -n anihpj BEFORE any proxy-config command — a
        static lint catches a typo'd host or missing subset in under a
        second, before you burn ten minutes reading live Envoy tables
      ⚡ "TCP behaves like Istio isn't even there" (no retries, no fault
        injection) is almost always a Service port not named http-*/grpc-*
        (3.9) — check the port name before touching any YAML
      ⚡ istioctl authn tls-check is a trap answer on the exam — it was
        removed years ago; the correct commands are istioctl x describe pod
        and istioctl proxy-config secret
      ⚡ On a "no sidecar" ticket, check the webhook object before the
        namespace label: kubectl get mutatingwebhookconfiguration
        istio-sidecar-injector — a broken CA bundle silently no-ops
        injection even when the label is correct

    └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    🧪 PRACTICE DRILL (8 minutes) — Prove the two planes on live anihpj
      1. (2 min) kubectl get pods -n anihpj -o wide
         → every jobpost-api/user-service/skills-service/etc pod should
           show 2/2 READY (data plane: sidecar present)
      2. (2 min) istioctl proxy-status
         → every proxy should show SYNCED, never STALE/NOT SENT
           (control plane: config actually delivered)
      3. (2 min) istioctl proxy-config listener deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj
         → confirm both capture listeners, 15001 and 15006, exist
      4. (1 min) kubectl exec deploy/jobpost-api -c istio-proxy -n anihpj -- id
         → confirm uid=1337(istio-proxy), the UID iptables exempts (3.5)
      5. (1 min) istioctl analyze -n anihpj
         → confirm "No validation issues found"
      If all five pass, you have independently verified injection, xDS
      sync, the iptables exemption, and config validity — the same four
      checks 3.7's golden order walks through on a real incident.
