    │ 🔷 SIDECAR ALREADY LANDED (3.4-3.5, 3.10): mutating webhook added  │
    │    istio-proxy; iptables (or istio-cni) redirect 15001/15006       │
    │         │                                                          │
    │         ▼                                                          │
    │ 📦 CLUSTER INVENTORY + LIVE READS (3.6-3.8): every pod istiod      │
    │    runs, and what istioctl proxy-status/proxy-config inspect       │
    │         │                                                          │
    │         ▼                                                          │
    │ 🔒 FILTER CHAIN ENFORCES IT (3.9): mTLS + rbac, then HTTP          │
    │    filters, router always last -- routed AND secured               │
    │         │                                                          │
    │         ▼                                                          │
    │ ⚙️ pilot-agent (3.11) kept certs + Envoy's bootstrap fresh the     │
    │    whole time, underneath every hop above                          │
    │         │                                                          │
    │         ▼                                                          │
    │ ✅ jobpost-api request returns -- encrypted, routed, measured       │
    │         │                                                          │
    │         └──▶ still wrong? loop back to 3.7's golden debug order    │
    └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    In prose: a YAML change wakes up the control plane (3.1-3.3), which
    pushes new tables over xDS to sidecars that only exist because
    injection and iptables wired them in ahead of time (3.4-3.5, 3.10);
    the next packet then walks that sidecar's filter chain and comes out
    the other side encrypted, authorized, and measured (3.9), kept alive
    the whole time by pilot-agent underneath (3.11), on top of the exact
    component inventory 3.6 named — and whenever any of that breaks,
    3.7-3.8 hand you the ordered checklist to find out which hop failed.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
PART 4: INSTALLING ISTIO — GETTING STARTED                               🟢
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

  Chapter 4 (only)  ·  Difficulty: 🟢 concepts → 🟡 hands-on install  ·  🎯 exam-critical
  What you'll build: a live Istio control plane with automatic sidecar
  injection running across all 7 anihpj services — installed, verified,
  and rebuilt at least twice more (istioctl vs Helm, sidecar vs ambient).
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

  [PART 4 INTRO]
  Parts 1-3 built a mental model entirely on paper: why a mesh exists, what
  Istio is, and how istiod and Envoy talk to each other under the hood. Not
  one anihpj Pod has an actual sidecar yet — every diagram so far has been a
  promise. Part 4 cashes that promise in: by the last section you will have
  run istioctl (or Helm) against a real cluster and watched jobpost-api and
  its six sibling services flip from 1/1 to 2/2, proven with istioctl
  proxy-status and istioctl analyze instead of taken on faith.

  This is also where the exam stops being theoretical. The ICA performance
  exam hands you a bare cluster and a clock — it does not care whether you
  can define "data plane" if you cannot also type the commands that put one
  there. Chapter 4 drills the decisions in the order you'll actually make
  them on test day: which profile, which install tool (istioctl or Helm),
  which data-plane mode (sidecar or ambient), and what to check first when
  a Pod refuses to come up at all.

  🧠 ANALOGY. Installing Istio is like retrofitting a finished apartment
  building with a shared intercom-and-camera system after every tenant has
  already moved in. You don't gut and rebuild each apartment — anihpj's
  Django code never changes — one crew (istioctl or Helm) runs a single job
  and wires a small junction box (the Envoy sidecar) into each unit as it's
  occupied (Pod creation), while one breaker panel in the basement (istiod)
  lights every wire from the same signal. Wire only some units and the
  building looks identical from the street — it just has no intercom.

  🐍 OUR RUNNING EXAMPLE — anihpj. Every command in this chapter targets the
  SAME seven anihpj Deployments used throughout the guide — jobpost-api,
  user-service, skills-service, location-service, notification-service,
  auth-service, search-service — in one namespace. You install once, verify
  once, then repeat the install two more ways (Helm in 4.10, ambient mode
  in 4.11) against those SAME services, so no path is a surprise on exam day.

  [HOW THE CHAPTER FLOWS — Part 4 map]

  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ 4.1-4.3          4.4-4.6           4.7-4.9              4.10-4.11       │
  │ PREPARE  ──▶  INSTALL & VERIFY ──▶ UNDERSTAND & FIX ──▶ ALTERNATE PATHS │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Read it as a sentence: first PREPARE (size the cluster, pick a profile),
  then INSTALL & VERIFY (the one true path, start to finish), then
  UNDERSTAND & FIX (what each profile really installs, and what breaks),
  and finally walk the SAME install down two ALTERNATE PATHS so a Helm or
  ambient-mode question never catches you unprepared.

  🧭 DECISION GUIDE — which install path fits you?

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ If you...                                            │ Then...                                            │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ install for the first time, on a demo/laptop cluster │ istioctl install --set profile=demo -y  (4.2-4.4)  │
  │ need GitOps-friendly, versioned, repeatable installs │ skip to 4.10 — install the Helm chart path instead │
  │ must cut sidecar CPU/RAM overhead on large fleets    │ read the ambient row in 4.3, then do 4.11          │
  │ deploy into a Pod-Security-Admission restricted ns   │ read the CNI note in 4.3 BEFORE installing         │
  │ are drilling for the ICA performance exam            │ run 4.4 once unaided, then work every case in 4.9  │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  WITHOUT vs WITH PART 4 — why this chapter is not optional

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ WITHOUT Part 4 (mesh still on paper)         │ WITH Part 4 done (mesh actually running)       │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ anihpj pods show 1/1 — zero Envoy sidecars   │ every anihpj pod shows 2/2 — app + istio-proxy │
  │ istioctl proxy-status has nothing to report  │ proxy-status shows all 7 services SYNCED       │
  │ Kiali/Grafana/Jaeger are just names you read │ istioctl dashboard kiali graphs real traffic   │
  │ ambient vs sidecar is a slide, not a choice  │ you installed BOTH paths and compared them     │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  CAPTION: none of Parts 5 through 9 work without this chapter. Traffic
  splitting, mTLS, retries, and Kiali graphs are all configuration objects
  that a running Envoy sidecar (or ztunnel) must read and enforce — with no
  sidecar injected, a VirtualService or PeerAuthentication applied later is
  just YAML sitting in etcd, doing nothing to real anihpj traffic.

  [PART 4 SUMMARY + IMPLEMENTATION — read before the chapter]
  By the end of Part 4 you can install Istio with either tool, on either
  data-plane mode, and prove success three independent ways: kubectl showing
  2/2 containers, istioctl proxy-status showing SYNCED, and istioctl analyze
  returning clean. Implementation thread — the exact sequence 4.4 walks by
  hand, and the one 4.10/4.11 repeat with a single step swapped:

      choose a profile (demo / default / ambient)
                          │
                          ▼
      istioctl install --set profile=<profile> -y      (or: helm install, 4.10)
                          │
                          ▼
      kubectl label namespace anihpj istio-injection=enabled
        (or istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient  →  4.11)
                          │
                          ▼
      kubectl apply -f anihpj/k8s/
        (jobpost-api · user-service · skills-service · location-service ·
         notification-service · auth-service · search-service)
                          │
                          ▼
      kubectl get pods -n anihpj  →  2/2 Running (app + istio-proxy)
                          │
                          ▼
      istioctl proxy-status → SYNCED       istioctl analyze → clean
                          │
                          ▼
      ✅ anihpj is IN the mesh — ready for Part 5 (traffic management)

  CAPTION: only two things ever change between the three install paths in
  this chapter — the install command itself, and which label you put on the
  anihpj namespace. Everything below that label (the Deployments you apply,
  the two verification commands) is identical, which is exactly why the
  exam can test any of the three and expect the same muscle memory.

Chapter 4: Installing and Configuring Istio
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Chapter 4 only · Difficulty: 🟢->🟡 · 🎯 Installation, Upgrade & Config — 20% of the ICA exam
  "You understand istiod and Envoy on paper — but does a real cluster with anihpj's
   7 services actually come up clean, or does it half-install and leave you
   debugging a webhook timeout at 2am?"

    WHY THIS MATTERS
    Chapter 3 opened the hood on istiod and Envoy and showed you the theory: the
    control plane pushes xDS, iptables redirects traffic, and a sidecar rides
    shotgun with every app container. Chapter 4 is where that theory has to
    survive contact with a real cluster. Every one of anihpj's seven services —
    jobpost-api, user-service, skills-service, location-service,
    notification-service, auth-service, search-service — has to be labeled,
    injected, verified, and PROVEN to route traffic through Envoy before any of
    Chapter 3's architecture matters in practice. Pick the wrong profile and you
    either strand a lab cluster without Kiali or blow a production node group's
    CPU budget on egress gateways and Jaeger nobody asked for. Skip the
    port-naming convention on a single Service and that one service silently
    falls back to raw TCP with no retries, no canary weights, and no per-route
    metrics — a bug that looks like "Istio isn't working" but is really "Istio
    never got the chance to work." This chapter turns istioctl, Helm,
    IstioOperator, ambient mode, the CNI plugin, and Pod Security Admission into
    one coherent decision: how do you stand up a mesh for anihpj that is both
    correct today and defensible under a security or platform review tomorrow.
    Get comfortable here — two other exam domains, Traffic Management and
    Troubleshooting, both assume the install already went right.

    LEARNING OBJECTIVES
    By the end of this chapter you will be able to:
      ✅ Install Istio on a cluster with istioctl using the correct profile for
         the scenario (demo, default, minimal, ambient)
      ✅ Enable and verify sidecar injection for the anihpj namespace, confirming
         2/2 READY across all 7 services
      ✅ Run istioctl proxy-status, istioctl analyze, and a live curl test to
         PROVE the mesh is routing traffic — not just that pods are Running
      ✅ Install the identical control plane using Helm's three-chart pipeline
         (base -> istiod -> gateway) and explain when Helm beats istioctl
      ✅ Stand up ambient mode for anihpj, label the namespace correctly, and
         read the 1/1-vs-2/2 signal to tell which data plane is active
      ✅ Decide when the Istio CNI plugin and Pod Security Admission's
         restricted level are required, and in what order to roll them out
      ✅ Diagnose the 5 most common install failures (Pending pods, webhook
         timeout, 1/1 instead of 2/2, analyze warnings, STALE proxy-status)
         from the symptom alone

    EXAM/ICA RELEVANCE
    This chapter IS the Linux Foundation's "Installation, Upgrade & Config"
    domain — 20% of the ICA exam, graded hands-on in a live cluster. Every named
    sub-skill in that domain maps directly onto a section below:

    well enough to FIX it when it breaks (4.7-4.9), before branching into

    PLATFORM & SECURITY overlays for restricted or managed clusters (4.13-4.14).

    4.1  Prerequisites and Cluster Requirements
         - Kubernetes version: 1.28+ recommended (1.22+ minimum)
         - kubectl configured and pointing to your cluster
         - Cluster sizing for Istio overhead:
           • istiod: ~500m CPU, 2Gi memory (1 replica)
           • Each Envoy sidecar: ~100m CPU, 128Mi memory
           • For anihpj with 7 services: add ~700m CPU, ~1Gi RAM overhead
           • For a total anihpj cluster: ~4 CPUs, 8GB RAM minimum
         - Supported platforms: minikube, k3s, kind, Docker Desktop K8s,
           EKS, GKE, AKS, OpenShift, on-prem clusters
         - Quick cluster readiness check:
           kubectl cluster-info
           kubectl get nodes  → all nodes should be Ready
           kubectl top nodes  → check available resources
         [RESOURCE CALCULATOR: table showing overhead per service count]

         [RESOURCE CALCULATOR — mesh overhead by service count]
         ┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────────┬────────────────┐
         │ Services │ Sidecar  │ Sidecar  │ istiod       │ TOTAL mesh     │
         │ (pods)   │ CPU      │ RAM      │ (replicas)   │ overhead       │
         ├──────────┼──────────┼──────────┼──────────────┼────────────────┤
         │    5     │   500m   │  640Mi   │ 500m/2Gi (1) │ ~1.0 CPU/2.6Gi │
         │ 7 anihpj │   700m   │  896Mi   │ 500m/2Gi (1) │ ~1.2 CPU/2.9Gi │
         │   10     │  1000m   │ 1.25Gi   │ 500m/2Gi (1) │ ~1.5 CPU/3.3Gi │
         │   25     │  2500m   │  3.2Gi   │ 1 CPU/4Gi (2)│ ~3.5 CPU/7.2Gi │
         │   50     │  5000m   │  6.4Gi   │ 1 CPU/4Gi (2)│ ~6 CPU/10.4Gi  │
         └──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────────┴────────────────┘
         - Math: each sidecar ≈ 100m CPU + 128Mi RAM; istiod baseline is
           500m CPU + 2Gi RAM → run 2 istiod replicas beyond ~20 services
         - Budget this overhead ON TOP of the application containers: for
           anihpj (7 services) a 4 CPU / 8GB cluster is comfortable

    4.2  Installing istioctl (The Istio CLI)
         - istioctl: Istio's command-line tool (like kubectl but for Istio)
         - Installation on all platforms (Linux/Mac/Windows)
         - Key istioctl commands overview:
           • istioctl install: install Istio on the cluster
           • istioctl analyze: validate Istio configuration
           • istioctl proxy-status: check proxy sync status
           • istioctl proxy-config: inspect Envoy config
           • istioctl dashboard: open Kiali, Grafana, Jaeger in browser
         [CODE BLOCK: istioctl installation commands for each OS]

         [INSTALLING istioctl]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  # Linux / macOS:                                      │
         │  curl -L https://istio.io/downloadIstio | sh -         │
         │  cd istio-1.22.0                                       │
         │  export PATH=$PWD/bin:$PATH                            │
         │                                                        │
         │  # Windows (PowerShell):                               │
         │  Invoke-WebRequest https://istio.io/downloadIstio      │
         │    -OutFile istio.zip                                   │
         │  Expand-Archive istio.zip                              │
         │  $env:PATH += ";.\istio-1.22.0\bin"                    │
         │                                                        │
         │  # Verify:                                             │
         │  istioctl version                                      │
         │  → client version: 1.22.0                             │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    4.3  Istio Installation Profiles
         - Istio has built-in installation profiles for different use cases:
           • default: production-grade (ingressgateway + istiod), minimal tools
           • demo: all features for learning (adds Kiali, Jaeger, Prometheus, Grafana)
             ⚠️ demo profile is for LEARNING only — NOT production!
           • minimal: control plane only (no gateway), for CI/CD pipeline tests
           • remote: for multi-cluster setups, connects to external control plane
           • empty: nothing pre-configured, for advanced custom installs
           • ambient: sidecar-free mode (ztunnel + waypoint proxy), lower overhead
           • preview: experimental features for testing upcoming releases
         - For this guide: use demo profile to get all observability tools
         - For production later: use default profile + add tools via Helm separately
         [PROFILE COMPARISON TABLE: what each profile includes]

         | Component             | default | demo | minimal | remote |
         | ──────────────────────│─────────│──────│─────────│────────│
         | istiod                | ✅      | ✅   | ✅      | ❌     |
         | istio-ingressgateway  | ✅      | ✅   | ❌      | ❌     │
         | istio-egressgateway   | ❌      | ✅   | ❌      | ❌     |
         | Kiali                 | ❌      | ✅   | ❌      | ❌     |
         | Jaeger                | ❌      | ✅   | ❌      | ❌     |
         | Prometheus            | ❌      | ✅   | ❌      | ❌     |
         | Grafana               | ❌      | ✅   | ❌      | ❌     |
         | Best for              | Prod   | Learn| CI/CD  | Multi  |

         [PROFILE SELECTION DECISION — which profile to use when]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │                                                                    │
         │  Are you learning / developing? ──── YES ──▶ demo profile         │
         │                                              (all tools included)  │
         │  ↓ NO                                                              │
         │  Is this production?  ──────────── YES ──▶ default profile        │
         │                                              (then add tools via   │
         │                                               Helm separately)     │
         │  ↓ NO                                                              │
         │  Is this a CI/CD pipeline test? ── YES ──▶ minimal profile        │
         │                                              (fastest install)     │
         │  ↓ NO                                                              │
         │  Is this a secondary cluster? ──── YES ──▶ remote profile         │
         │                                              (connects to primary)  │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [EXPECTED OUTPUT after: istioctl install --set profile=demo -y]

    4.4  Step-by-Step: Install Istio for anihpj
         [COMPLETE INSTALLATION WALKTHROUGH]
         Step 1: Verify cluster is ready
           kubectl cluster-info
           kubectl get nodes
         Step 2: Install Istio with demo profile
           istioctl install --set profile=demo -y
         Step 3: Verify installation
           kubectl get pods -n istio-system
           kubectl get svc -n istio-system
         Step 4: Enable sidecar injection for anihpj namespace
           kubectl create namespace anihpj
           kubectl label namespace anihpj istio-injection=enabled
           kubectl get namespace anihpj --show-labels
         Step 5: Deploy anihpj services
           kubectl apply -f anihpj/k8s/
         Step 6: Verify sidecars were injected
           kubectl get pods -n anihpj
           → Each pod should show 2/2 containers (app + istio-proxy)
         Step 7: Open observability dashboards
           istioctl dashboard kiali
           istioctl dashboard grafana
           istioctl dashboard jaeger
         [CODE BLOCKS with expected output at each step]

         [STEP 1 — VERIFY CLUSTER IS READY: command + expected output]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  $ kubectl cluster-info                                        │
         │  Kubernetes control plane is running at https://<api>:6443     │
         │                                                                │
         │  $ kubectl get nodes                                           │
         │  NAME     STATUS   ROLES           AGE   VERSION               │
         │  node-1   Ready    control-plane   12d   v1.30.2               │
         │  node-2   Ready    <none>          12d   v1.30.2               │
         │                                                                │
         │  ✅ All nodes Ready → safe to install Istio                     │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [STEP 2 — INSTALL ISTIO WITH DEMO PROFILE: command + output]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  $ istioctl install --set profile=demo -y                      │
         │  ✔ Istio core installed                                        │
         │  ✔ Istiod installed                                            │
         │  ✔ Egress gateways installed                                   │
         │  ✔ Ingress gateways installed                                  │
         │  ✔ Installation complete                                       │
         │  Made this installation the default for injection and          │
         │  validation.                                                   │
         │                                                                │
         │  ✅ Five ✔ marks = control plane up (takes ~1-2 minutes)        │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [STEP 3 — VERIFY INSTALLATION: pods + services in istio-system]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

    4.5  Verifying Istio is Working
         - Check proxy sync status:
           istioctl proxy-status
           → All pods should show "SYNCED" next to istiod
         - Check a specific proxy's config:
           istioctl proxy-config cluster deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj
         - Analyze your configuration for problems:
           istioctl analyze -n anihpj
         - Generate a traffic test and watch Kiali:
           kubectl exec -it deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj -- curl user-service/users/
         [EXPECTED OUTPUT SCREENSHOTS with annotations]

         [EXPECTED OUTPUT — istioctl proxy-status: every column SYNCED]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  $ istioctl proxy-status                                           │
         │  NAME                             CDS     LDS     EDS     RDS      │
         │  jobpost-api-7d4f8b9c.anihpj      SYNCED  SYNCED  SYNCED  SYNCED   │
