         │                             ▼  HTTP (decrypted)                     │
         │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐       │
         │  │  🚦 VIRTUALSERVICE Resource: jobpost-api-vs              │       │
         │  │                                                         │       │
         │  │  "Now I route this request:"                            │       │
         │  │                                                         │       │
         │  │  Match: uri prefix /jobs/  → YES ✅                     │       │
         │  │                                                         │       │
         │  │  Route options:                                         │       │
         │  │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐       │       │
         │  │  │  subset: v1  →  weight: 90  →  90% traffic  │       │       │
         │  │  │  subset: v2  →  weight: 10  →  10% traffic  │       │       │
         │  │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘       │       │
         │  │                                                         │       │
         │  │  Policies applied HERE:                                 │       │
         │  │  • timeout: 10s                                         │       │
         │  │  • retries: attempts: 3, perTryTimeout: 2s             │       │
         │  │  • fault: (none)                                        │       │
         │  │                                                         │       │
         │  │  → Chose subset v1 (90% weight)                         │       │
         │  │  → Forwards to DestinationRule for policy lookup        │       │
         │  └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘       │
         │                             │                                       │
         │                             ▼  "send to jobpost-api, subset v1"     │
         │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐       │
         │  │  📋 DESTINATIONRULE Resource: jobpost-api-dr             │       │
         │  │                                                         │       │
         │  │  "subset v1 = pods with labels: version=v1"             │       │
         │  │  "Now I apply destination policies:"                    │       │
         │  │                                                         │       │
         │  │  Policies applied HERE:                                 │       │
         │  │  • loadBalancer: LEAST_CONN                             │       │
         │  │    → picks pod with fewest active connections           │       │
         │  │  • circuitBreaker: consecutiveErrors: 5                 │       │
         │  │    → checks: has this pod failed 5 times?              │       │
         │  │  • tls: mode: ISTIO_MUTUAL                              │       │
         │  │    → opens mTLS tunnel to destination pod               │       │
         │  │  • connectionPool: maxConnections: 100                  │       │
         │  │                                                         │       │
         │  │  → Selected: Pod jobpost-api-v1-abc (LEAST_CONN)        │       │
         │  │  → Circuit breaker: CLOSED (healthy) ✅                  │       │
         │  │  → mTLS tunnel established 🔒                            │       │
         │  └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘       │
         │                             │                                       │
         │                             ▼  mTLS encrypted                       │
         │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐       │
         │  │  📦 KUBERNETES SERVICE: jobpost-api                      │       │
         │  │                                                         │       │
         │  │  "My selector: app=jobpost-api"                         │       │
         │  │  "My endpoints: 10.244.1.5:8000, 10.244.2.3:8000, ..." │       │
         │  │  (Istio overrides K8s default round-robin)              │       │
         │  └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘       │
         │                             │                                       │
         │                             ▼  mTLS → Envoy inbound                 │
         │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐       │
         │  │  🫛 POD: jobpost-api-v1-abc                              │       │
         │  │                                                         │       │
         │  │  ┌──────────────────────┐  ┌────────────────────────┐  │       │
         │  │  │ 🔷 Envoy (inbound)   │  │ 🐍 Django Container    │  │       │
         │  │  │ port 15006           │  │ port 8000              │  │       │
         │  │  │                      │  │                        │  │       │
         │  │  │ 1. Terminate mTLS 🔓 │  │ 6. Process GET /jobs/  │  │       │
         │  │  │ 2. Verify SPIFFE cert│──▶│ 7. Query PostgreSQL   │  │       │
         │  │  │ 3. AuthzPolicy check │  │ 8. Return JSON         │  │       │
         │  │  │ 4. Record metrics    │◀──│                        │  │       │
         │  │  │ 5. Forward to :8000  │  │                        │  │       │
         │  │  └──────────────────────┘  └────────────────────────┘  │       │
         │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘       │
         │                                                                     │
         │  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════    │
         │  RESOURCE RESPONSIBILITY SUMMARY:                                   │
         │  ┌──────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
         │  │  Gateway     │  WHO can enter? (host, port, TLS)            │   │
         │  │  VirtualSvc  │  WHERE to route? (path, weight, headers)     │   │
         │  │  DestRule    │  HOW to send? (LB, mTLS, circuit breaker)    │   │
         │  │  K8s Service │  WHAT pods exist? (endpoint discovery)        │   │
         │  │  PeerAuth    │  ENCRYPT? (mTLS mode per namespace)          │   │
         │  │  AuthzPolicy │  ALLOWED? (who can call this service)        │   │
         │  └──────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
         └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Chapter 5: Gateway — The Front Door to Your Mesh
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Chapter 5 of 5-8  ·  Difficulty: 🟡 Intermediate  ·  🎯 Traffic
    Management — 35% of the ICA exam (the single biggest domain)
    "Before anything is routed, retried, or load-balanced for anihpj —
     who may enter the mesh at all?"

    WHY THIS MATTERS
         Every other resource in Part 5 assumes a request already made it
         inside the mesh — but for anihpj's public users, nothing is
         inside yet. Chapter 5 is where that changes: the Gateway is the
         FIRST of the four Traffic Management CRDs, the only one that
         ever touches raw internet traffic before istiod, VirtualService,
         or DestinationRule get a say. Skip it, or misconfigure its
         selector, and every later chapter in this Part becomes
         theoretical — jobpost-api can be canary-split, retried, and
         circuit-broken to perfection, and a real customer's browser
         still gets a plain connection timeout, because the mesh's front
         door was never opened. Get the Gateway right once, on ports 80
         and 443 for api.anihpj.com, and every remaining chapter in Part
         5 finally has real traffic to work with.

    LEARNING OBJECTIVES — by the end of Chapter 5 you can:
         ✅ Explain what a Gateway is and how it differs from a plain
            Kubernetes Ingress (5.1)
         ✅ Write a complete, annotated Gateway YAML that accepts HTTP on
            :80 and HTTPS on :443 for api.anihpj.com (5.2)
         ✅ Verify a Gateway actually reached the edge Envoy with
            istioctl proxy-config listener, not just kubectl get (5.2)
         ✅ Wire a Gateway to a VirtualService via the gateways: field and
            explain why one without the other drops or over-scopes
            traffic (5.3)
         ✅ Choose and build the right production pattern — HTTP-only,
            HTTPS SIMPLE, or HTTP->HTTPS redirect — for a given anihpj
            requirement (5.4)
         ✅ Pick the correct tls.mode (SIMPLE / MUTUAL / PASSTHROUGH /
            ISTIO_MUTUAL / OPTIONAL_MUTUAL) for a scenario and name its
            required secret keys (5.5, 5.7)
         ✅ Scope a shared Gateway safely across namespaces using hosts[]
            prefixes and fully-qualified gateways[] references (5.8)

    ICA EXAM RELEVANCE
         🎯 Gateway configuration sits squarely inside Traffic Management,
         the 35%-weighted domain that decides more exam points than any
         other single topic. The graded skills are narrow and mechanical
         — which is good news under a clock:

         ┌───────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┐
         │ Graded skill                  │ Where Chapter 5 teaches it │
         ├───────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
         │ TLS termination at the edge   │ 5.2, 5.5, 5.7              │
         │ Host / hostname matching      │ 5.2, 5.8                   │
         │ Port + protocol config        │ 5.2, 5.4, 5.9              │
         │ Gateway<->VirtualService bind │ 5.3, 5.8                   │
         │ Namespace-scoped edge sharing │ 5.8, 5.9                   │
         └───────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┘

         Note the split from 5.6's exam callout: writing the Gateway YAML
         is graded here under Traffic Management, while the TLS SECURITY
         judgment calls it also enables (mTLS, cert rotation) are graded
         under the separate Securing Workloads domain (25%) — one
         resource, two exam domains, both worth points.

    SECTION MAP

         ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ CHAPTER 5 SECTION MAP — 9 sections in 4 logical groups          │
         │                                                                 │

         Read top to bottom: Chapter 5 first DEFINES what a Gateway is
         (5.1), then shows you how to WRITE and WIRE one into production
         with real patterns (5.2-5.4), then goes deep on picking the
         right TLS MODE and API style (5.5-5.7), and finally covers the
         ADVANCED SCOPING knobs that keep a shared Gateway safe once more
         than one anihpj team depends on it (5.8-5.9).

    5.1  What is an Istio Gateway?
         - A Gateway is the entry point for traffic FROM OUTSIDE the mesh
         - It replaces (or works alongside) a Kubernetes Ingress
         - Deployed as its own Pod: istio-ingressgateway (Envoy-based)
         - More powerful than Ingress: supports header manipulation, mTLS,
           custom ports, weight-based routing, etc.
         - Two types:
           • IngressGateway: external traffic INTO the mesh
           • EgressGateway: controlled traffic OUT of the mesh (to external APIs)
         [GATEWAY POSITION DIAGRAM: internet → Gateway → VirtualService → Pods]

         [GATEWAY POSITION — INTERNET → LB → EDGE ENVOY POD → MESH]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  ISTIO GATEWAY PATH (anihpj)          PLAIN K8S INGRESS PATH       │
         │  ───────────────────────────          ──────────────────────       │
         │  🌐 Internet                          🌐 Internet                  │
         │      │ GET https://api.anihpj.com         │ any Host header        │
         │      ▼                                    ▼                        │
         │  Cloud LoadBalancer (TCP :443)        Cloud LoadBalancer           │
         │      │                                    │                        │
         │      ▼                                    ▼                        │
         │  🔷 istio-ingressgateway POD          📦 ingress-controller POD    │
         │     (standalone Envoy proxy)          (nginx / traefik / ...)      │
         │     programmed by Gateway CRD         programmed by Ingress        │
         │      │ decrypt TLS, match host            │ host/path rules        │
         │      ▼                                    ▼                        │
         │  ═══ ENTERS THE MESH 🔒 ═══           K8s Service (kube-proxy)     │
         │      │ VirtualService routing,            │                        │
         │      │ retries, mTLS, metrics             ▼                        │
         │      ▼                                Pod (no sidecar powers)      │
         │  jobpost-api Pod 🔷 (sidecar)                                      │
         │                                                                    │
         │  → SAME position in the network path — but the Istio edge pod      │
         │    is a FULL Envoy: every mesh feature applies from hop one        │
         │  → a K8s Ingress pod is only an HTTP router — mesh policy stops    │
         │    at its door — no mTLS, no weights, no fault injection           │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [GATEWAY vs KUBERNETES INGRESS COMPARISON]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  KUBERNETES INGRESS          ISTIO GATEWAY             │
         │  ──────────────────          ─────────────────         │
         │  ✅ Simple host/path routing  ✅ Same + more            │
         │  ❌ No header manipulation    ✅ Full header control     │
         │  ❌ No mTLS termination       ✅ mTLS at the edge        │
         │  ❌ No weighted routing       ✅ % traffic split        │
         │  ❌ Limited TLS options       ✅ Advanced TLS/SNI        │
         │  ❌ No egress control         ✅ Egress gateway          │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - DEFINITION: the Gateway CRD is pure CONFIGURATION — the thing that
           actually moves packets is the istio-ingressgateway POD (an Envoy)
           → the CRD's selector labels bind the config to that pod
           → wrong labels = kubectl accepts the YAML but NO Envoy ever
             receives it (a silent failure — the classic gateway gotcha)
         - The Gateway resource itself may live in ANY namespace; putting it
           in istio-system is merely a common convention, not a requirement

    5.2  Gateway YAML — Accepting Traffic for anihpj
         - How to write a Gateway resource for anihpj.example.com
         - port 80 (HTTP) and port 443 (HTTPS with TLS certificate)
         - selector: istio: ingressgateway (which Envoy handles this)
         - hosts: ["anihpj.example.com"] (which hostnames to accept)
         [ANNOTATED Gateway YAML with every field explained]

         [COMPLETE ANNOTATED Gateway YAML for anihpj]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1                                │
         │  kind: Gateway                                                     │
         │  metadata:                                                         │
         │    name: anihpj-gateway          # ← name this gateway            │
         │    namespace: anihpj                                               │
         │  spec:                                                             │
         │    selector:                                                       │
         │      istio: ingressgateway       # ← which Envoy pod handles this │
         │    servers:                                                        │
         │    - port:                                                         │
         │        number: 80               # ← accept HTTP on port 80        │
         │        name: http                                                  │
         │        protocol: HTTP                                              │
         │      hosts:                                                        │
         │      - "anihpj.example.com"     # ← only accept this hostname     │
         │    - port:                                                         │
         │        number: 443              # ← accept HTTPS on port 443      │
         │        name: https                                                 │
         │        protocol: HTTPS                                             │
         │      tls:                                                          │
         │        mode: SIMPLE            # ← TLS termination at gateway     │
         │        credentialName: anihpj-tls-cert  # ← K8s secret with cert │
         │      hosts:                                                        │
         │      - "anihpj.example.com"                                        │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - Applying the YAML is only half the job — always verify the config
           actually reached the edge Envoy:
           • kubectl get gateway → proves the API server ACCEPTED it, nothing
             more (a Gateway with a wrong selector still shows up here)
           • istioctl proxy-config listener → proves the edge Envoy is
             actually LISTENING (the test that matters)

         [VERIFY THE GATEWAY LANDED IN THE EDGE ENVOY — two-step check]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  # step 1 — resource accepted? (necessary, NOT sufficient)         │
         │  kubectl get gateway anihpj-gateway -n anihpj                      │
         │  # NAME             AGE                                            │
         │  # anihpj-gateway   12s   ← exists in etcd, says nothing more      │
         │                                                                    │
         │  # step 2 — did the edge Envoy get it? (the real test)             │
         │  istioctl proxy-config listener deploy/istio-ingressgateway \      │
         │      -n istio-system                                               │
         │  # ADDRESS  PORT  MATCH  DESTINATION                               │
         │  # 0.0.0.0  8080  ALL    Route: http.80   ← :80 server pushed      │
         │  # 0.0.0.0  8443  SNI    Route: https.443 ← :443 + TLS pushed      │
         │  # (pod ports 8080/8443 sit behind service ports 80/443)           │
         │                                                                    │
         │  # step 2 empty? → selector matched no pod. Check the labels:      │
         │  kubectl get pods -n istio-system -l istio=ingressgateway          │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    5.3  How Gateway Connects to VirtualService
         - Gateway: "I accept traffic on port 80 for anihpj.example.com"
         - VirtualService: "Route it to jobpost-api service on port 8000"
         - They are linked by the gateways field in VirtualService
         - Two-step pattern: Gateway defines port/host, VS defines routing
         [FLOW DIAGRAM: request → Gateway → VirtualService → Service → Pod]

         [GATEWAY + VIRTUALSERVICE — the mandatory two-resource pattern]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │                                                                    │
         │   STEP 1: Gateway resource says "I accept this traffic"           │
         │   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐        │
         │   │  Gateway: anihpj-gateway                             │        │
         │   │  • listen on port 80/443                             │        │
         │   │  • for host: anihpj.example.com                      │        │
         │   │  • on: istio-ingressgateway pod                      │        │
         │   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘        │
         │                          │                                         │
         │                          │ ← traffic arrives here                 │
         │                          ▼                                         │
         │   STEP 2: VirtualService says "now route it like this"            │
         │   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐        │
         │   │  VirtualService: jobpost-vs                          │        │
         │   │  • gateways: [anihpj-gateway]   ← reference gateway │        │
         │   │  • hosts: [anihpj.example.com]                       │        │
         │   │  • match: uri /jobs/*                                │        │
         │   │  • route: to: jobpost-api:8000                       │        │
         │   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘        │
         │                          │                                         │
         │                          ▼                                         │
         │          Kubernetes Service: jobpost-api                           │
         │                          │                                         │
         │                          ▼                                         │
         │          Pod: jobpost-api (with Envoy sidecar)                     │
         │                                                                    │
         │  ⚠️  KEY RULE: Gateway WITHOUT VirtualService = traffic DROPPED    │
         │     VirtualService without Gateway = only mesh-internal routing    │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - REAL SCENARIO — anihpj launch morning: the team applied the
           Gateway, DNS cutover went live... and every request to
           api.anihpj.com returned 404. kubectl showed the Gateway healthy.
           → cause: the VirtualService was still sitting in a git branch —
             the Gateway was accepting traffic with ZERO routing rules
           → fix took 30 seconds: kubectl apply the VirtualService with
             gateways: [anihpj-gateway] — the 404s stopped instantly
           → lesson: a Gateway alone NEVER routes; treat Gateway + VS as
             one deployment unit and always apply them together

    5.4  Common Gateway Patterns — Production-Ready Configurations
         - DEFINITION: a gateway "pattern" is a ready-made spec.servers[]
           recipe — the three below cover ~95% of real clusters and are the
           exact configs the ICA exam asks you to write from scratch
         - Why it matters: gateways fail silently (wrong selector, missing
           secret, absent VirtualService) → starting from a known-good
           pattern removes whole classes of launch-day surprises for anihpj
         - How it works: every pattern is just a different combination of
           port.protocol and the tls: block inside ONE Gateway resource
           • Pattern 1 HTTP-only    → dev clusters, quick demos
           • Pattern 2 HTTPS SIMPLE → the production baseline
           • Pattern 3 HTTP→HTTPS   → production + automatic 301 upgrade
         - All YAML below uses apiVersion networking.istio.io/v1 — the GA
           API since Istio 1.22; prefer it for everything you write today

         [PATTERN 1 — HTTP-ONLY GATEWAY (dev / demos, NEVER production)]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1                                │
         │  kind: Gateway                                                     │
         │  metadata:                                                         │
         │    name: anihpj-gateway-dev                                        │
         │    namespace: anihpj            # ← any namespace works            │
         │  spec:                                                             │
         │    selector:                                                       │
         │      istio: ingressgateway      # ← default edge pod's label       │
         │    servers:                                                        │
         │    - port:                                                         │
         │        number: 80               # ← plaintext HTTP, no tls: block  │
         │        name: http                                                  │
         │        protocol: HTTP                                              │
         │      hosts:                                                        │
         │      - "dev.anihpj.example.com" # ← keep dev hostnames explicit    │
         │  # ⚠️ credentials, cookies, JWTs travel UNENCRYPTED — dev only     │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [PATTERN 2 — HTTPS WITH credentialName (production baseline)]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1                                │
         │  kind: Gateway                                                     │
         │  metadata:                                                         │
         │    name: anihpj-gateway-https                                      │
         │    namespace: anihpj                                               │
         │  spec:                                                             │
         │    selector:                                                       │
         │      istio: ingressgateway                                         │
         │    servers:                                                        │
         │    - port:                                                         │
         │        number: 443              # ← TLS port                       │
         │        name: https                                                 │
         │        protocol: HTTPS                                             │
         │      tls:                                                          │
         │        mode: SIMPLE             # ← terminate TLS at the edge      │
         │        credentialName: anihpj-tls-cert  # ← K8s TLS secret         │
         │      hosts:                                                        │
         │      - "api.anihpj.com"                                            │
         │  # the secret must sit in the EDGE POD's namespace (istio-system   │
         │  # in the default install), whatever namespace the Gateway is in:  │
         │  #   kubectl create secret tls anihpj-tls-cert \                   │
         │  #     --cert=server.crt --key=server.key -n istio-system          │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [PATTERN 3 — HTTP→HTTPS REDIRECT via httpsRedirect: true (301)]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1                                │
         │  kind: Gateway                                                     │
         │  metadata:                                                         │
         │    name: anihpj-gateway                                            │
         │    namespace: anihpj                                               │
         │  spec:                                                             │
         │    selector:                                                       │
         │      istio: ingressgateway                                         │
         │    servers:                                                        │
         │    - port:                                                         │
         │        number: 80                                                  │
         │        name: http                                                  │
         │        protocol: HTTP                                              │
         │      hosts:                                                        │
         │      - "api.anihpj.com"                                            │
         │      tls:                                                          │
         │        httpsRedirect: true      # ← every HTTP request → 301       │
         │    - port:                                                         │
         │        number: 443                                                 │
         │        name: https                                                 │
         │        protocol: HTTPS                                             │
         │      tls:                                                          │
         │        mode: SIMPLE                                                │
         │        credentialName: anihpj-tls-cert                             │
         │      hosts:                                                        │
         │      - "api.anihpj.com"                                            │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - What the client sees with Pattern 3 — the redirect never reaches
           any VirtualService; the gateway Envoy answers it directly:

         [REDIRECT ROUND-TRIP — WHAT ACTUALLY GOES OVER THE WIRE]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  T=0ms:  GET http://api.anihpj.com/jobs/  ──────▶ gateway :80      │
         │  T=1ms:  ◀────── 301 Moved Permanently                             │
         │          Location: https://api.anihpj.com/jobs/                    │
         │  T=2ms:  client re-issues the request over TLS ──▶ gateway :443    │
         │  T=5ms:  TLS handshake (SIMPLE) → VirtualService → jobpost-api     │
         │  ✅ one extra round trip on FIRST contact; browsers cache the 301  │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         🔧 UNDER THE HOOD — httpsRedirect: true skips routing entirely:
           Pilot compiles that HTTP server's tls.httpsRedirect into the
           listener's own route config with requireTls set, so the edge
           Envoy answers the 301 straight from local route state — no
           Cluster lookup, no RDS hand-off to a VirtualService, and no hit
           against jobpost-api's request metrics. The real work only
           happens on the second request, the one that lands on :443.

    5.5  Deep Dive — TLS Modes: SIMPLE vs MUTUAL vs PASSTHROUGH
         - DEFINITION: tls.mode on a Gateway server decides WHERE the TLS
           tunnel ends and WHO must prove their identity with a certificate
         - Why it matters: pick wrong and you either break every client
           (MUTUAL without client certs), lose end-to-end encryption
           guarantees, or double-terminate TLS — the ICA tests all modes
         - How it works: the gateway Envoy either TERMINATES the handshake
           itself (SIMPLE / MUTUAL — needs a cert secret) or forwards the
           still-encrypted bytes onward (PASSTHROUGH — no secret at all)

         📖 KEY TERM — TLS termination: the point in the connection path
           where an encrypted TLS tunnel is decrypted. tls.mode picks that
           point for a Gateway server — SIMPLE and MUTUAL terminate AT the
           gateway Envoy; PASSTHROUGH pushes termination all the way to the
           jobpost-api Pod, leaving the mesh hop encrypted the whole way.

         [TLS MODE MATRIX — WHO HOLDS CERTS, WHO GETS VERIFIED]
         ┌──────────────────┬──────────┬──────────────┬───────────────────────┐
         │ tls.mode         │ GW cert? │ client cert? │ secret data keys      │
         ├──────────────────┼──────────┼──────────────┼───────────────────────┤
         │ SIMPLE           │ yes      │ no           │ tls.crt + tls.key     │
         │ MUTUAL           │ yes      │ REQUIRED     │ tls.crt + tls.key     │
         │                  │          │              │   + ca.crt            │
         │ PASSTHROUGH      │ no       │ no           │ none (SNI routing)    │
         │ AUTO_PASSTHROUGH │ no       │ no           │ none (SNI → cluster)  │
         └──────────────────┴──────────┴──────────────┴───────────────────────┘

         - Use cases, one line each:
           • SIMPLE           → public HTTPS for api.anihpj.com (the default)
           • MUTUAL           → B2B partners must present a client cert 🔒
           • PASSTHROUGH      → jobpost-api pod holds its own certificate;
                                the gateway must never see plaintext
           • AUTO_PASSTHROUGH → multi-cluster east-west gateways; the SNI
                                alone encodes the destination — no
                                VirtualService needed to route it
         - Secret contents differ by mode — the #1 exam trap:
           • SIMPLE: tls.crt + tls.key (kubectl create secret tls ...)
           • MUTUAL: tls.crt + tls.key + ca.crt (the CA that signed the
             CLIENT certificates — forget ca.crt and NO client can connect)
           • PASSTHROUGH / AUTO_PASSTHROUGH: no credentialName, no secret

         [SNI ROUTING — HOW PASSTHROUGH ROUTES WITHOUT DECRYPTING]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  1. client opens TCP to gateway :443, sends TLS ClientHello        │
         │     → the SNI field ("api.anihpj.com") is UNENCRYPTED by design    │
         │  2. gateway Envoy peeks at the SNI — nothing else is readable      │
         │  3. SNI matched against Gateway servers[].hosts                    │
         │  4. VirtualService tls: rules match on sniHosts → pick the         │
         │     destination service                                            │
         │  5. the encrypted stream is piped to the jobpost-api pod byte-     │
         │     for-byte — the POD's own certificate finishes the handshake 🔒 │
         │                                                                    │
         │  # VirtualService snippet used with PASSTHROUGH:                   │
         │  tls:                                                              │
         │  - match:                                                          │
         │    - port: 443                                                     │
         │      sniHosts: ["api.anihpj.com"]     # ← route key = SNI          │
         │    route:                                                          │
         │    - destination:                                                  │
         │        host: jobpost-api                                           │
         │        port:                                                       │
         │          number: 8000                                              │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [HANDSHAKE WALKTHROUGH — THE THREE MODES SIDE BY SIDE]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  SIMPLE — one-way TLS (public HTTPS default)                       │
         │  client ──ClientHello─────────▶ gateway                            │
         │  client ◀──server cert───────── gateway  client verifies gateway   │
         │  client ──encrypted HTTP─────▶ gateway → DECRYPTS → routes plain   │
         │           (then re-encrypts pod-to-pod with mesh mTLS 🔒)          │
         │                                                                    │
         │  MUTUAL — two-way TLS at the edge (B2B / partner APIs)             │
         │  client ◀──server cert───────── gateway  client verifies gateway   │
         │  client ──client cert────────▶ gateway  gateway verifies client    │
         │           against ca.crt from the secret                           │
         │  😈 no cert / untrusted cert → handshake FAILS, no HTTP at all     │
         │                                                                    │
         │  PASSTHROUGH — no termination at the edge (end-to-end TLS)         │
         │  client ──TLS bytes──────────▶ gateway ──TLS bytes──▶ backend pod  │
         │  gateway reads only the SNI; the BACKEND pod presents the cert     │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    5.6  Deep Dive — Kubernetes Gateway API vs Istio APIs
         - DEFINITION: the Kubernetes Gateway API (gateway.networking.k8s.io)
           is the vendor-neutral SIG-Network standard for ingress + routing —
           one CRD set implemented by Istio, Envoy Gateway, nginx, GKE, ...
         - Why it matters: Istio treats it as the FUTURE default traffic API;
           new Istio docs lead with it, and the ICA may show either style
         - How it works: install the Gateway API CRDs, create a Gateway with
           gatewayClassName: istio, then attach HTTPRoute resources to it
           via parentRefs — Istio programs Envoy from those resources
           → big behavioral difference: an istio-class Gateway API Gateway
             AUTO-PROVISIONS its own Envoy Deployment + Service (you no
             longer pre-install a shared istio-ingressgateway pod)

         [CONCEPT MAP — ISTIO API ↔ KUBERNETES GATEWAY API]
         ┌──────────────────┬────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┐
         │ concept          │ Istio API              │ Kubernetes Gateway API   │
         ├──────────────────┼────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┤
         │ edge entry point │ Gateway                │ Gateway                  │
         │ API group        │ networking.istio.io/v1 │ gateway.networking.k8s.io│
         │ HTTP routing     │ VirtualService (http:) │ HTTPRoute                │
         │ TCP / TLS routes │ VS tcp: / tls: blocks  │ TCPRoute / TLSRoute      │
         │ gRPC routing     │ VirtualService (http:) │ GRPCRoute                │
         │ traffic split    │ route[].weight         │ backendRefs[].weight     │
         │ header rewrite   │ headers.request.add    │ RequestHeaderModifier    │
         │ route → gateway  │ gateways: [gw-name]    │ parentRefs: [gw-name]    │
         │ edge proxy pod   │ pre-installed, shared  │ auto-provisioned per GW  │
         └──────────────────┴────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┘

         [GATEWAY API IN ACTION — anihpj EDGE, 90/10 CANARY INCLUDED]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1                          │
         │  kind: Gateway                                                     │
         │  metadata:                                                         │
         │    name: anihpj-gw                                                 │
         │    namespace: anihpj                                               │
         │  spec:                                                             │
         │    gatewayClassName: istio      # ← Istio implements this Gateway  │
         │    listeners:                                                      │
         │    - name: http                                                    │
         │      hostname: "*.anihpj.com"   # ← wildcard listener              │
         │      port: 80                                                      │
         │      protocol: HTTP                                                │
         │      allowedRoutes:                                                │
         │        namespaces:                                                 │
         │          from: Same             # ← only routes from this ns       │
         │  ---                                                               │
         │  apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1                          │
         │  kind: HTTPRoute                                                   │
         │  metadata:                                                         │
         │    name: jobpost-route                                             │
         │    namespace: anihpj                                               │
         │  spec:                                                             │
         │    parentRefs:                                                     │
         │    - name: anihpj-gw            # ← binds route to the Gateway     │
         │    hostnames: ["api.anihpj.com"]                                   │
         │    rules:                                                          │
         │    - matches:                                                      │
         │      - path:                                                       │
         │          type: PathPrefix                                          │
         │          value: /jobs           # ← same idea as a VS uri prefix   │
         │      backendRefs:                                                  │
         │      - name: jobpost-api        # ← 90/10 canary, GW-API style     │
         │        port: 8000                                                  │
         │        weight: 90                                                  │
         │      - name: jobpost-api-v2                                        │
         │        port: 8000                                                  │
         │        weight: 10                                                  │
         │  # applying this creates Deployment/anihpj-gw-istio +              │
         │  # Service/anihpj-gw-istio automatically — check with:             │
         │  #   kubectl get deploy,svc -n anihpj | grep anihpj-gw             │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - Adoption guidance for anihpj (and for the exam):
           • Gateway API CRDs are NOT bundled with Istio or Kubernetes —
             kubectl apply the release manifest from the gateway-api repo
             BEFORE creating any Gateway of class istio
           • both API families coexist happily in one mesh — migrate the
             edge hostname-by-hostname, no big-bang rewrite required
           • DestinationRule-level policy (circuit breaking, LB algorithm,
             subsets) still comes from Istio APIs — keep them alongside
           • mesh-internal (east-west) routing with HTTPRoute exists too:
             set parentRefs to kind: Service (the GAMMA initiative)
           • rule of thumb: NEW clusters → start with Gateway API at the
             edge; existing anihpj configs → migrate opportunistically

         🎯 ICA EXAM NOTE: "Securing Edge Traffic with TLS" is graded under
         the Securing Workloads domain (25%), NOT Traffic Management — but
         it is TAUGHT here in 5.2 (credentialName + TLS block) and 5.5
         (SIMPLE/MUTUAL/PASSTHROUGH modes) because the Gateway resource is
         where edge TLS actually lives. If the exam asks you to secure
         edge traffic, come back to 5.2/5.5, not Chapter 12 (which covers
         MESH-INTERNAL mTLS between sidecars, a different problem).


    5.7  Completing the TLS Mode Set — ISTIO_MUTUAL and OPTIONAL_MUTUAL
         - DEFINITION: two more tls.mode values exist beyond 5.5's four —
           ISTIO_MUTUAL secures the gateway with certificates Istio's own
           CA issues and auto-rotates, and OPTIONAL_MUTUAL runs the same
           handshake as MUTUAL but still accepts clients that send no
           certificate at all
         - Why it matters: ISTIO_MUTUAL is the mode real multi-cluster and
           east-west gateways run in production — confusing it with MUTUAL
           is a documented exam trap because both modes REQUIRE a client
           cert, yet only MUTUAL needs a credentialName secret at all;
           OPTIONAL_MUTUAL lets anihpj roll out partner client-certs
           gradually instead of a hard cutover that breaks old callers
         - How it works: ISTIO_MUTUAL skips credentialName entirely — Envoy
           fetches its cert/key over the same SDS (Secret Discovery
           Service) channel every sidecar uses, signed by istiod's own CA,
           and expects the PEER to present a cert from that same CA back;
           OPTIONAL_MUTUAL still requests a client cert during the
           handshake but never rejects a connection that omits one

         [TLS MODE MATRIX — THE TWO MODES 5.5 LEFT OUT]
         ┌──────────────────┬──────────┬──────────────┬───────────────────────┐
         │ tls.mode         │ GW cert? │ client cert? │ secret data keys      │
         ├──────────────────┼──────────┼──────────────┼───────────────────────┤
         │ ISTIO_MUTUAL     │ auto     │ auto (mesh)  │ none (Istiod CA)      │
         │ OPTIONAL_MUTUAL  │ yes      │ optional     │ tls.crt + tls.key     │
         └──────────────────┴──────────┴──────────────┴───────────────────────┘

         - Use cases, one line each:
           • ISTIO_MUTUAL     → east-west / multi-cluster gateways trusting
                                the mesh's own CA — no manual certs to issue
           • OPTIONAL_MUTUAL  → a public API that wants client certs from
                                registered partners but must keep serving
                                anonymous callers during the migration
         - anihpj gotcha: ISTIO_MUTUAL on the PUBLIC ingress gateway means
           only callers holding an Istio-issued mesh certificate can
           connect — that excludes every browser and external client, so
           it belongs on internal/east-west gateways, never on the public
           edge api.anihpj.com sits behind

    5.8  Namespace-Scoped Hosts and Cross-Namespace Gateway Binding
         - DEFINITION: two independent namespace rules govern a shared
           Gateway — the hosts[] entry's optional "namespace/" prefix picks
           WHICH namespace's VirtualServices may claim a hostname, and a
           VirtualService's own gateways[] field decides WHICH Gateway (and
           in what namespace) it is even asking to bind to
         - Why it matters: production clusters rarely dedicate one
           istio-ingressgateway per team — anihpj's real cluster has
           several teams sharing the SAME edge Envoy; skip the hosts[]
           namespace prefix and ANY team's VirtualService can claim ANY
           hostname mesh-wide, and a copy-pasted gateways: [anihpj-gateway]
           silently points at the WRONG Gateway the moment a VirtualService
           moves to a different namespace
         - How it works: hosts[] accepts <namespace>/<dnsName> — the
           namespace half is a literal name, "." (this Gateway's own
           namespace only), or "*" (any namespace) — and when NO prefix is
           written at all, Istio silently defaults to "*/", i.e. any
           namespace may bind; gateways[] resolves a bare name against the
           VirtualService's OWN namespace, so cross-namespace references
           must be written <gateway namespace>/<gateway name>

         🧠 ANALOGY. A bare gateways: [anihpj-gateway] reference works like
           paging a coworker by first name over an office intercom — it
           reaches "anihpj-gateway" on YOUR OWN floor (namespace) without
           asking further. Move to a different floor and the same page
           reaches nobody; only "floor + name" — gateways:
           [anihpj/anihpj-gateway] — still gets through.

         [HOSTS[] NAMESPACE PREFIX — SYNTAX AND MEANING]
         ┌──────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ hosts[] syntax               │ which VirtualServices may bind      │
         ├──────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ ns1/*.example.com            │ only VS living IN namespace ns1     │
         │ ./api.anihpj.com             │ only VS in the GATEWAY's own ns     │
         │ */api.anihpj.com             │ VS in ANY namespace (explicit)      │
         │ api.anihpj.com (no prefix)   │ ANY namespace — same as */, default │
         └──────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────┘

         [GATEWAYS[] FIELD — WHY A BARE NAME IS NAMESPACE-RELATIVE]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  SCENARIO A — VS and Gateway share a namespace (works)             │
         │    Gateway            anihpj/anihpj-gateway                        │
         │    VirtualService     anihpj/jobpost-vs                            │
         │    gateways: [anihpj-gateway]                                      │
         │      → resolves to anihpj/anihpj-gateway  (correct)                │
         │                                                                    │
         │  SCENARIO B — VS lives in a DIFFERENT namespace (breaks silently)  │
         │    Gateway            anihpj/anihpj-gateway                        │
         │    VirtualService     jobpost-team/jobpost-vs                      │
         │    gateways: [anihpj-gateway]                                      │
         │      → looks for jobpost-team/anihpj-gateway — NOT FOUND           │
         │      → route never attaches, kubectl shows no error at all         │
         │                                                                    │
         │  FIX — always namespace-qualify cross-namespace references:        │
         │    gateways: [anihpj/anihpj-gateway]   # explicit, always correct  │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - anihpj rule of thumb: lock down hosts[] with an explicit
           namespace prefix on every shared production Gateway, and always
           write cross-namespace gateways[] references in full ns/name
           form — never rely on the silent "*/" default

    5.9  Advanced Server Fields — name, bind, and Selector Scope
         - DEFINITION: three lesser-known knobs round out the Gateway CRD —
           Server.name (a label for stats and logs), Server.bind (pins a
           listener to one IP or a Unix domain socket instead of every
           interface), and PILOT_SCOPE_GATEWAY_TO_NAMESPACE (an istiod
           environment variable that changes how far a Gateway's selector
           search reaches)
         - Why it matters: without Server.name, every server in a
           multi-port Gateway shows up in istioctl/Prometheus output as an
           anonymous port number — debugging which listener a stat belongs
           to becomes guesswork; Server.bind matters on dual-homed or
           host-network edge nodes; PILOT_SCOPE_GATEWAY_TO_NAMESPACE is the
           difference between "any namespace's Gateway can bind the shared
           istio-ingressgateway" (the cluster-wide default) and a locked-
           down mesh where only Gateways inside istio-system itself may
         - How it works: name must be unique across the Servers in one
           Gateway and is purely cosmetic — Envoy uses it to prefix stats
           and logs; bind takes an IP literal or unix:///path/to/uds and
           overrides the "listen on every interface" default; the PILOT
           flag lives on the istiod Deployment — false (the default)
           searches ALL namespaces for selector-matching pods, true
           restricts that search to the Gateway's own configuration
           namespace

         [ADVANCED SERVER FIELDS AT A GLANCE]
         ┌──────────────────┬────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┐
         │ field            │ default        │ why you'd set it               │
         ├──────────────────┼────────────────┼────────────────────────────────┤
         │ Server.name      │ unset          │ stats/log prefix (unique/GW)   │
         │ Server.bind      │ all interfaces │ pin listener to one IP or UDS  │
         │ PILOT_SCOPE_...  │ false (all ns) │ restrict selector to own ns    │
         └──────────────────┴────────────────┴────────────────────────────────┘

         [CHECKING & USING name / bind / THE PILOT SCOPE FLAG]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  # is PILOT_SCOPE_GATEWAY_TO_NAMESPACE already set on istiod?      │
         │  kubectl get deploy istiod -n istio-system -o yaml \               │
         │    | grep -A1 PILOT_SCOPE_GATEWAY_TO_NAMESPACE                     │
         │                                                                    │
         │  # Server.name + Server.bind inside a real Gateway server:         │
         │  servers:                                                          │
         │  - port:                                                           │
         │      number: 443                                                   │
         │      name: https-api        # ← appears in proxy-config listener   │
         │      protocol: HTTPS                                               │
         │    bind: 10.0.0.5            # ← pin to one NIC, dual-homed node   │
         │    hosts: ["api.anihpj.com"]                                       │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - anihpj rule of thumb: name every server the moment a Gateway has
           more than one port — it is the only thing that makes
           `istioctl proxy-config listener` and Envoy access logs readable
           once http, https, and a redirect server all share one Gateway

    UNDER THE HOOD — FROM YAML TO A LIVE LISTENER (the xDS pipeline) 🔧
         Every fact in 5.1-5.9 is really one pipeline seen from different
         angles. Here it is end to end, for one real request: an HTTPS
         GET to api.anihpj.com hitting the Pattern-2 Gateway from 5.4.

         ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ 1. kubectl apply -f anihpj-gateway-https.yaml                       │
         │    -> apiserver stores the object in etcd (5.2's "necessary, NOT    │
         │      sufficient" step — nothing is listening yet)                   │
         │                                                                     │
         │ 2. istiod's Pilot WATCHES Gateway objects cluster-wide (or just one │
         │    namespace if PILOT_SCOPE_GATEWAY_TO_NAMESPACE=true, 5.9)         │
         │    -> resolves spec.selector {istio: ingressgateway} against live   │
         │      Pods — the exact match 5.1 warned can fail silently on a       │
         │      typo'd label                                                   │
         │                                                                     │
         │ 3. Pilot compiles the matched Gateway into xDS resources:           │
         │    • LDS: a listener on 0.0.0.0:8443, named from Server.name if     │
         │      you set one (5.9) — otherwise an anonymous port number         │
         │    • SDS: fetches the TLS cert — from the credentialName secret for │
         │      SIMPLE/MUTUAL, or istiod's own CA for ISTIO_MUTUAL (5.7)       │
         │    • RDS: the HTTP route table 5.3's VirtualService will attach to, │
         │      keyed by its gateways: reference                               │
         │                                                                     │
         │ 4. Pilot pushes all three over a gRPC xDS STREAM to every Envoy pod │
         │    the selector matched — a hot reload, zero restart, zero dropped  │
         │    connections                                                      │
         │                                                                     │
         │ 5. `istioctl proxy-config listener` (5.2) reads this exact          │
         │    in-memory state — it is not guessing, it IS the live truth       │
         │                                                                     │
         │ 6. a real ClientHello for api.anihpj.com now arrives at :8443:      │
         │    Envoy inspects the SNI at L4 FIRST, before any TLS work, to pick │
         │    the right filter chain if multiple Gateways share the port ->    │
         │    THEN terminates TLS per the tls.mode matrix (5.5, 5.7) -> THEN   │
         │    the HTTP Connection Manager hands off to the RDS route table     │
         │    5.3 wired to jobpost-api                                         │
         └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    SPEED TIPS
         ⚡ Default to SIMPLE + credentialName for every public host —
            it is correct ~95% of the time; reach for MUTUAL/PASSTHROUGH
            only when the requirement explicitly says "client cert" or
            "the app owns TLS"
         ⚡ Write hosts[] with an explicit namespace prefix (ns/host or
            ./host) on day one — retrofitting it later means finding
            every VirtualService that silently relied on the "*/" default
         ⚡ Wildcard hosts ("*.anihpj.com") save a Gateway server block
            per subdomain, but one wildcard SNI can't serve multiple
            unrelated certs on the same port — one cert per wildcard
         ⚡ The #1 exam-day failure mode is a Gateway/VirtualService
            mismatch: grep both for the SAME host string and the SAME
            gateway name before moving on — a typo compiles fine, it
            just never routes
         ⚡ `istioctl proxy-config listener` beats `kubectl get gateway`
            whenever you're unsure the config landed — get only proves
            etcd saw it, not that Envoy did
         ⚡ Name every Server the moment a Gateway has more than one
            port (5.9) — future-you debugging Envoy stats will thank
            present-you

    COMMANDS CHEAT-CARD

         ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ # apply / inspect the Gateway                                       │
         │ kubectl apply -f anihpj-gateway.yaml -n anihpj                      │
         │ kubectl get gateway -n anihpj        # accepted != delivered (5.2)  │
         │ kubectl describe gateway anihpj-gateway -n anihpj                   │
         │                                                                     │
         │ # verify it actually reached the edge Envoy                         │
         │ istioctl proxy-config listener deploy/istio-ingressgateway \        │
         │     -n istio-system                  # the REAL test, not get (5.2) │
         │ kubectl get pods -n istio-system -l istio=ingressgateway  # (5.1)   │
         │                                                                     │
         │ # TLS secrets + namespace scoping + mismatch-catching               │
         │ kubectl create secret tls anihpj-tls-cert \                         │
         │     --cert=server.crt --key=server.key -n istio-system  # (5.2/5.4) │
         │ kubectl get deploy istiod -n istio-system -o yaml \                 │
         │     | grep -A1 PILOT_SCOPE_GATEWAY_TO_NAMESPACE          # (5.9)    │
         │ istioctl analyze -n anihpj           # catch GW/VS mismatches early │
         └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    PRACTICE DRILL 🧪 (8 minutes)
         Write and verify a production-shaped Gateway for a new anihpj
         hostname right now — don't just read this, do it:
           1. Write a Gateway named search-gateway in namespace anihpj
              that accepts HTTPS on :443 for host search.anihpj.com,
              tls.mode: SIMPLE, credentialName: search-anihpj-tls-cert
              (5.2, 5.4)
           2. Add an HTTP :80 server on the SAME Gateway with
              tls.httpsRedirect: true so plaintext requests 301 to
              HTTPS (5.4 Pattern 3)
           3. kubectl apply it, then run `kubectl get gateway
              search-gateway -n anihpj` — remember this only proves
              acceptance, not delivery
           4. Prove delivery with `istioctl proxy-config listener
              deploy/istio-ingressgateway -n istio-system` — you should
              see both an 8080 and an 8443 listener for the new host
           5. Namespace-scope it defensively: add a "./" prefix to
              hosts[] so only VirtualServices inside anihpj can bind
              search.anihpj.com (5.8)

    VISUAL SUMMARY

         ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ 🚫 no Gateway                                                     │
         │    anihpj's mesh is sealed — nothing outside can reach it (5.1)   │
         │          │                                                        │
         │          ▼ write spec.selector + spec.servers[]                   │
         │ 🌐 Gateway exists, unverified                                     │
         │    kubectl get gateway OK   istioctl proxy-config listener ??     │
         │    (5.2 — apply is not proof; verify the edge Envoy got it)       │
         │          │                                                        │
         │          ▼ bind with gateways: [name] on a VirtualService         │
         │ 🚦 Gateway + VirtualService, routing live (5.3)                   │
         │    "Gateway alone never routes — treat them as one unit"          │
         │          │                                                        │
         │          ▼ pick a production pattern (5.4)                        │
         │ 🔒 HTTPS live, right TLS mode chosen (5.5, 5.7)                   │
         │    SIMPLE (public) · MUTUAL (B2B) · PASSTHROUGH (pod owns cert)   │
         │    · ISTIO_MUTUAL (east-west) · OPTIONAL_MUTUAL (migration)       │
         │          │                                                        │
         │          ▼ scope it so ONE team's mistake can't hijack the edge   │
         │ 🏢 Namespace-scoped, multi-team-safe (5.8, 5.9)                   │
         │    hosts[] prefix locked · gateways[] fully qualified ·           │
         │    Server.name set · PILOT_SCOPE reach understood                 │
         │          │                                                        │
         │          ▼                                                        │
         │ ✅ api.anihpj.com is open, verified, routed, encrypted, and safe   │
         │    to share across anihpj's teams — Chapter 6 can now assume this │
         │    front door exists and start routing INSIDE it                  │
         └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         .vs-prose — Chapter 5 took anihpj from a sealed mesh to a
         scoped, production-ready front door in five moves: define what
         a Gateway even is and how its selector binds to a real Envoy
         pod (5.1), write and VERIFY its YAML instead of trusting
         kubectl's silent acceptance (5.2), pair it with a
         VirtualService because a Gateway alone never routes anything
         (5.3), choose a battle-tested pattern for HTTP, HTTPS, or a
         redirect (5.4), and pick exactly the right TLS mode for the
         situation from the full five-mode set spread across 5.5 and
         5.7. The last two sections made that Gateway safe to share:
         namespace-scoped hosts and fully-qualified gateway references
         stop one anihpj team's VirtualService from silently hijacking
         another's hostname (5.8), and naming servers plus understanding
         PILOT_SCOPE_GATEWAY_TO_NAMESPACE keep a multi-port, multi-team
         edge debuggable (5.9). Every later chapter in Part 5 —
         VirtualService's routing, DestinationRule's load balancing,
         ServiceEntry's egress — only matters once this front door is
         open, verified, and locked down correctly.

Chapter 6: VirtualService — Smart Traffic Routing
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Chapter 6 of 5-8  ·  Difficulty: 🟡 Intermediate  ·  🎯 Traffic Management —
  35% of the ICA exam (the single biggest domain, and the one Part 5 lives in)
  "Where does a request go once it's already inside the mesh?"

  [WHY THIS MATTERS]
  Chapter 5's Gateway only gets a request through anihpj's front door — it
  says nothing about which of jobpost-api's pods answers it, whether a canary
  version sees any traffic at all, or what happens the instant user-service
  or auth-service has a bad five seconds. VirtualService is the resource that
  answers all of that, and it is the single CRD you will touch the most in
  this entire guide: every canary release, every A/B test, every retry
  policy, every timeout, and every chaos-engineering fault injection in
  anihpj is one YAML block inside a VirtualService's http: list. Get the
  weighted canary split wrong here and real users hit an untested
  jobpost-api:v2; get the retry/timeout math wrong here and a 200ms blip in
  skills-service turns into a page-wide 504. Because Traffic Management is
  35% of the ICA exam — more than Securing Workloads and Troubleshooting
  each on their own — and because VirtualService alone anchors most of that
  domain's named subtopics, this chapter earns careful reading rather than a
  skim.

  [LEARNING OBJECTIVES] By the end of Chapter 6 you can:
  ✅ Explain what a VirtualService governs (WHERE traffic goes) versus what
     a DestinationRule governs (HOW it behaves once it arrives, Chapter 7)
  ✅ Write a weighted canary split (e.g. 90/10) between jobpost-api:v1 and
     :v2, and reason correctly about how Envoy normalizes the weights
  ✅ Route by HTTP header (A/B testing) and by URI prefix/exact/regex
     (path-based routing), ordering rules so the specific ones fire first
  ✅ Configure retries (attempts, perTryTimeout, retryOn) and a request
     timeout whose numbers never conflict with each other's math (6.12)
  ✅ Inject delay and abort faults to prove resilience features actually
     work, and explain why fault + retries/timeout can't share one route
  ✅ Predict, for any multi-rule VirtualService, exactly which single rule
     Envoy matches first — and debug a real "my route isn't firing" bug
  ✅ Scope an Envoy's visibility with the Sidecar CRD and pick the ONE owner
     (app code or mesh) for a given timeout/retry to avoid a conflict

  [EXAM RELEVANCE] Per the official Linux Foundation ICA blueprint (see the
  OFFICIAL ICA EXAM BLUEPRINT panel earlier in this guide), VirtualService is
  graded across most of Traffic Management's named subtopics — everything
  except pure ingress/egress wiring (Gateway/ServiceEntry, Ch5/Ch8) and
  destination-only policy (DestinationRule, Ch7). "Using Fault Injection" is
  even graded as its own standalone subtopic, separate from the resilience
  features it tests:

  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ VirtualService SKILL -> OFFICIAL ICA SUBTOPIC (Domain 2, Traffic Mgmt 35%) │
  │ ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │

  │ Header/path/URI matching (6.4,   -> Configuring Routing within a Service   │

  │ Fault injection (6.8)             -> Using Fault Injection (its OWN named  │
  │                                       subtopic, graded separately)         │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
