    9.5  Custom Metrics and Telemetry API
         - Add custom metrics beyond RED: e.g., number of active jobpost listings
         - Istio Telemetry API for customizing what is measured
         - Add custom labels to metrics (e.g., job_category, user_region)
         [YAML: Telemetry resource adding custom dimension to metrics]
         - DEFINITION: Telemetry API — the CRD (telemetry.istio.io/v1)
           that tunes WHAT Envoy reports (metrics, access logs, trace
           sampling) per mesh, per namespace, or per workload — no app
           code changes, no Envoy restart

         📖 KEY TERM — Telemetry API scope: ONE CRD, THREE possible blast
            radii, decided only by where you point it — mesh-wide in
            istio-system, namespace-wide in anihpj (this section's
            example), or a single workload via spec.selector. Same
            fields every time; only metadata.namespace + selector change.
         - How it works: istiod translates the Telemetry resource into
           Envoy stats config and pushes it over xDS → allow ~30s
           end-to-end (istiod ~5s → xDS push ~5s → next scrape 15s)
         - anihpj scenario: product wants req/s split by job category, so
           ops adds a job_category label sourced from the x-job-category
           header that jobpost-api already sends downstream

         [ANNOTATED YAML — Telemetry: custom dimensions on REQUEST_COUNT]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  apiVersion: telemetry.istio.io/v1    # v1 since Istio 1.22    │
         │  kind: Telemetry                                               │
         │  metadata:                                                     │
         │    name: anihpj-custom-metrics                                 │
         │    namespace: anihpj            ← every workload in anihpj     │
         │  spec:                                                         │
         │    metrics:                                                    │
         │    - providers:                                                │
         │      - name: prometheus         ← the built-in stats provider  │
         │      overrides:                                                │
         │      - match:                                                  │
         │          metric: REQUEST_COUNT      ← istio_requests_total     │
         │          mode: CLIENT_AND_SERVER    ← REPORTER note below      │
         │        tagOverrides:                                           │
         │          job_category:              ← NEW Prometheus label     │
         │            value: request.headers['x-job-category']            │
         │          user_region:               ← 2nd custom dimension     │
         │            value: request.headers['x-user-region']             │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - REPORTER note: every request yields TWO copies of each metric —
           the client sidecar reports reporter="source", the server
           sidecar reports reporter="destination"
         - → mode: CLIENT_AND_SERVER applies the tagOverride to BOTH
           copies; use CLIENT or SERVER to touch only one side
         - → in PromQL always pin one side (reporter="destination") or
           your req/s doubles — 847 req/s becomes a phantom 1,694

         [VERIFY THE NEW DIMENSION — apply, drive traffic, query]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  $ kubectl apply -f telemetry-custom.yaml                      │
         │  $ kubectl exec deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj -- \              │
         │      curl -s -H "x-job-category: devops" \                     │
         │      http://skills-service:8090/api/skills/                    │
         │  $ istioctl dashboard prometheus                               │
         │    PromQL> sum(rate(istio_requests_total{                      │
         │              job_category="devops",                            │
         │              reporter="destination"}[5m]))                     │
         │    → non-empty result = the custom dimension is live ✅         │
         │                                                                │
         │  NOTE: allow ~30s — istiod push (~10s) + next scrape (15s)     │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    9.6  Access Logs — Auditing Every Request
         - DEFINITION: access log — one text line PER REQUEST, written by
           the Envoy sidecar to the istio-proxy container's stdout
         - Why it matters: metrics AGGREGATE (individual requests vanish
           into averages) and traces are SAMPLED (most requests are
           dropped) — access logs keep EVERY request → your audit trail
         - Use them for: security audits ("who hit /admin/ last night?"),
           debugging ONE specific failed request, compliance evidence
         - OFF by default in the production profile — switch on per
           namespace with the Telemetry API (accessLogging), no restart
         - Read them live:
           kubectl logs -f deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj -c istio-proxy
         - Ship stdout to Loki / EFK for retention and cross-service
           search over all anihpj services
         - The logged x-request-id also rides the trace headers → paste
           it into Jaeger search to jump from a log line to its trace

         [ACCESS LOG LINE — field-by-field anatomy (default text format)]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  $ kubectl logs deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj -c istio-proxy    │
         │                                                                │
         │  [2026-06-02T10:30:45.360Z] "GET /api/jobs/123 HTTP/1.1" 200   │
         │  - via_upstream - "-" 0 4523 45 43 "10.244.0.1" "curl/8.5.0"   │
         │  "d209e46f-9ed5-9b61-bbdd-43e22662702a" "anihpj.example.com"   │
         │  "10.244.1.5:8000" inbound|8000|| 127.0.0.6:52413 ...          │
         ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │  FIELD                          MEANING                        │
         │  [2026-06-02T10:30:45.360Z]     request START time (UTC)       │
         │  "GET /api/jobs/123 HTTP/1.1"   method + path + protocol       │
         │  200                            HTTP response code             │
         │  -                              response flags: "-" = none     │
         │                                 (UH/UO/NR/DC = Envoy-level     │
         │                                 failures — memorize these!)    │
         │  via_upstream                   response came from the app     │
         │  0 4523                         bytes received / bytes sent    │
         │  45 43                          total ms / upstream ms →       │
         │                                 45-43 = 2ms spent inside Envoy │
         │  "10.244.0.1"                   X-Forwarded-For (caller IP)    │
         │  "curl/8.5.0"                   user-agent header              │
         │  "d209e46f-...-702a"            x-request-id → paste into      │
         │                                 Jaeger to find the trace       │
         │  "anihpj.example.com"           :authority / Host header       │
         │  "10.244.1.5:8000"              upstream host (the app itself) │
         │  inbound|8000||                 Envoy cluster: direction+port  │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [ANNOTATED YAML — Telemetry: switch on access logs (envoy)]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  apiVersion: telemetry.istio.io/v1     # v1 since Istio 1.22   │
         │  kind: Telemetry                                               │
         │  metadata:                                                     │
         │    name: anihpj-access-logs                                    │
         │    namespace: anihpj            ← apply here: anihpj pods only │
         │  spec:                          #  (istio-system = mesh-wide)  │
         │    accessLogging:                                              │
         │    - providers:                                                │
         │      - name: envoy              ← built-in stdout text logger  │
         │      filter:                    ← OPTIONAL — drop this block   │
         │        expression: response.code >= 400    # to log everything │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - JSON instead of text: set meshConfig.accessLogEncoding: JSON —
           easier for Loki/EFK to parse field-by-field
         - ⚠️ volume warning: at 847 req/s, full access logging writes
           ~73M lines/day for jobpost-api alone — keep the errors-only
           filter in production, log everything only while debugging

    9.7  Control Plane Metrics — Monitoring istiod Health
         - DEFINITION: control-plane metrics — istiod monitoring ITSELF,
           exposed on the istiod pod at :15014/metrics (Prometheus
           scrapes it automatically alongside the sidecars)
         - Why it matters: 9.1-9.6 watch anihpj's health; these watch
           ISTIO's health — a sick istiod means STALE proxies, stuck
           cert rotation, and route changes that never arrive
         - Where to look: Grafana "Istio Control Plane Dashboard"
           (pre-built) → istiod CPU/memory, push latency, error counters
         - Quick manual peek:
           kubectl exec deploy/istiod -n istio-system -- \
             curl -s localhost:15014/metrics | grep pilot_
         - Three metric LEVELS — keep them apart on the exam:
           • proxy-level: raw Envoy stats (envoy_cluster_*, connection +
             TLS handshake errors) — deepest debugging layer
           • service-level: the istio_* RED metrics of 9.2-9.3 — what
             the Grafana dashboards show; the most-tested on the ICA
           • control-plane: istiod's own health — this section

         [ISTIOD SELF-MONITORING METRICS — watchlist + alert thresholds]
         ┌────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┐
         │  METRIC (istiod :15014)        │  WHAT IT MEANS / ALERT WHEN      │
         ├────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
         │  pilot_proxy_convergence_time  │  time from config change to      │
         │  (histogram)                   │  proxy ACK — ALERT: p99 > 1s     │
         ├────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
         │  pilot_xds_pushes (counter)    │  xDS pushes by type (cds/eds/    │
         │                                │  lds/rds) — sudden spike =       │
         │                                │  config churn storm              │
         ├────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
         │  pilot_total_xds_rejects       │  Envoy REJECTED a config push    │
         │  (counter)                     │  — ALERT: any increase (> 0)     │
         ├────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
         │  citadel_server_csr_count      │  workload cert CSRs signed —     │
         │  (counter)                     │  a FLAT line = rotation stuck    │
         ├────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
         │  citadel_server_root_cert_     │  root CA expiry (unix time) —    │
         │  expiry_timestamp (gauge)      │  ALERT: fewer than 30 days left  │
         ├────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
         │  galley_validation_failed      │  CRD rejected by the validating  │
         │  (counter)                     │  webhook — ALERT: any increase   │
         ├────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
         │  pilot_xds (gauge)             │  proxies connected to THIS       │
         │                                │  istiod — should equal your      │
         │                                │  sidecar count                   │
         └────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┘

         [PROMETHEUS ALERT RULES — istiod health, copy-paste PromQL]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  # 1) proxies rejecting config (should ALWAYS be zero)       │
         │  increase(pilot_total_xds_rejects[10m]) > 0                  │
         │                                                              │
         │  # 2) config slow to converge (p99 above 1 second)           │
         │  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(                          │
         │    pilot_proxy_convergence_time_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 1    │
         │                                                              │
         │  # 3) root CA certificate expiring within 30 days            │
         │  citadel_server_root_cert_expiry_timestamp - time()          │
         │    < 30 * 24 * 3600                                          │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    9.8  Deep Dive — Counters, Gauges, Histograms in PromQL
         - Istio emits three Prometheus metric TYPES — using the wrong
           PromQL function on the wrong type produces a meaningless graph
         - DEFINITION: COUNTER — a value that only ever goes UP (and
           resets to 0 when the pod restarts); istio_requests_total
           → NEVER graph it raw: you get "145,632 and climbing"
           → wrap it in rate() / increase() to get per-second truth
         - DEFINITION: GAUGE — a snapshot that goes up AND down;
           pilot_xds (connected proxies), envoy_cluster_upstream_cx_active
           → query it raw, or smooth it with avg_over_time()
         - DEFINITION: HISTOGRAM — observations sorted into cumulative
           "le" (less-or-equal) buckets; the buckets themselves are
           counters; istio_request_duration_milliseconds_bucket
           → extract percentiles with histogram_quantile()
         - Real scenario: during the skills-service incident the on-call
           graphed istio_requests_total raw and saw a line climbing
           forever → panic; wrapped in rate() it showed a steady 89 req/s
           — traffic was normal, the 8.1% errors were the real problem

         [THREE METRIC TYPES — the right PromQL for each]
         ┌──────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  COUNTER     │  istio_requests_total                          │
         │              │  only increases → use rate() / increase()      │
         │              │  raw query = a meaningless growing number      │
         ├──────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │  GAUGE       │  pilot_xds, envoy_cluster_upstream_cx_active   │
         │              │  up AND down → query raw or avg_over_time()    │
         ├──────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │  HISTOGRAM   │  istio_request_duration_milliseconds_bucket    │
         │              │  cumulative buckets → histogram_quantile()     │
         │              │  bucket label: le="5","10",...,"+Inf" (ms)     │
         └──────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [SAMPLE PROMQL — the RED queries for jobpost-api]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  # RATE — requests per second (COUNTER + rate)                 │
         │  sum(rate(istio_requests_total{reporter="destination",         │
         │    destination_service=~"jobpost-api.*"}[5m]))                 │
         │  → 847 req/s for jobpost-api                                   │
         │                                                                │
         │  # ERRORS — share of 5xx responses                             │
         │  sum(rate(istio_requests_total{reporter="destination",         │
         │    destination_service=~"jobpost-api.*",                       │
         │    response_code=~"5.."}[5m]))                                 │
         │  / sum(rate(istio_requests_total{reporter="destination",       │
         │    destination_service=~"jobpost-api.*"}[5m])) * 100           │
         │  → 2.1 (%)                                                     │
         │                                                                │
         │  # DURATION — p99 latency (HISTOGRAM + histogram_quantile)     │
         │  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(                            │
         │    istio_request_duration_milliseconds_bucket{                 │
         │      destination_service=~"jobpost-api.*"}[5m])) by (le))      │
         │  → 234 (ms)                                                    │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [CARDINALITY WARNING — labels multiply time series]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  istio_requests_total already carries ~25 labels               │
         │  (source_workload, destination_service, response_code, ...)    │
         │                                                                │
         │  time series ≈ every UNIQUE label combination that occurs      │
         │  anihpj today:  10 workloads × 10 services × 10 codes × 2      │
         │                 protocols × 2 TLS modes ≈ 4,000 series ✅ fine  │
         │                                                                │
         │  now add a BAD tagOverride: user_id from the x-user-id header  │
         │  50,000 users × 4,000 = 200,000,000 time series                │
         │  → Prometheus eats RAM → OOMKilled → NO metrics for anyone ❌   │
         │                                                                │
         │  RULE: only add LOW-cardinality dimensions (category, region,  │
         │  tier — a handful of values); NEVER user IDs, request IDs,     │
         │  session tokens, or full URLs                                  │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘


    9.9  The Standard Dimensions — Full Label Reference for istio_requests_total
         - DEFINITION: standard dimensions — the ~25 labels Istio's proxy
           extension attaches to every istio_requests_total (and
           istio_request_duration_milliseconds, istio_request_bytes,
           istio_response_bytes) sample automatically, before any
           Telemetry API customization ever runs
         - Why it matters: 9.5's tagOverrides ADD labels on top of this
           set — you can't design a good custom dimension, or explain
           an empty PromQL result, without knowing what's already there
         - Every dimension below is recorded TWICE per request — once
           by the caller's sidecar (reporter="source") and once by the
           callee's sidecar (reporter="destination"); see 9.5's
           REPORTER note
         - Four groups: WHO called (source), WHO answered (destination),
           WHAT happened (request/response), and HOW + WHERE
           (security/topology)

         ┌──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ VISUAL: SOURCE-IDENTITY DIMENSIONS -- who sent the request                │
         ├──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ LABEL (Prometheus name)      │ WHAT IT CAPTURES                           │
         ├──────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ reporter                     │ side that recorded it: source|destination  │
         │ source_workload              │ calling Deployment, e.g. jobpost-api       │
         │ source_workload_namespace    │ namespace the caller runs in               │
         │ source_principal             │ caller SPIFFE ID (mTLS identity)           │
         │ source_app                   │ app label of the caller Pod                │
         │ source_version               │ version label of the caller Pod            │
         └──────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         ┌────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ VISUAL: DESTINATION-IDENTITY DIMENSIONS -- who received it                              │
         ├────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ LABEL (Prometheus name)        │ WHAT IT CAPTURES                                       │
         ├────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ destination_workload           │ called Deployment, e.g. skills-service                 │
         │ destination_workload_namespace │ namespace the callee runs in                           │
         │ destination_principal          │ callee SPIFFE ID (mTLS identity)                       │
         │ destination_app                │ app label of the callee Pod                            │
         │ destination_version            │ version label of the callee Pod                        │
         │ destination_service            │ FQDN dialed, e.g. skills-svc.anihpj.svc.cluster.local  │
         │ destination_service_name       │ short Service name, e.g. skills-service                │
         │ destination_service_namespace  │ namespace of the Service object                        │
         └────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         ┌────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ VISUAL: REQUEST/RESPONSE DIMENSIONS -- what happened            │
         ├────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ LABEL (Prometheus name)│ WHAT IT CAPTURES                       │
         ├────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ request_protocol       │ http | grpc | https | tcp              │
         │ response_code          │ HTTP status: 200, 404, 500 ...         │
         │ grpc_response_status   │ gRPC status code (grpc traffic only)   │
         └────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────┘

         ┌────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ VISUAL: SECURITY & TOPOLOGY DIMENSIONS -- how + where                           │
         ├────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ LABEL (Prometheus name)        │ WHAT IT CAPTURES                               │
         ├────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ connection_security_policy     │ mutual_tls | none | unknown                    │
         │ response_flags                 │ Envoy outcome code: UH, UO, NR, DC, "-"        │
         │ source_canonical_service       │ stable service name (survives version bumps)   │
         │ source_canonical_revision      │ stable revision tag of the caller              │
         │ destination_canonical_service  │ stable service name of the callee              │
         │ destination_canonical_revision │ stable revision tag of the callee              │
         │ source_cluster                 │ multicluster: cluster the caller runs in       │
         │ destination_cluster            │ multicluster: cluster the callee runs in       │
         └────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - anihpj scenario: a security audit needs every caller still
           hitting skills-service in plaintext — combine
           destination_workload with connection_security_policy:

         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ ANIHPJ SCENARIO: security audit -- find any plaintext hop into           │
         │ skills-service (should be 100% mutual_tls inside the mesh)               │
         │                                                                          │
         │ sum(rate(istio_requests_total{                                           │
         │   reporter="destination",                                                │
         │   destination_workload="skills-service",                                 │
         │   connection_security_policy!="mutual_tls"}[5m]))                        │
         │ by (source_workload, connection_security_policy)                         │
         │                                                                          │
         │ -> any non-zero result names the exact caller still sending              │
         │    plaintext -- fix its DestinationRule/PeerAuthentication (Ch6)         │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    9.10  TCP Metrics — Measuring Raw (Non-HTTP) Connections
         - DEFINITION: TCP metrics — the 4 counters Istio's proxy
           extension emits for connections it can only see as bytes
           (Postgres, Redis, raw gRPC without HTTP framing detected, any
           protocol the mesh treats as plain TCP)
         - Why it matters: 9.2-9.8 all assume HTTP (response_code, path,
           RED). A TCP hop has none of that — anihpj's Postgres
           connection is real mesh traffic that still needs metrics
         - How Istio decides HTTP vs TCP: protocol sniffing (or an
           explicit port-name prefix like tcp- on the Service) — traffic
           recognized as HTTP gets the full istio_requests_total
           treatment; everything else gets only these 4 counters

         🔧 UNDER THE HOOD. The sniff happens once, at connection setup,
            entirely inside Envoy's own process — it inspects the first
            bytes for HTTP framing (a request line, or the HTTP/2 preface)
            before a single byte reaches the upstream app. Guess HTTP: the
            connection gets the full istio_requests_total treatment for
            its whole lifetime. Guess TCP (or skip the guess entirely
            because the Service port already carries a tcp- name prefix):
            it's locked onto only the 4 counters above, for skills-
            service's Postgres hop and everything like it.

         ┌──────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ VISUAL: THE FOUR TCP METRICS -- for raw (non-HTTP) traffic                        │
         ├──────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ METRIC NAME                          │ TYPE + MEANING                             │
         ├──────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ istio_tcp_connections_opened_total   │ COUNTER -- a new TCP connection was opened │
         │ istio_tcp_connections_closed_total   │ COUNTER -- a TCP connection was closed     │
         │ istio_tcp_sent_bytes_total           │ COUNTER -- bytes sent, proxy to downstream │
         │ istio_tcp_received_bytes_total       │ COUNTER -- bytes received from downstream  │
         └──────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ ANIHPJ SCENARIO: skills-service -> PostgreSQL (raw TCP, not HTTP)        │
         │                                                                          │
         │ skills-service opens a plain TCP connection to postgres:5432             │
         │ (a DB driver speaks the Postgres wire protocol -- not HTTP --            │
         │  so Envoy can only see bytes and connection events, no path,             │
         │  method, or response_code)                                               │
         ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ 1. CONNECTION OPENS                                                      │
         │    istio_tcp_connections_opened_total{                                   │
         │      destination_service="postgres.anihpj.svc.cluster.local"} += 1       │
         ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ 2. DATA FLOWS (recorded continuously, every 15s by default --            │
         │    interval name: tcpReportingDuration, per the official docs)           │
         │    istio_tcp_sent_bytes_total{...}     += bytes proxy->downstream        │
         │    istio_tcp_received_bytes_total{...} += bytes downstream->proxy        │
         ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ 3. CONNECTION CLOSES                                                     │
         │    istio_tcp_connections_closed_total{                                   │
         │      destination_service="postgres.anihpj.svc.cluster.local"} += 1       │
         │    (final byte counters flush on close too)                              │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ # throughput -- bytes/sec flowing to postgres (COUNTER + rate)           │
         │ sum(rate(istio_tcp_sent_bytes_total{                                     │
         │   destination_service=~"postgres.*"}[5m]))                               │
         │                                                                          │
         │ # connection churn -- opens vs closes should track each other;           │
         │ # opens without matching closes = a connection leak                      │
         │ sum(rate(istio_tcp_connections_opened_total{                             │
         │   destination_service=~"postgres.*"}[5m]))                               │
         │                                                                          │
         │ # active connections right now (GAUGE-style via subtraction)             │
         │ sum(istio_tcp_connections_opened_total{destination_service=~             │
         │   "postgres.*"}) - sum(istio_tcp_connections_closed_total{               │
         │   destination_service=~"postgres.*"})                                    │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - TCP metrics carry a NARROWER label set than HTTP: still
           destination_service, source_workload, reporter,
           connection_security_policy — but NEVER response_code,
           request_protocol, or grpc_response_status (there is no
           status code to read in raw bytes)

    9.11  The Telemetry API Deep Dive — Full Resource Structure
         - DEFINITION: recap from 9.5 — Telemetry (telemetry.istio.io/v1)
           is the CRD that tunes metrics, access logs, and tracing per
           mesh/namespace/workload; this section is the FULL field map,
           not just the single tagOverrides slice 9.5 showed

         ┌─────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ VISUAL: Telemetry spec -- THE FOUR TOP-LEVEL FIELDS                     │
         ├─────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ spec: FIELD     │ WHAT IT CONFIGURES                                    │
         ├─────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ selector        │ label-match workloads in THIS namespace               │
         │ targetRefs      │ newer alternative: point at a Gateway/Service         │
         │ metrics[]       │ providers + overrides for metrics (9.5, 9.11)         │
         │ accessLogging[] │ providers + filter for access logs (9.6)              │
         │ tracing[]       │ providers + sampling % for traces (Chapter 10)        │
         └─────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         ┌─────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ VISUAL: match.metric -- THE IstioMetric ENUM (Telemetry API)   │
         ├─────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ match: metric: VALUE    │ TARGETS THIS REAL METRIC             │
         ├─────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ ALL_METRICS             │ every Istio default metric at once   │
         │ REQUEST_COUNT           │ istio_requests_total                 │
         │ REQUEST_DURATION        │ istio_request_duration_milliseconds  │
         │ REQUEST_SIZE            │ istio_request_bytes                  │
         │ RESPONSE_SIZE           │ istio_response_bytes                 │
         │ TCP_OPENED_CONNECTIONS  │ istio_tcp_connections_opened_total   │
         │ TCP_CLOSED_CONNECTIONS  │ istio_tcp_connections_closed_total   │
         │ TCP_SENT_BYTES          │ istio_tcp_sent_bytes_total           │
         │ TCP_RECEIVED_BYTES      │ istio_tcp_received_bytes_total       │
         │ GRPC_REQUEST_MESSAGES   │ istio_request_messages_total         │
         │ GRPC_RESPONSE_MESSAGES  │ istio_response_messages_total        │
         └─────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────┘

         ┌─────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ VISUAL: MetricsOverrides + TagOverride -- FULL FIELD MAP                 │
         ├─────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ FIELD                   │ MEANING                                        │
         ├─────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ overrides[].match       │ MetricSelector: metric + mode (9.5)            │
         │ overrides[].disabled    │ bool -- true STOPS this metric being emitted   │
         │ overrides[].tagOverrides│ map<label name, TagOverride>                   │
         ├─────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ tagOverrides.X.operation│ UPSERT (default) or REMOVE                     │
         │ tagOverrides.X.value    │ attribute expr, UPSERT only (9.5 example)      │
         └─────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - anihpj scenario: RESPONSE_SIZE for jobpost-api is disabled
           (nobody dashboards on it, and it's a full histogram of
           cardinality-multiplying series) AND the
           source_canonical_revision tag is REMOVEd mesh-wide (anihpj
           ships canary-free, so that tag is dead weight on every series)

         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │apiVersion: telemetry.istio.io/v1    # v1 since Istio 1.22            │
         │kind: Telemetry                                                       │
         │metadata:                                                             │
         │  name: anihpj-trim-metrics                                           │
         │  namespace: anihpj                                                   │
         │spec:                                                                 │
         │  metrics:                                                            │
         │  - providers:                                                        │
         │    - name: prometheus                                                │
         │    overrides:                                                        │
         │    - match:                                                          │
         │        metric: RESPONSE_SIZE   ← disable one metric                  │
         │        mode: SERVER            ← only the callee side                │
         │      disabled: true            ← drop it for jobpost-api             │
         │    - match:                                                          │
         │        metric: ALL_METRICS     ← every remaining metric              │
         │      tagOverrides:                                                   │
         │        source_canonical_revision:                                    │
         │          operation: REMOVE     ← anihpj has no canary                │
         │                                 #   rollouts -- cut cardinality      │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - OLD way vs NEW way: before the Telemetry API, ANY metric
           customization meant hand-writing an EnvoyFilter patch against
           Envoy's stats config (Lua or WASM, redeploy every matching
           proxy). The Telemetry API replaced that for tagging,
           disabling, and re-scoping — but EnvoyFilter is still the ONLY
           way to invent a brand-new metric NAME from scratch; the
           Telemetry API can only shape Istio's own default metrics
         - ⚠️ since Istio 1.18 the Prometheus EnvoyFilter is no longer
           installed by default (meshConfig.defaultProviders drives it
           instead) — and a hand-written EnvoyFilter targeting the SAME
           stats as a Telemetry resource is NOT supported together;
           pick one mechanism per metric, don't mix them

         ┌────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ ASPECT             │ EnvoyFilter (OLD WAY)            │ Telemetry API (NEW)                    │
         ├────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ How you scope it   │ patches the proxy, error-prone   │ selector / targetRefs (namespace)      │
         │ New custom metric  │ yes -- Lua/Wasm, full control    │ no -- relabels EXISTING metrics only   │
         │ Add a dimension    │ Lua/Wasm, redeploy proxies       │ tagOverrides UPSERT, no restart        │
         │ Drop a dimension   │ Lua/Wasm, redeploy proxies       │ tagOverrides REMOVE, no restart        │
         │ Disable a metric   │ hand-edit stats config           │ overrides[].disabled: true             │
         │ Mix the two        │ not supported together (1.18+)   │ the documented, recommended path       │
         └────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────┘

    9.12  Access Log Format Reference — Every Default Field, Field by Field
         - DEFINITION: recap from 9.6 — this section gives the COMPLETE
           default TEXT format string verbatim (9.6 only walked through
           the fields visible in one example line) plus the JSON
           alternative
         - meshConfig field, not the Telemetry API, decides the FORMAT
           (Telemetry API's accessLogging only turns logging on/off and
           picks the provider)

         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ this is meshConfig.accessLogFormat's DEFAULT value verbatim:         │
         │                                                                      │
         │[%START_TIME%] "%REQ(:METHOD)% %REQ(X-ENVOY-ORIGINAL-PATH?:PATH)%     │
         │%PROTOCOL%" %RESPONSE_CODE% %RESPONSE_FLAGS% %RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%  │
         │%CONNECTION_TERMINATION_DETAILS% "%UPSTREAM_TRANSPORT_FAILURE_REASON%"│
         │%BYTES_RECEIVED% %BYTES_SENT% %DURATION%                              │
         │%RESP(X-ENVOY-UPSTREAM-SERVICE-TIME)% "%REQ(X-FORWARDED-FOR)%"        │
         │"%REQ(USER-AGENT)%" "%REQ(X-REQUEST-ID)%" "%REQ(:AUTHORITY)%"         │
         │"%UPSTREAM_HOST%" %UPSTREAM_CLUSTER_RAW% %UPSTREAM_LOCAL_ADDRESS%     │
         │%DOWNSTREAM_LOCAL_ADDRESS% %DOWNSTREAM_REMOTE_ADDRESS%                │
         │%REQUESTED_SERVER_NAME% %ROUTE_NAME%                                  │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         ┌──────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ VISUAL: THE DEFAULT TEXT ACCESS LOG -- every macro, in order                    │
         ├──────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ ENVOY LOG MACRO                      │ MEANING                                  │
         ├──────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ %START_TIME%                         │ request start timestamp, UTC             │
         │ %REQ(:METHOD)%                       │ HTTP method: GET, POST ...               │
         │ %REQ(X-ENVOY-ORIGINAL-PATH?:PATH)%   │ the request path                         │
         │ %PROTOCOL%                           │ HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, ...                    │
         ├──────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ %RESPONSE_CODE%                      │ HTTP status code                         │
         │ %RESPONSE_FLAGS%                     │ Envoy outcome: UH, UO, NR, DC, "-"       │
         │ %RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%              │ why: via_upstream, route_not_found...    │
         │ %CONNECTION_TERMINATION_DETAILS%     │ why the connection closed, usually "-"   │
         │ %UPSTREAM_TRANSPORT_FAILURE_REASON%  │ TLS/transport failure reason, or "-"     │
         ├──────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ %BYTES_RECEIVED%                     │ request body size, bytes                 │
         │ %BYTES_SENT%                         │ response body size, bytes                │
         │ %DURATION%                           │ total request time, ms                   │
         │ %RESP(X-ENVOY-UPSTREAM-SERVICE-TIME)%│ upstream-only time, ms                   │
         ├──────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ %REQ(X-FORWARDED-FOR)%               │ caller IP chain                          │
         │ %REQ(USER-AGENT)%                    │ client user-agent string                 │
         │ %REQ(X-REQUEST-ID)%                  │ correlation id -- paste into Jaeger      │
         │ %REQ(:AUTHORITY)%                    │ :authority / Host header                 │
         ├──────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ %UPSTREAM_HOST%                      │ backend ip:port that served the request  │
         │ %UPSTREAM_CLUSTER_RAW%               │ Envoy cluster: direction|port|subset|svc │
         │ %UPSTREAM_LOCAL_ADDRESS%             │ proxy's own ip:port dialing upstream     │
         │ %DOWNSTREAM_LOCAL_ADDRESS%           │ ip:port the client connected to          │
         │ %DOWNSTREAM_REMOTE_ADDRESS%          │ the calling client's ip:port             │
         │ %REQUESTED_SERVER_NAME%              │ SNI hostname (TLS handshake)             │
         │ %ROUTE_NAME%                         │ matched VirtualService route name        │
         └──────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - Three meshConfig fields control access logs, independent of
           the Telemetry API's on/off switch:
           • accessLogFile — destination path, default EMPTY (disabled);
             the demo install profile sets it to /dev/stdout for you —
             the default/production profiles do not, by design
           • accessLogEncoding — TEXT (default, shown above) or JSON
           • accessLogFormat — replace the ENTIRE default string above
             with your own macros (add/drop/reorder fields)

         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ apiVersion: telemetry.istio.io/v1                                        │
         │ kind: Telemetry                                                          │
         │ metadata:                                                                │
         │   name: anihpj-json-logs                                                 │
         │   namespace: anihpj                                                      │
         │ spec:                                                                    │
         │   accessLogging:                                                         │
         │   - providers:                                                           │
         │     - name: envoy                                                        │
         ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ meshConfig.accessLogEncoding: JSON  # set mesh-wide at install time      │
         │ (Telemetry API turns logging ON/OFF and picks the provider; the          │
         │  TEXT vs JSON *encoding* choice itself is still a meshConfig field)      │
         ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ resulting anihpj log line (keys mirror the TEXT macros, lower-           │
         │ cased -- one JSON object per request, easy for Loki/EFK to index):       │
         │ {"start_time":"2026-06-02T10:30:45.360Z","method":"GET",                 │
         │  "path":"/api/jobs/123","response_code":200,                             │
         │  "response_flags":"-","bytes_received":0,"bytes_sent":4523,              │
         │  "duration":45,"upstream_service_time":"43",                             │
         │  "upstream_cluster":"inbound|8000||",                                    │
         │  "request_id":"d209e46f-9ed5-9b61-bbdd-43e22662702a",                    │
         │  "authority":"anihpj.example.com"}                                       │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     🔧 UNDER THE HOOD — one incident, five hops: counter to red panel
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    9.8 taught you the three PromQL metric types and 9.11 mapped the full
    Telemetry CRD — this is neither. This is the clock: exactly how long it
    takes the skills-service incident to travel from one Envoy counter to a
    red rectangle on a human's screen, and why every hop above takes the
    time it takes.

    ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ THE skills-service INCIDENT -- FROM ONE COUNTER TO A RED GRAFANA PANEL     │
    │                                                                            │
    │ HOP 1 -- Envoy counts it the instant it happens (in-process, no network)   │
    │   istio_requests_total{destination_service="skills-service",               │
    │     response_code="500"} += 1                                              │
    │   istio_request_duration_milliseconds{...} = 1240                          │
    │                                                                            │
    │ HOP 2 -- the counter sits on the sidecar, stale until someone scrapes it   │
    │   origin: Envoy :15090 raw stats -> merged onto istio-agent :15020 (9.3)   │
    │   -- nothing has left the Pod yet; this is a number sitting in memory      │
    │                                                                            │
    │ HOP 3 -- Prometheus's scrape tick pulls it into the time-series DB         │
    │   scrape_interval: 15s (9.3) -> worst case 15s of lag before Prometheus    │
    │   has even SEEN the bad request exists                                     │
    │                                                                            │
    │ HOP 4 -- PromQL turns raw cumulative counters into a real percentage (9.8) │
    │   sum(rate(istio_requests_total{destination_service=~"skills-service.*",   │
    │     response_code=~"5.."}[5m])) /                                          │
    │   sum(rate(istio_requests_total{destination_service=~"skills-service.*"}   │
    │     [5m])) * 100                                                           │
    │   -> as bad requests fill the 5m window: 2.1% baseline climbs to 8.1%      │
    │                                                                            │
    │ HOP 5 -- Grafana re-runs that same query on its own panel refresh timer    │
    │   Istio Service Dashboard (9.4), skills-service panel turns red            │
    │   -> total time, first 500 to human sees red:                              │
    │      scrape lag (<=15s) + Grafana refresh (10-30s typ.) = under a minute   │
    │                                                                            │
    │ -- this is the automatic engine behind 9.2's dashboard mockup: nobody      │
    │    ran a query by hand -- the pipeline above was already running before    │
    │    the incident even started                                               │
    └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     ⚡ SPEED TIPS
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
      ⚡ Reach for the RED trio first (rate / errors / duration) before
         anything fancier — most "what's wrong" questions die right there.
      ⚡ Wrap every counter in rate() or increase() before you look at it —
         a raw istio_requests_total graph is always a misleading staircase.
      ⚡ Pin reporter="destination" (or "source") in every query — forget
         it and every number silently doubles (847 becomes a phantom
         1,694, see 9.5).
      ⚡ istioctl dashboard grafana/prometheus opens the right port-forward
         for you — faster than hunting down the Service name and port.
      ⚡ RED is for services; USE (Utilization/Saturation/Errors) is for
         the node a service runs on — don't reach for CPU graphs when it's
         a service's error rate that moved.
      ⚡ A flat citadel_server_csr_count or a climbing
         pilot_total_xds_rejects (9.7) means istiod is the problem, not
         anihpj — check control-plane metrics before you blame the app.

    │                                                                         │
    │ ① REQUEST: GET /api/jobs/ -> jobpost-api                                │
    │    (mesh baseline: 847 req/s, 2.1% errors, p99 234ms)                   │
    │                               ▼                                         │
    │ ② ENVOY SIDECAR records it, all in one pass:                            │
    │    • HTTP RED counters + duration histogram ............ 9.2, 9.8       │
    │    • ~25 standard dimensions stamped on every sample ..... 9.9          │
    │    • 4 TCP counters for any raw hop (e.g. -> postgres) .. 9.10          │
    │    • one access-log line, full default field set ... 9.6, 9.12          │
    │                               ▼                                         │
    │ ③ COLLECTION: :15090 raw stats merge onto :15020 (istio-agent)          │
    │    -> Prometheus scrapes every 15s ......................... 9.3        │
    │                               ▼                                         │
    │ ④ SHAPING (optional): Telemetry API adds/drops dimensions,              │
    │    flips access logs on -- no restart, ~30s to take effect .. 9.5, 9.11 │
    │                               ▼                                         │
    │ ⑤ READING: PromQL turns counters/histograms into a real                 │
    │    rate / error% / p99 -> Grafana renders the panel ....... 9.4, 9.8    │
    │                               ▼                                         │
    │ ⑥ WATCHING THE WATCHER (parallel path, always on): istiod's own         │
    │    :15014 metrics confirm the pipeline ITSELF is healthy .... 9.7       │
    │                               ▼                                         │
    │ ⑦ OUTCOME: skills-service flagged -- 8.1% errors, p99 1240ms            │
    │    -> the ONE clue that sends you to Chapter 10 to find WHERE           │
    │       in its call chain the 1,240ms is actually lost                    │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    CAPTION: one request into jobpost-api triggers Envoy to record HTTP RED
    counters, ~25 standard dimensions, TCP counters for any raw hop, and a
    full access-log line — all before Prometheus ever scrapes anything.
    Collection merges Envoy's raw stats onto the agent's port and pulls
    them in every 15 seconds; the Telemetry API can reshape what gets
    collected without a restart; PromQL and Grafana turn the raw numbers
    into a panel a human can read at a glance; and istiod's own metrics
    confirm the whole pipeline is healthy in parallel. The payoff is the
    same one this chapter opened with: skills-service lights up at 8.1%
    errors and a 1,240ms p99, and that single red signal is precisely what
    Chapter 10 picks up next to find WHERE inside skills-service the time
    is actually going.

Chapter 10: Distributed Tracing — Follow Any Request Across All Services
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Chapter 10 of 9-11 (Part 6: Observability) · Difficulty: 🟡 Intermediate
    Tooling for the Troubleshooting domain (20% of the ICA exam) — not a
    graded domain of its own
    🧠 The hook: Chapter 9's metrics just named skills-service as a suspect
    — "but where, exactly, inside that request, is it slow?"

    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     WHY THIS CHAPTER MATTERS
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    Chapter 9's RED metrics can tell an anihpj on-call engineer that
    skills-service's p99 latency just jumped to 1,240ms — that names WHAT
    looks wrong. But a Grafana panel cannot show you the one GET /jobs/
    request that took 342ms, or which of its downstream hops — user-
    service, auth-service, skills-service, location-service — actually
    burned the time. Distributed tracing closes exactly that gap: it
    follows ONE real request as it crosses every service boundary in the
    anihpj mesh and renders the result as a Gantt-style waterfall where the
    widest bar IS the answer. In this chapter's running incident, a 342ms
    trace through jobpost-api exposes a single 195ms skills-service span
    as the bottleneck — a fact no dashboard of averages could ever surface
    on its own. By the end of this chapter you will be able to go from
    "users say the site feels slow" to "the skills-service call inside
    trace 7f3e9a12b4c06d8e is the culprit" in about the time it takes to
    open one dashboard.

    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     LEARNING OBJECTIVES — BY THE END OF THIS CHAPTER YOU CAN...
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    ✅ Explain the difference between a trace and a span, and name the five
       fields every span carries (traceId, spanId, parentSpanId, duration,
       tags)
    ✅ Read a Jaeger Gantt waterfall for an anihpj GET /jobs/ request and
       identify the widest bar as the bottleneck span
    ✅ Explain why Envoy's automatic span creation still requires your
       Django code to forward the x-b3-* headers between hops
    ✅ Set a Telemetry resource's randomSamplingPercentage for dev (100%)
       vs prod (1-5%), and force-sample one prod request with
       x-b3-flags: 1
    ✅ Compare B3 headers against W3C traceparent/tracestate, and name the
       providers that speak each (Zipkin, Jaeger, OpenTelemetry)
    ✅ Diagnose "zero traces" or "many 1-span traces" symptoms using the
       sampling-precedence order and the header-propagation checklist
    ✅ Add custom tags (literal, environment, header) to anihpj spans via
       the Telemetry API, without leaving the legacy MeshConfig block
       fighting it

    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     EXAM / ICA RELEVANCE  🎯
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    Distributed tracing is NOT a named ICA exam domain by itself — Part 6
    (Chapters 9-11: Metrics, Tracing, Kiali) is tooling in service of the
    Troubleshooting domain (20% of the exam), alongside Config, Control
    Plane, and Data Plane troubleshooting. You will not be asked to define
    a span in isolation on the exam. You WILL be handed scenarios shaped
    exactly like this chapter's incidents — "traces are missing," "traces
    show 1 span instead of 5," "sampling was raised but nothing changed" —
    and be expected to reach for the right knob (Telemetry resource, pod
    annotation, header propagation) fast. Treat 10.5-10.9's deep dives as
    the troubleshooting muscle memory the exam is actually testing.
