    10.1 What is Distributed Tracing?
         - A single HTTP request to anihpj /jobs/ triggers 5+ service calls
         - Without tracing: you see an error but have no idea WHICH service caused it
         - With tracing: see the ENTIRE call chain — every hop, every duration
         - Key concepts:
           • Trace: the entire journey of one request (root span + child spans)
           • Span: one unit of work (one service call) with start time + duration
           • Trace ID: unique ID linking all spans of one request
           • Parent/Child: shows the hierarchy of calls
         [TRACE DIAGRAM: one request → many spans visualized as Gantt chart]

         [DISTRIBUTED TRACE — anihpj GET /jobs/ request]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  Trace ID: 7f3e9a12b4c06d8e  Duration: 342ms                │
         │                                                              │
         │  ▶ jobpost-api (GET /jobs/)                    0ms → 342ms  │
         │    ▶ user-service (GET /users/42/)            12ms → 87ms   │
         │      ▶ auth-service (POST /validate-token/)  15ms → 45ms   │
         │    ▶ skills-service (GET /skills/?ids=1,2,3)  92ms → 287ms  │
         │      ← 195ms ← SLOW! This is the bottleneck                │
         │    ▶ location-service (GET /locations/7/)    295ms → 320ms  │
         │                                                              │
         │  🔍 skills-service call took 195ms — investigate!           │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - DEFINITION: a span is the atomic unit of tracing — ONE timed
           operation in ONE service, stamped with IDs that link it to the
           rest of the request's journey

         📖 KEY TERM — Span: the exam-critical distinction is SPAN (one
            timed hop, one service) vs TRACE (the whole request, all
            spans stitched together under one shared traceId). A
            question that asks for "the slowest span" wants the widest
            bar in ONE waterfall — not the 342ms total trace duration.
         - Learn the five fields every span carries and every Jaeger
           screen becomes instantly readable:
           • traceId — shared by ALL spans of one request (the glue)
           • spanId — unique per span; identifies THIS hop only
           • parentSpanId — spanId of whoever called me (builds the tree)
           • duration — start time → end time of this one hop
           • tags — key/value metadata: http.method, http.url, status code
         - The root span has NO parentSpanId — that is how Jaeger knows
           where the call tree starts (jobpost-api in the trace above)

         [SPAN ANATOMY — the skills-service span from the trace above]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  SPAN = one unit of work (one service call)                  │
         │  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
         │  traceId:      7f3e9a12b4c06d8e  ← same on ALL 5 spans       │
         │  spanId:       a1b2c3d4e5f60718  ← unique to THIS span       │
         │  parentSpanId: 9f8e7d6c5b4a3928  ← the jobpost-api span      │
         │  operation:    GET /skills/?ids=1,2,3                        │
         │  startTime:    T=92ms            duration: 195ms  ← SLOW!    │
         │                                                              │
         │  tags:                                                       │
         │    http.method       GET                                     │
         │    http.url          /skills/?ids=1,2,3                      │
         │    http.status_code  200                                     │
         │    component         proxy   ← span created by Envoy        │
         │    upstream_cluster  outbound|8090||skills-service.anihpj   │
         │                                                              │
         │  ROOT SPAN rule: empty parentSpanId → jobpost-api is root   │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    10.2 How Istio Enables Tracing (Almost Automatically)
         - Istio's Envoy injects tracing headers automatically:
           x-request-id, x-b3-traceid, x-b3-spanid, x-b3-parentspanid
         - Your Django code MUST forward these headers between services!
         - Istio does the heavy lifting; you just propagate the headers

         🧠 ANALOGY. Trace headers behave like a relay race baton, not a
            status update. jobpost-api doesn't tell user-service "the
            trace ID is X" — it physically hands over the SAME baton
            (x-b3-traceid and friends), unchanged, to the next runner.
            Drop the baton mid-handoff — swap HTTP client libraries,
            skip one header — and the race doesn't slow down, it just
            STARTS OVER at the next runner: one 5-span trace becomes
            five disconnected 1-span traces (10.5).
         [CODE EXAMPLE: Django middleware to forward Istio tracing headers]

         [REQUIRED: Header propagation in Django views.py]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  # Add this to your Django views that call services:   │
         │                                                        │
         │  ISTIO_HEADERS = [                                     │
         │      'x-request-id',                                   │
         │      'x-b3-traceid',                                   │
         │      'x-b3-spanid',                                    │
         │      'x-b3-parentspanid',                              │
         │      'x-b3-sampled',                                   │
         │      'x-b3-flags',                                     │
         │  ]                                                     │
         │                                                        │
         │  def get_jobs(request):                                │
         │      # Forward headers to propagate trace context:     │
         │      headers = {h: request.META.get(                   │
         │          'HTTP_' + h.upper().replace('-', '_'))        │
         │          for h in ISTIO_HEADERS                        │
         │          if request.META.get(                          │
         │              'HTTP_' + h.upper().replace('-', '_'))    │
         │      }                                                 │
         │      users = requests.get('http://user-service/users/',│
         │                           headers=headers)             │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - Real anihpj scenario: SREs suddenly saw five 1-span traces per
           GET /jobs/ instead of one 5-span chain — user-service had
           swapped its HTTP client library and silently stopped forwarding
           the headers → every hop began a brand-new trace
           → Envoy CREATES spans automatically, but it cannot see INSIDE
             your process — only your code can tie inbound to outbound
         - Rule of thumb: Istio does 80% (span creation, header injection,
           reporting); your Django code does the critical 20% (forwarding)
           — see 10.5 for the full contract and a middleware version

         [BROKEN vs CONNECTED TRACE — same request, two outcomes]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ ❌ HEADERS DROPPED (no propagation)                          │
         │    Jaeger shows FIVE separate traces, one span each:         │
         │    trace 8a01…  jobpost-api       GET /jobs/         342ms   │
         │    trace 3f77…  user-service      GET /users/42/      75ms   │
         │    trace c2b9…  auth-service      POST /validate/     30ms   │
         │    trace 91d4…  skills-service    GET /skills/       195ms   │
         │    trace 6e05…  location-service  GET /locations/7/   25ms   │
         │    → no hierarchy, no bottleneck view, no story              │
         │                                                              │
         │ ✅ HEADERS FORWARDED (10.2 snippet / 10.5 middleware)        │
         │    ONE trace 7f3e9a12…, 5 spans, full Gantt waterfall —      │
         │    the skills-service 195ms bottleneck is instantly visible  │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    10.3 Jaeger — Visualizing Traces
         - Jaeger is the default tracing backend for Istio (demo profile)
         - Open with: istioctl dashboard jaeger
         - Features: trace search, service dependency graph, latency histograms
         - Find the slowest trace: sort by duration → identify bottleneck
         [JAEGER UI MOCKUP with anihpj traces annotated]

         [JAEGER UI MOCKUP — trace search + Gantt waterfall, annotated]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ JAEGER UI ▸ Search                                           │
         │   Service:   jobpost-api.anihpj    Lookback: last 15 min     │
         │   Operation: GET /jobs/            Sort: Longest Duration ▼  │
         │   Tags: (none)                     [ Find Traces ]           │
         ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ ▸ 7f3e9a12b4c06d8e  jobpost-api: GET /jobs/  342ms  5 spans  │
         │                                                              │
         │                          0ms       114ms     228ms  342ms    │
         │ jobpost-api GET /jobs/   ██████████████████████████████ 342ms│
         │  ├ user-service /users/   ███████ 75ms                       │
         │  │  └ auth-svc /validate/ ███ 30ms                           │
         │  ├ skills-service /skills/       ██████████████████ 195ms    │
         │  │                               ^^ WIDEST BAR = BOTTLENECK  │
         │  └ location-service /loc/7/                        ██ 25ms   │
         │                                                              │
         │ Click the widest bar → span detail shows its tags:           │
         │   http.url = /skills/?ids=1,2,3    http.status_code = 200    │
         │   → 200 = slow, NOT failing → suspect the PostgreSQL query   │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - Bottleneck workflow: Search → sort by Longest Duration → open
           the slowest trace → widest bar = bottleneck → click that span
           → read its tags → cross-reference logs at that timestamp
         - Span tags to read first: http.method, http.url,
           http.status_code, component=proxy, upstream_cluster
         - The skills-service bar is wide but returns 200 → slow, not
           failing → next stop is its PostgreSQL query plan (psql:
           EXPLAIN ANALYZE), not its error logs
         - Dependency graph view: Jaeger draws the real anihpj service
           map from traces — compare it with your architecture diagram
           to spot calls you didn't know existed

    10.4 Tracing Sampling Rate
         - By default, Istio traces 1% of requests (to reduce overhead)
         - For development: set to 100% (trace everything)
         - For production: 1-5% is sufficient (100% is too expensive)
         [YAML: Configure sampling rate in Istio Telemetry resource]

         [TELEMETRY YAML — 100% sampling in dev, 1% mesh-wide default]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ # DEV — trace EVERYTHING in the anihpj namespace:            │
         │ apiVersion: telemetry.istio.io/v1                            │
         │ kind: Telemetry                                              │
         │ metadata:                                                    │
         │   name: dev-tracing                                          │
         │   namespace: anihpj            # ← namespace-scoped override │
         │ spec:                                                        │
         │   tracing:                                                   │
         │   - randomSamplingPercentage: 100.0  # ← every request       │
         │ ---                                                          │
         │ # PROD — 1% mesh-wide default (root namespace):              │
         │ apiVersion: telemetry.istio.io/v1                            │
         │ kind: Telemetry                                              │
         │ metadata:                                                    │
         │   name: mesh-default-tracing                                 │
         │   namespace: istio-system      # ← applies to whole mesh     │
         │ spec:                                                        │
         │   tracing:                                                   │
         │   - randomSamplingPercentage: 1.0    # ← 1 in 100 traced     │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - Namespace-scoped Telemetry overrides the istio-system default:
           anihpj traces everything while the rest of the mesh stays at 1%
         - 0% = tracing off: Envoy stamps x-b3-sampled: 0, headers still
           flow, but no spans are reported to Jaeger

         🔧 UNDER THE HOOD: the sampling decision is made ONCE, at the
            FIRST Envoy a request touches (usually the ingress gateway),
            by rolling a random number against randomSamplingPercentage
            and stamping the verdict into x-b3-sampled. Every downstream
            Envoy (user-service, skills-service, ...) just reads and
            honors that same bit instead of re-rolling its own dice —
            this "head-based" design is WHY a trace is always ALL five
            anihpj spans or NONE of them, never a partial trace.
         - Need ONE traced request in prod without touching any config?
           → send x-b3-flags: 1 — the debug flag FORCES sampling for that
             request (and every downstream hop), overriding the
             randomSamplingPercentage

         [FORCE-SAMPLING — x-b3-flags: 1 beats the sampling percentage]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ # trace ONE request in prod without changing any config:     │
         │ kubectl exec deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj -- \               │
         │   curl -s -H "x-b3-flags: 1" \                               │
         │           -H "x-user-id: test-user-42" \                     │
         │           http://skills-service:8090/skills/                 │
         │                                                              │
         │ # x-b3-flags: 1 = debug flag → Envoy ALWAYS samples this     │
         │ # trace, even at randomSamplingPercentage: 1.0 — and the     │
         │ # flag propagates, so every downstream hop is captured too   │
         │ # Debug tool only — never set it fleet-wide in production    │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    10.5  Deep Dive — The B3 Header Propagation Contract
         - DEFINITION: B3 is the trace-context header format (born in
           Zipkin; "B3" = its internal codename "BigBrotherBird") that
           carries trace identity between services as plain HTTP headers
         - Why it matters: a trace survives only if EVERY hop carries the
           same context — the x-b3-* headers ARE that context; drop them
           once and the chain snaps into disconnected spans
         - How it works:
           → the FIRST Envoy in the chain (usually the ingress gateway)
             mints x-b3-traceid and makes the sampling decision
           → every later Envoy creates a child span and UPDATES
             x-b3-spanid / x-b3-parentspanid for its own hop
           → your app's only job: copy the headers from the inbound
             request onto every outbound call, UNCHANGED
         - x-request-id rides along too: not a B3 header, but Envoy's
           per-request UUID — forward it so access logs in every service
           can be joined to the trace afterwards

         [B3 HEADER CONTRACT — the 5 B3 headers + x-request-id]
         ┌────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┬───────────────┐
         │ Header             │ Purpose                  │ Who sets it   │
         ├────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┼───────────────┤
         │ x-b3-traceid       │ 64/128-bit trace ID —    │ first Envoy   │
         │                    │ the glue on ALL spans    │ (gateway)     │
         ├────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┼───────────────┤
         │ x-b3-spanid        │ ID of THIS hop's span    │ every Envoy,  │
         │                    │                          │ each hop      │
         ├────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┼───────────────┤
         │ x-b3-parentspanid  │ spanId of the caller —   │ every Envoy   │
         │                    │ builds the call tree     │               │
         ├────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┼───────────────┤
         │ x-b3-sampled       │ 1 = trace, 0 = skip      │ first Envoy   │
         │                    │ (the sampling verdict)   │               │
         ├────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┼───────────────┤
         │ x-b3-flags         │ 1 = debug — FORCES       │ you, manually │
         │                    │ sampling (beats the %)   │ (curl -H)     │
         ├────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┼───────────────┤
         │ x-request-id       │ Envoy request UUID for   │ first Envoy   │
         │                    │ log-to-trace joins       │               │
         └────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┴───────────────┘

         [DIVISION OF LABOUR — Envoy does 80%, your code does 20%]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  ENVOY SIDECAR — automatic (the 80%)                         │
         │  ✅ creates span context (traceId, spanId, timing)           │
         │  ✅ injects x-b3-* headers into requests                     │
         │  ✅ updates spanid/parentspanid at every hop                 │
         │  ✅ reports finished spans to the tracing backend            │
         │                                                              │
         │  YOUR DJANGO CODE — manual (the critical 20%)                │
         │  □ read x-b3-* + x-request-id from the inbound request       │
         │  □ attach them, UNCHANGED, to every outbound HTTP call       │
         │                                                              │
         │  ❌ skip the 20% → every hop starts a NEW trace:             │
         │     Jaeger shows five 1-span traces instead of one 5-span    │
         │     call chain — the #1 tracing failure in the field         │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - Per-view forwarding (10.2) works, but relies on every
           developer remembering it in every view — the production answer
           is a Django MIDDLEWARE that captures the headers once per
           request, automatically
         - Never generate your own IDs — Envoy owns span creation; your
           code is only the courier

         [DJANGO MIDDLEWARE — automatic B3 propagation for anihpj]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ # anihpj/middleware.py — capture once, use everywhere        │
         │ TRACE_HEADERS = [                                            │
         │     'x-request-id',      'x-b3-traceid',   'x-b3-spanid',    │
         │     'x-b3-parentspanid', 'x-b3-sampled',   'x-b3-flags',     │
         │ ]                                                            │
         │                                                              │
         │ class IstioTracingMiddleware:                                │
         │     def __init__(self, get_response):                        │
         │         self.get_response = get_response                     │
         │                                                              │
         │     def __call__(self, request):                             │
         │         request.trace_headers = {      # ← UNCHANGED copy    │
         │             h: request.META['HTTP_' +                        │
         │                             h.upper().replace('-', '_')]     │
         │             for h in TRACE_HEADERS                           │
         │             if 'HTTP_' + h.upper().replace('-', '_')         │
         │                in request.META                               │
         │         }                                                    │
         │         return self.get_response(request)                    │
         │                                                              │
         │ # settings.py                                                │
         │ MIDDLEWARE = [                                               │
         │     'anihpj.middleware.IstioTracingMiddleware',              │
         │     # ... the rest ...                                       │
         │ ]                                                            │
         │                                                              │
         │ # any views.py — no per-view header plumbing needed:         │
         │ requests.get('http://skills-service:8090/skills/',           │
         │              headers=request.trace_headers)                  │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    10.6  Deep Dive — Tracing Providers: Zipkin, Jaeger, OpenTelemetry
         - DEFINITION: a tracing provider is the backend Envoy ships
           finished spans to; Istio can speak several dialects — Zipkin,
           OpenTelemetry (OTLP), Datadog, and more
         - Why it matters: "Jaeger" in the demo profile is really Envoy
           speaking the ZIPKIN protocol to a Jaeger collector on port
           9411 — knowing which protocol and port are in play is half of
           every "no traces appearing" debug session
         - How it works: declare providers once under meshConfig
           .extensionProviders, then a Telemetry resource selects WHICH
           provider is active (plus its sampling rate) — mesh-wide from
           istio-system or per namespace
         - The industry direction is OpenTelemetry: Envoy sends OTLP to
           one collector, and the collector fans out to Jaeger, Tempo,
           or a vendor APM — swap backends without touching Envoy again

         [MESHCONFIG — extensionProviders + Telemetry selecting one]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ # IstioOperator excerpt (istioctl install -f iop.yaml):      │
         │ meshConfig:                                                  │
         │   extensionProviders:                                        │
         │   - name: jaeger-zipkin                                      │
         │     zipkin:                                                  │
         │       service: zipkin.istio-system.svc.cluster.local         │
         │       port: 9411               # ← Zipkin v2 span API        │
         │   - name: otel                                               │
         │     opentelemetry:                                           │
         │       service: otel-collector.istio-system.svc.cluster.local │
         │       port: 4317               # ← OTLP over gRPC            │
         │ ---                                                          │
         │ # A Telemetry resource picks the ACTIVE provider:            │
         │ apiVersion: telemetry.istio.io/v1                            │
         │ kind: Telemetry                                              │
         │ metadata:                                                    │
         │   name: mesh-tracing                                         │
         │   namespace: istio-system                                    │
         │ spec:                                                        │
         │   tracing:                                                   │
         │   - providers:                                               │
         │     - name: otel               # ← switch backends HERE      │
         │     randomSamplingPercentage: 1.0                            │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [OTEL COLLECTOR PIPELINE — one receiver, many exporters]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  anihpj Envoy sidecars (every namespace, every sidecar pod)  │
         │                        │                                     │
         │                        │ OTLP gRPC :4317                     │
         │                        ▼                                     │
         │         ┌─────────────────────────────────┐                  │
         │         │ otel-collector (istio-system)   │                  │
         │         │   receivers:  [otlp]            │                  │
         │         │   processors: [batch]           │                  │
         │         │   exporters:  [jaeger, tempo]   │                  │
         │         └───────┬─────────────────┬───────┘                  │
         │                 │                 │                          │
         │                 ▼                 ▼                          │
         │         Jaeger (today's UI)   Grafana Tempo / vendor APM     │
         │                                                              │
         │  Swap or add a backend = edit ONLY the collector config —    │
         │  Envoy keeps sending OTLP :4317 to the same address          │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [HEADER FORMATS — B3 (Zipkin) vs W3C traceparent (OTel)]
         ┌───────────────┬───────────────────────┬──────────────────────┐
         │               │ B3 (Zipkin-style)     │ W3C Trace Context    │
         ├───────────────┼───────────────────────┼──────────────────────┤
         │ headers       │ x-b3-traceid,         │ traceparent +        │
         │               │ -spanid,              │ tracestate           │
         │               │ -parentspanid,        │ (2 headers total)    │
         │               │ -sampled, -flags      │                      │
         ├───────────────┼───────────────────────┼──────────────────────┤
         │ format        │ five separate         │ one combined value:  │
         │               │ headers (or the       │ 00-<traceid>-        │
         │               │ compact single "b3")  │ <spanid>-<flags>     │
         ├───────────────┼───────────────────────┼──────────────────────┤
         │ used by       │ classic Zipkin /      │ OTel SDKs and the    │
         │               │ Jaeger path (demo)    │ otel provider        │
         ├───────────────┼───────────────────────┼──────────────────────┤
         │ standard?     │ de-facto (Zipkin)     │ official W3C rec     │
         └───────────────┴───────────────────────┴──────────────────────┘

         - Migration guidance (Zipkin/B3 → OpenTelemetry), the safe order:
           → 1. deploy an OTel collector; add the "otel" provider in
                meshConfig NEXT TO the existing Zipkin one (they coexist)
           → 2. point the collector's exporter at the EXISTING Jaeger —
                same UI, new pipeline; verify traces still assemble
           → 3. flip the Telemetry provider for the anihpj namespace
                first, watch for broken chains, then go mesh-wide
           → 4. teach apps to forward traceparent + tracestate IN
                ADDITION to x-b3-* during the transition; drop B3 only
                after every service and client has switched
         - Gotcha: a mixed mesh where jobpost-api forwards only B3 and
           skills-service forwards only traceparent → the chain snaps at
           that boundary; forwarding BOTH during migration is the fix


    10.7  Deep Dive — Custom Tags & the Telemetry API vs Legacy MeshConfig
         - DEFINITION: Istio has TWO ways to declare "how tracing
           behaves," one legacy and one current — the legacy path is a
           single meshConfig.defaultConfig.tracing block (a hold-over
           from before the Telemetry API existed); the current path is
           meshConfig.extensionProviders (WHO to send spans to) plus a
           Telemetry resource (WHICH provider + WHAT sampling rate)
         - Why it matters: leaving the legacy block populated while ALSO
           adding a Telemetry resource does not "merge" the two — the
           official install docs have you explicitly zero out the legacy
           block (tracing: {}) so there is only ONE source of truth; skip
           that step and anihpj SREs will "fix" sampling in a Telemetry
           resource and see nothing change, because the legacy block is
           still winning
         - How it works:
           → step 1: declare the backend under extensionProviders (10.6)
           → step 2: explicitly empty the legacy block so it cannot
             conflict: defaultConfig.tracing: {}
           → step 3: turn tracing on mesh-wide: enableTracing: true
           → step 4: apply a Telemetry resource that references the
             provider BY NAME and sets the sampling rate

         [DISABLE LEGACY TRACING — the migration step teams skip]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ # IstioOperator excerpt (istioctl install -f iop.yaml):        │
         │ meshConfig:                                                    │
         │   enableTracing: true                                          │
         │   defaultConfig:                                               │
         │     tracing: {}       ← empties the LEGACY sampling path       │
         │   extensionProviders:                                          │
         │   - name: "jaeger"                                             │
         │     opentelemetry:                                             │
         │       service: jaeger-collector.istio-system.svc.cluster.local │
         │       port: 4317                                               │
         │ ---                                                            │
         │ # Telemetry resource is now the ONLY sampling source:          │
         │ apiVersion: telemetry.istio.io/v1                              │
         │ kind: Telemetry                                                │
         │ metadata:                                                      │
         │   name: mesh-default                                           │
         │   namespace: istio-system                                      │
         │ spec:                                                          │
         │   tracing:                                                     │
         │   - providers:                                                 │
         │     - name: "jaeger"                                           │
         │     randomSamplingPercentage: 1.00                             │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - Custom tags: a Telemetry resource can stamp EXTRA key/value
           pairs onto every span anihpj generates — three sources exist,
           and specifying customTags on a namespace/workload resource
           REPLACES the parent's tags entirely (no field-by-field merge)
           • literal — a fixed string, same on every span
           • environment — reads a proxy environment variable (e.g. the
             pod's cluster ID), with an optional fallback defaultValue
           • header — copies a value straight off the inbound request
             (e.g. a caller-supplied user ID), with an optional default

         [CUSTOM TAGS — three sources, one Telemetry resource]
         ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ apiVersion: telemetry.istio.io/v1     │
         │ kind: Telemetry                       │
         │ metadata:                             │
         │   name: anihpj-span-tags              │
         │   namespace: anihpj                   │
         │ spec:                                 │
         │   tracing:                            │
         │   - providers:                        │
         │     - name: "jaeger"                  │
         │     randomSamplingPercentage: 100.00  │
         │     customTags:                       │
         │       "app_version":                  │
         │         literal:                      │
         │           value: "anihpj-v2.4.1"      │
         │       "cluster_id":                   │
         │         environment:                  │
         │           name: ISTIO_META_CLUSTER_ID │
         │           defaultValue: "Kubernetes"  │
         │       "caller_user_id":               │
         │         header:                       │
         │           name: "x-user-id"           │
         │           defaultValue: "anonymous"   │
         └───────────────────────────────────────┘

         [CUSTOM TAG TYPES — source, syntax, anihpj use case]
         ┌─────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┐
         │ Type        │ Reads from                       │ anihpj example                 │
         ├─────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────┤
         │ literal     │ a fixed string in the CRD        │ "app_version": "anihpj-v2.4.1" │
         ├─────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────┤
         │ environment │ a proxy env var + defaultValue   │ ISTIO_META_CLUSTER_ID          │
         ├─────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────┤
         │ header      │ an inbound header + defaultValue │ x-user-id -> "caller_user_id"  │
         └─────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────┘

         - Field length guard: extensionProviders also accepts
           maxTagLength (default 256) to cap how much of a long URL or
           header value gets stamped onto a tag — raise it if anihpj's
           /jobs/?filter=... query strings are getting truncated in Jaeger

    10.8  Deep Dive — W3C Trace Context & the Complete Header Checklist
         - DEFINITION: W3C Trace Context is the vendor-neutral trace
           header standard — two headers, traceparent and tracestate —
           that OpenTelemetry SDKs and Istio's "otel" extension provider
           speak natively, alongside (not instead of) B3
         - Why it matters: 10.5 covered the 5 B3 headers; official Istio
           guidance is that EVERY anihpj service should be ready to
           forward BOTH families at once during any migration — dropping
           either one snaps the trace at that hop, exactly like dropping
           a B3 header does
         - How it works: traceparent packs everything into ONE value —
           version-traceid-parentid-traceflags — where parentid is the
           sender's own span ID (the same role x-b3-spanid plays in B3);
           tracestate carries extra vendor-specific state and is mostly
           opaque to your code — just copy it through unmodified

         [TRACEPARENT ANATOMY — one header, four dash-separated fields]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01 │
         │                                                                      │
         │   00                                ← version (always 00)            │
         │   4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736    ← trace-id (32 hex chars)      │
         │   00f067aa0ba902b7                    ← parent-id (16 hex chars)     │
         │   01                                  ← trace-flags (01 = sampled)   │
         │                                                                      │
         │ tracestate: rojo=00f067aa0ba902b7,congo=t61rcWkgMzE                  │
         │   ← opaque vendor key=value list — forward it UNCHANGED              │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - The COMPLETE list: every header an anihpj service must be
           ready to read on the way in and copy on the way out — this is
           the checklist to paste into a code-review template

         [COMPLETE HEADER PROPAGATION CHECKLIST — B3 + W3C + Envoy]
         ┌───────────────────┬────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┐
         │ Header            │ Family             │ Required for               │
         ├───────────────────┼────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
         │ x-request-id      │ Envoy (own header) │ ALWAYS - every hop         │
         ├───────────────────┼────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
         │ x-b3-traceid      │ B3 multi-header    │ Zipkin/Jaeger backends     │
         ├───────────────────┼────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
         │ x-b3-spanid       │ B3 multi-header    │ Zipkin/Jaeger backends     │
         ├───────────────────┼────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
         │ x-b3-parentspanid │ B3 multi-header    │ Zipkin/Jaeger backends     │
         ├───────────────────┼────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
         │ x-b3-sampled      │ B3 multi-header    │ Zipkin/Jaeger backends     │
         ├───────────────────┼────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
         │ x-b3-flags        │ B3 multi-header    │ Zipkin/Jaeger backends     │
         ├───────────────────┼────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
         │ b3                │ B3 single-header   │ alternative to the 5 above │
         ├───────────────────┼────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
         │ traceparent       │ W3C Trace Context  │ otel provider, OTel SDKs   │
         ├───────────────────┼────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
         │ tracestate        │ W3C Trace Context  │ otel provider, OTel SDKs   │
         └───────────────────┴────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┘

         - During a Zipkin → OpenTelemetry migration (10.6, step 4),
           forward the B3 block AND traceparent/tracestate together —
           only drop B3 once every anihpj service and every client has
           cut over

         [MIDDLEWARE UPGRADE — 10.5's TRACE_HEADERS, now W3C-aware]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ # anihpj/middleware.py — B3 AND W3C, forwarded together    │
         │ TRACE_HEADERS = [                                          │
         │     'x-request-id',                                        │
         │     'x-b3-traceid',   'x-b3-spanid',  'x-b3-parentspanid', │
         │     'x-b3-sampled',   'x-b3-flags',   'b3',                │
         │     'traceparent',    'tracestate',    # ← W3C, added here │
         │ ]                                                          │
         │                                                            │
         │ class IstioTracingMiddleware:                              │
         │     def __init__(self, get_response):                      │
         │         self.get_response = get_response                   │
         │                                                            │
         │     def __call__(self, request):                           │
         │         request.trace_headers = {                          │
         │             h: request.META['HTTP_' +                      │
         │                             h.upper().replace('-', '_')]   │
         │             for h in TRACE_HEADERS                         │
         │             if 'HTTP_' + h.upper().replace('-', '_')       │
         │                in request.META                             │
         │         }                                                  │
         │         return self.get_response(request)                  │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    10.9  Deep Dive — Sampling Precedence & the "Zero Traces" Runbook
         - DEFINITION: sampling percentage can be set in THREE places at
           once — a Telemetry resource, a per-pod annotation, and the
           legacy MeshConfig — and Istio defines an explicit precedence
           order for which one wins when they disagree
         - Why it matters: an anihpj on-call engineer once bumped a
           namespace Telemetry resource to 100% to debug a P1, saw NO
           change, and lost 20 minutes before finding a leftover
           proxy.istio.io/config pod annotation from an old load test —
           the annotation was outranking the Telemetry resource
         - How it works — precedence order (highest wins):
           → 1. Telemetry API (namespace or workload-scoped resource)
           → 2. Pod annotation (proxy.istio.io/config, per-Deployment)
           → 3. MeshConfig defaultConfig.tracing.sampling (legacy/global)
         - Special case: if a custom OpenTelemetry sampler is configured
           on the provider, IT overrides all three of the above, AND
           randomSamplingPercentage is forced to 100 and CANNOT be
           changed — the sampler, not Istio, makes the call

         [SAMPLING PRECEDENCE — three knobs, one winner]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ #1  Telemetry API           (namespace or workload)  ← HIGHEST         │
         │        ↓ overrides #2 and #3                                           │
         │ #2  Pod annotation          (proxy.istio.io/config)                    │
         │        ↓ overrides #3                                                  │
         │ #3  MeshConfig               (defaultConfig.tracing.sampling — legacy) │
         │                                                         ← LOWEST       │
         │                                                                        │
         │ Custom OTel sampler configured on the provider → BEATS ALL THREE,      │
         │ and locks randomSamplingPercentage to 100 (not configurable)           │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [PER-POD OVERRIDE — annotation beats MeshConfig, loses to Telemetry]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ apiVersion: apps/v1                                      │
         │ kind: Deployment                                         │
         │ metadata:                                                │
         │   name: skills-service                                   │
         │   namespace: anihpj                                      │
         │ spec:                                                    │
         │   template:                                              │
         │     metadata:                                            │
         │       annotations:                                       │
         │         proxy.istio.io/config: |                         │
         │           tracing:                                       │
         │             sampling: 20   # ← this Deployment only, 20% │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - The runbook — work top to bottom the moment Jaeger shows zero
           (or too few) anihpj traces:

         [ZERO-TRACES RUNBOOK — symptom → likely cause → fix]
         ┌────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────┐
         │ Symptom                │ Likely cause                     │ Fix                             │
         ├────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┤
         │ No traces at all       │ tracing disabled / no provider   │ enable + wire provider (10.6)   │
         ├────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┤
         │ Traces need 100+ reqs  │ 1% default - working as intended │ raise % for dev only (10.4)     │
         ├────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┤
         │ Raised % but no change │ pod annotation outranks it       │ check proxy.istio.io/config     │
         ├────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┤
         │ Many 1-span traces     │ app not forwarding headers       │ apply 10.8 checklist/middleware │
         ├────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┤
         │ One service missing    │ still points at OLD collector    │ repoint to new service:port     │
         └────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────┘

    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     🔧 UNDER THE HOOD — THE COMPLETE HEADER LIFECYCLE, ONE HOP AT A TIME
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    10.5-10.9 each zoomed into ONE piece of the tracing puzzle — the B3
    contract, providers, custom tags, W3C headers, sampling precedence.
    Here they are stitched into a single walkthrough: the exact header
    lifecycle of the anihpj incident this chapter keeps returning to, as
    ONE request crosses the jobpost-api -> skills-service hop that produced
    the 195ms span. Follow one row at a time — this is the mental model an
    exam-style "why are traces broken" question is actually testing.

    ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ STEP 1 -- jobpost-api INBOUND Envoy (request enters the mesh)         │
    │   reads:  nothing (this IS the first hop)                             │
    │   mints:  x-b3-traceid + the sampling verdict x-b3-sampled (10.9)     │
    │                                                                       │
    │ STEP 2 -- jobpost-api Django, IstioTracingMiddleware (10.5)           │
    │   reads:    every x-b3-*, x-request-id, traceparent/tracestate (10.8) │
    │   forwards: all of it UNCHANGED onto the outbound call -- mints       │
    │             nothing, pure courier                                     │
    │                                                                       │
    │ STEP 3 -- jobpost-api OUTBOUND Envoy (dialing skills-service)         │
    │   reads:    request.trace_headers set in step 2                       │
    │   mints:    new x-b3-spanid; x-b3-parentspanid = its own span id;     │
    │             stamps 10.7 custom tags; translates protocol per the      │
    │             10.6 provider config (e.g. Zipkin -> OTLP)                │
    │   forwards: x-b3-traceid + x-b3-sampled UNCHANGED                     │
    │                                                                       │
    │ STEP 4 -- skills-service INBOUND Envoy (span: 92ms -> 287ms = 195ms)  │
    │   reads:  all headers carried from step 3                             │
    │   mints:  its own span; forwards x-request-id for log-to-trace joins  │
    │                                                                       │
    │ STEP 5 -- Jaeger / OTel backend                                       │
    │   receives the finished spans from steps 3 and 4, stitches them       │
    │   under ONE traceId (7f3e9a12b4c06d8e) -- the 342ms trace from 10.3   │
    └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    The lesson underneath every row: exactly ONE actor in this chain mints
    new IDs at each hop (Envoy), exactly ONE actor is a pure courier with
    zero mint responsibility (your Django code), and the moment step 2
    fails to forward even ONE header, step 3 has nothing correct to mint
    from — which is precisely how a 5-span trace becomes five 1-span traces.

    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     ⚡ SPEED TIPS — TRACING
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    ⚡ Traces missing or arriving as disconnected 1-span fragments? Check
       header propagation (10.5/10.8) BEFORE touching sampling — 100%
       sampling with dropped headers still produces five 1-span traces,
       not the one connected story you need
    ⚡ Raised the sampling % and nothing changed? Per the Zero-Traces
       Runbook, check for a leftover proxy.istio.io/config pod annotation
       first — a stale annotation from an old debug session is the most
       common reason a Telemetry change appears to do nothing (10.9)
    ⚡ Need one traced request in prod without touching any config? Send
       x-b3-flags: 1 — it forces sampling for that request and every
       downstream hop, no YAML required (10.4)
    ⚡ Never leave 100% sampling on in production — it is a dev-only
       setting; 1-5% is the production range this chapter recommends (10.4)
    ⚡ Migrating providers? Forward BOTH B3 and W3C headers during the
       transition (10.6/10.8) — dropping either family snaps the chain at
       whichever service switched first
    ⚡ A 200 status code on the widest span means SLOW, not FAILING — go
       straight to the database query plan, not the error logs (10.3)

    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     🔑 COMMANDS CHEAT-CARD — TRACING
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ istioctl dashboard jaeger                                               │
    │   # opens the Jaeger UI (10.3) -- port-forward handled for you          │
    │                                                                         │
    │ kubectl exec deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj -- \                          │
    │   curl -s -H "x-b3-flags: 1" http://skills-service:8090/skills/         │
    │   # force-samples ONE prod request, bypassing the % (10.4)              │
    │                                                                         │
    │ kubectl apply -f dev-tracing.yaml                                       │
    │   # namespace-scoped Telemetry, e.g. 100% sampling in anihpj (10.4)     │
    │                                                                         │
    │ kubectl get telemetry -A                                                │
    │   # lists every Telemetry resource mesh-wide -- find who set what       │
    │                                                                         │
    │ kubectl get deploy skills-service -n anihpj -o yaml \                   │
    │   | grep -A2 proxy.istio.io/config                                      │
    │   # reveals a pod-annotation sampling override (10.9 runbook)           │
    │                                                                         │
    │ istioctl proxy-config bootstrap deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj -o json \  │
    │   | grep -i trac                                                        │
    │   # confirms which tracing provider/collector Envoy actually has (10.6) │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

     🧪 PRACTICE DRILL — FIND THE 195ms SPAN (5-10 MIN)
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    🧪 Do this now, timed:
       1. (1 min) Run istioctl dashboard jaeger and let it open in your
          browser
       2. (1 min) Search Service: jobpost-api.anihpj, Operation: GET
          /jobs/, Sort: Longest Duration

          Gantt waterfall — confirm it is the ~195ms skills-service span
       4. (2 min) Click that span and read its tags — confirm

     VISUAL SUMMARY — CHAPTER 10 END TO END
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ 1 request: GET /jobs/ -> jobpost-api -> user-service -> auth-service  │
    │                       -> skills-service -> location-service           │
    │         (10.1: trace = the whole journey, span = one timed hop)       │
    │                                  |                                    │
    │                                  ▼                                    │
    │ Envoy auto-creates spans + injects x-b3-* headers (10.2) -- YOUR CODE │
    │ must forward them unchanged, hop to hop (10.5 B3 + 10.8 W3C headers)  │
    │                                  |                                    │
    │                                  ▼                                    │
    │ Jaeger renders the Gantt waterfall (10.3) -- widest bar = the 195ms   │
    │ skills-service span = the bottleneck                                  │
    │                                  |                                    │
    │                                  ▼                                    │
    │ How much of this gets recorded? Sampling (10.4) -- precedence order   │
    │ is Telemetry API > pod annotation > MeshConfig (10.9)                 │
    │                                  |                                    │
    │                                  ▼                                    │
    │ When it breaks: check the provider/protocol (10.6), audit custom      │
    │ tags (10.7), then run the Zero-Traces runbook top to bottom (10.9)    │
    └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    In prose: a single anihpj request generates one span per hop the
    instant Envoy sees it (10.1-10.2); Jaeger turns those spans into a
    Gantt waterfall that makes the 195ms skills-service bottleneck visible
    at a glance (10.3); the sampling rate decides how many requests ever
    reach that waterfall in the first place, with the Telemetry API always
    outranking a pod annotation and both outranking legacy MeshConfig
    (10.4, 10.9); and when any of that silently stops working, the fix is
    almost always a header that stopped propagating, a provider pointed at
    the wrong collector, or a stale override left behind by an old debug
    session (10.5-10.9). Chapter 11 (Kiali) now takes this same incident
    and turns it into a picture you can read in seconds.

Chapter 11: Kiali — Visualizing Your Entire Service Mesh
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Chapter 11 of 9-11 · Difficulty: 🔴 · Tooling for Troubleshooting (20%
    of the ICA exam) — not its own graded domain
    "Forget the numbers and the spans for a second — just show me the
     whole mesh, at a glance."

    WHY THIS MATTERS
         By this point in Part 6, Grafana has already flagged a WHAT
         (skills-service's p99 climbing to 1240ms) and Jaeger has already
         found a WHERE (a 1,100ms PostgreSQL span inside it). Kiali is
         where those two answers finally become ONE picture: run istioctl
         dashboard kiali and the same skills-service incident that took
         two chapters to diagnose lights up as a single red edge on a
         graph of all seven anihpj services. Metrics told you a number
         moved and traces told you which hop it moved on, but only Kiali
         shows you the shape of the whole mesh at once — which services
         are healthy, which edges are failing, and whether a broken
         VirtualService is the cause before you even open a trace. It
         also closes a loop the earlier two chapters could not: Kiali
         validates the live Istio YAML behind every edge, so the same
         graph that shows you a red connection can tell you, on the same
         screen, that a DestinationRule subset typo is why. That is why
         Kiali is the capstone of Part 6, not a third tool bolted onto
         the first two — it is the one screen you actually leave open
         all day.

    LEARNING OBJECTIVES — by the end of Chapter 11 you can:
         ✅ Open the Kiali dashboard with istioctl dashboard kiali and
            read the anihpj service graph's color-coded health at a
            glance (11.1-11.2)
         ✅ Identify a failing edge (jobpost-api -> skills-service) and
            pull its req/s, error %, and p99 without leaving the graph
            (11.2)
         ✅ Explain what Kiali validates — VirtualService, DestinationRule,
            Gateway, AuthorizationPolicy, and more — and how its checks
            differ from istioctl analyze (11.3, 11.8)
         ✅ Use a Kiali wizard to generate a Traffic Shifting, Request
            Routing, Fault Injection, or Request Timeout VirtualService /
            DestinationRule pair without hand-typing YAML (11.4)
         ✅ Walk the four-step Grafana -> Kiali -> Jaeger -> logs debug
            flow on a real incident, in the right order (11.5)
         ✅ Describe the three live sources — Prometheus, the Kubernetes
            API, and Istio config — Kiali merges to build the graph on
            every refresh (11.6)
         ✅ Choose the right install path (sample add-on vs kiali-operator
            vs Helm) and the right graph type (Workload / Versioned App /
            App / Service) for a given task (11.7, 11.9)

    EXAM/ICA RELEVANCE
         🎯 Kiali never appears by name on the ICA blueprint — like the
         rest of Part 6, it is tooling that supports Troubleshooting
         (Domain 4, 20% of the exam), not a graded line item of its own.
         But its Validation feature (11.3, 11.8) is a direct rehearsal
         for the exam's Configuration troubleshooting sub-skill: every
         KIA-coded error you learn to read here is checking the exact
         same VirtualService/DestinationRule/Gateway correctness that
         istioctl analyze checks from the CLI, just with a UI in front of
         it. You likely will not have a browser tab for Kiali on exam
         day, so the real skill being tested is the underlying config
         literacy — a route pointing at a subset that does not exist, a
         Gateway selector matching no workload — which you demonstrate
         with istioctl analyze and kubectl describe instead. Treat
         11.3-11.4 and 11.8 as a visual crash course in the same mistakes
         the exam plants in raw YAML.

    11.1 What is Kiali?
         - Kiali is the "control panel" for your Istio mesh
         - Shows: service topology, real-time traffic flow, config validation
         - Not just a dashboard — it can GENERATE Istio YAML from a UI
         - Open with: istioctl dashboard kiali
         [KIALI DASHBOARD MOCKUP with anihpj service graph]

         - DEFINITION: Kiali is the open-source management console for
           the Istio mesh — it merges Prometheus metrics, Istio config,
           and Kubernetes state into one live, clickable picture
         - Why it matters: "which anihpj service is unhealthy RIGHT NOW?"
           is answered in seconds by looking at colored nodes and edges
         - Kiali stores nothing itself — it is a read-mostly UI over data
           that already exists (deleting Kiali loses no telemetry)
         - The four capabilities you will use daily:
           • Topology   → live service graph built from real traffic
           • Health     → RED metrics per node (service) and edge (call)
           • Validation → catches broken VirtualService/DestinationRule
           • Wizards    → generate correct Istio YAML from the UI

         [KIALI OVERVIEW PAGE — first screen after istioctl dashboard kiali]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  KIALI                                     Namespace: [anihpj ▼]   │
         ├──────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │  ▸ Overview  │  anihpj                                7 services   │
         │  ▸ Graph     │  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
         │  ▸ Apps      │  │  Health:   6 OK   1 failing (skills-service)  │  │
         │  ▸ Workloads │  │  Traffic:  847 req/s      Errors: 2.1%        │  │
         │  ▸ Services  │  │  Config:   ❌ 1 error   ⚠️ 2 warnings         │  │
         │  ▸ Istio     │  └───────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
         │    Config    │  mTLS: 🔒 enabled namespace-wide                    │
         ├──────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │  Open with: istioctl dashboard kiali                               │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    11.3 Validating Istio Configuration
         - Kiali validates your VirtualService and DestinationRule YAML
         - Common errors Kiali detects:
           • VirtualService references a subset not in DestinationRule
           • Gateway references a port not open in the gateway pod
           • Conflicting VirtualService rules
         - Kiali shows errors inline in the YAML editor
         [KIALI VALIDATION SCREENSHOT MOCKUP with error annotations]

         - How it works: Kiali cross-checks every Istio object against
           the live service registry and against every OTHER Istio
           object — most real mistakes are dangling references between
           two objects that are each valid on their own

         🧠 ANALOGY. A VirtualService that still points at a renamed
         subset is like calling a coworker's old desk extension after
         they moved to a new desk: the extension number you dialed is
         still perfectly valid, and the coworker still works at the
         company — the two facts just no longer point at each other.
         Kiali's validation is the office directory that catches the
         mismatch before you pick up the phone and hear silence.
         - Errors show as ❌ in the Istio Config list AND inline next to
           the offending line in Kiali's YAML editor
         - Real anihpj story: a DestinationRule renamed subset "v2" to
           "canary" but the VirtualService still said "v2" → every
           canary request failed → Kiali flagged KIA1107 seconds after
           the apply, long before anyone read a log

         [KIALI CONFIG VALIDATION — three real anihpj errors annotated]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  Istio Config — Namespace: anihpj          ❌ 2 errors ⚠️ 1 warning│
         ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │                                                                    │
         │  ❌ VirtualService/jobpost-api          KIA1107                    │
         │     route[0].destination.subset: "v2"                              │
         │     └─▶ subset not found in any DestinationRule                    │
         │         (DR "jobpost-api" only defines subsets: v1, canary)        │
         │                                                                    │
         │  ❌ Gateway/anihpj-gateway              KIA0302                     │
         │     selector: istio: eastwest-gateway                              │
         │     └─▶ no workload matches this selector in the namespace         │
         │         (anihpj's ingress pods use istio: ingressgateway)          │
         │                                                                    │
         │  ⚠️ VirtualService/jobpost-api-legacy   KIA1106                    │
         │     hosts: ["jobpost-api"]                                         │
         │     └─▶ two VirtualServices define routes for the same host —      │
         │         rules may conflict; merge them into a single VS            │
         │                                                                    │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [KIALI VALIDATION vs ISTIOCTL ANALYZE — pick the right tool]
         ┌──────────────────────┬──────────────────────┬──────────────────────┐
         │  Aspect              │  Kiali Validation    │  istioctl analyze    │
         ├──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┤
         │  Interface           │  Web UI, visual      │  CLI, text output    │
         │  Runs                │  continuously, live  │  on demand           │
         │  Scope               │  all namespaces      │  -n <ns> or -A       │
         │  Offline YAML check  │  ❌ live only        │  ✅ file.yaml        │
         │  CI/CD pipelines     │  ❌ not scriptable   │  ✅ exit code ≠ 0    │
         │  Error detail        │  click for docs      │  IST code + message  │
         │  Best for            │  discovery, triage   │  automation, pre-    │
         │                      │                      │  apply gate          │
         ├──────────────────────┴──────────────────────┴──────────────────────┤
         │  Different code prefixes (KIA1107 vs IST0101) — same class of      │
         │  checks; on the exam run istioctl analyze -n anihpj, then Kiali    │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    11.4 Kiali Wizards — Generate Istio YAML From UI
         - Without writing YAML: use Kiali wizard to create:
           • Traffic Shifting (canary): slide percentage bars
           • Request Routing (A/B test): header-based routing
           • Fault Injection: add delays/aborts via checkbox
           • Request Timeouts: set HTTP timeout & retry policy per route
         - Kiali generates the correct VirtualService + DestinationRule YAML
         [WIZARD FLOW MOCKUP: Kiali UI → generated YAML comparison]

         - Why wizards matter: hand-written canary YAML is the #1 source
           of subset typos — the wizard reads LIVE pod labels, so the
           subsets it generates always match running pods
         - How it works: right-click the service node → Actions → pick a
           wizard → fill the form → Preview shows the exact YAML →
           Create applies it to the cluster
         - DEFINITION: a Kiali wizard is a form that outputs standard
           VirtualService/DestinationRule objects — nothing proprietary;
           kubectl can read, edit, or delete them like any YAML you wrote
         - Update or delete wizard-created rules later from the same
           Actions menu — Kiali labels the objects it manages

         [KIALI WIZARDS — the four wizards and the YAML each generates]
         ┌───────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  Wizard               │  Generated Istio YAML                      │
         ├───────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │  Traffic Shifting     │  VirtualService with weight: fields +      │
         │  (canary %)           │  DestinationRule with one subset per       │
         │                       │  version label found on live pods          │
         ├───────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │  Request Routing      │  VirtualService with match: blocks         │
         │  (A/B by header)      │  (headers/uri) routed to per-version       │
         │                       │  subsets in a DestinationRule              │
         ├───────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │  Fault Injection      │  VirtualService with fault: block —        │
         │  (delay / abort)      │  fixedDelay + percentage, or abort         │
         │                       │  with httpStatus for chaos testing         │
         ├───────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │  Request Timeouts     │  VirtualService with a timeout: field —    │
         │  (HTTP timeout)       │  e.g. timeout: 3s on the route, plus a     │
         │                       │  retries: block (attempts, perTryTimeout)  │
         └───────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────┘
