         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         Read the map as one sentence: Chapter 15 first shows you WHAT to
         configure (local/global rate limits and traffic shaping), then WHY
         it works via token-bucket math and the WasmPlugin/Lua extension
         internals, and finally HOW to wire and govern EnvoyFilter safely so
         a second team's patch doesn't silently collide with yours in
         production.

    15.1 Local Rate Limiting (Per-Pod)
         - Limit how many requests each jobpost-api pod accepts per second
         - Uses Envoy's built-in local rate limiter
         - Applied via EnvoyFilter resource
         - Example: max 100 req/s per pod → protects Django from overload
         [EnvoyFilter YAML for local rate limiting on jobpost-api]

         [ENVOYFILTER YAML — local rate limit 100 req/s on jobpost-api]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3    # EnvoyFilter never    │
         │ kind: EnvoyFilter                           # graduated past alpha │
         │ metadata:                                                          │
         │   name: jobpost-api-local-ratelimit                                │
         │   namespace: anihpj                 # ← lives beside the workload  │
         │ spec:                                                              │
         │   workloadSelector:                                                │
         │     labels:                                                        │
         │       app: jobpost-api              # ← ONLY these pods patched    │
         │   configPatches:                                                   │
         │   - applyTo: HTTP_FILTER            # add to the HTTP filter chain │
         │     match:                                                         │
         │       context: SIDECAR_INBOUND      # ← inbound = protect Django   │
         │       listener:                                                    │
         │         filterChain:                                               │
         │           filter:                                                  │
         │             name: envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager    │
         │     patch:                                                         │
         │       operation: INSERT_BEFORE      # slot in before the router    │
         │       value:                                                       │
         │         name: envoy.filters.http.local_ratelimit                   │
         │         typed_config:                                              │
         │           "@type": type.googleapis.com/udpa.type.v1.TypedStruct    │
         │           # NOTE: type_url is ONE long line in the real file       │
         │           type_url: type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions           │
         │                     .filters.http.local_ratelimit.v3               │
         │                     .LocalRateLimit                                │
         │           value:                                                   │
         │             stat_prefix: http_local_rate_limiter                   │
         │             token_bucket:                                          │
         │               max_tokens: 100       # ← burst ceiling (bucket cap) │
         │               tokens_per_fill: 100  # ← tokens added per refill    │
         │               fill_interval: 1s     # ← refill period → 100 req/s  │
         │             filter_enabled:         # % of traffic EVALUATED       │
         │               default_value:                                       │
         │                 numerator: 100                                     │
         │                 denominator: HUNDRED                               │
         │             filter_enforced:        # % actually LIMITED (429s)    │
         │               default_value:                                       │
         │                 numerator: 100                                     │
         │                 denominator: HUNDRED                               │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - Tuning: change the numbers → kubectl apply; delete the
           EnvoyFilter → the limit disappears instantly (no restart)
         - filter_enabled vs filter_enforced enables a DRY-RUN: evaluate
           100% but enforce 0% → watch would-be 429s in metrics first

         [VERIFY — prove the limiter is live, then trip it]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ $ istioctl proxy-config listener deploy/jobpost-api \        │
         │     -n anihpj -o json | grep local_ratelimit                 │
         │ "name": "envoy.filters.http.local_ratelimit"   ← filter live │
         │                                                              │
         │ $ for i in $(seq 1 150); do \                                │
         │     curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \               │
         │       http://jobpost-api:8000/jobs/; done | sort | uniq -c   │
         │     100 200        ← first 100 grabbed a token               │
         │      50 429        ← bucket empty → rejected by Envoy        │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [LOCAL RATE LIMITING — per-pod bucket diagram]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  LOCAL rate limit: 100 req/s per Pod                              │
         │                                                                    │
         │  jobpost-api has 3 pods:                                           │
         │                                                                    │
         │  [Pod 1]  ┌─────────────────────────┐                             │
         │           │  Token bucket: 100 tok/s │  ← 100 allowed/sec        │
         │           │  ████████░░░░░  82/100   │  ← 82 used this second    │
         │           └─────────────────────────┘                             │
         │                                                                    │
         │  [Pod 2]  ┌─────────────────────────┐                             │
         │           │  Token bucket: 100 tok/s │  ← own independent bucket │
         │           │  ██████████████  100/100 │  ← AT LIMIT → 429 returned│
         │           └─────────────────────────┘                             │
         │                                                                    │
         │  [Pod 3]  ┌─────────────────────────┐                             │
         │           │  Token bucket: 100 tok/s │                             │
         │           │  ███░░░░░░░░░░░  30/100  │  ← 30 used this second    │
         │           └─────────────────────────┘                             │
         │                                                                    │
         │  Total capacity: 3 pods × 100 = 300 req/s                         │
         │  Pod 2 hit its limit → returns 429 Too Many Requests               │
         │  (Other pods still serving — local limit, not global!)            │
         │                                                                    │
         │  EnvoyFilter YAML (simplified):                                    │
         │  spec:                                                             │
         │    configPatches:                                                  │
         │    - applyTo: HTTP_FILTER                                         │
         │      match: {context: SIDECAR_INBOUND}                            │
         │      patch:                                                        │
         │        value:                                                      │
         │          typed_config:                                             │
         │            maxTokens: 100                                          │
         │            tokensPerFill: 100                                      │
         │            fillInterval: 1s                                       │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    15.2 Global Rate Limiting (Shared Counter)
         - Rate limit by source IP, user, API key across ALL pods combined
         - Requires a rate limit service (e.g., Redis-backed rate limiter)
         - Example: limit each unique IP to 1000 requests/minute to /jobs/
         [ARCHITECTURE DIAGRAM: Envoy → rate limit service → Redis]

         [GLOBAL RATE LIMITING — architecture for anihpj]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │                                                                    │
         │  Request from IP 203.0.113.42 → jobpost-api                       │
         │                                                                    │
         │  [jobpost-api Pod] ──▶ Envoy sidecar                              │
         │                              │                                     │
         │                    "Check rate limit for this IP"                 │
         │                              │  gRPC check                        │
         │                              ▼                                     │
         │                  [Rate Limit Service]  ← deployed separately      │
         │                              │  "Has IP 203... exceeded limit?"   │
         │                              ▼                                     │
         │                      [Redis Cache]                                 │
         │                      IP: 203.0.113.42                              │
         │                      count: 987/1000  ← under limit ✅             │
         │                              │                                     │
         │                    Response: "ALLOWED" + remaining: 13            │
         │                              │                                     │
         │                              ▼                                     │
         │               Request forwarded to Django ✅                       │
         │                                                                    │
         │  REQUEST 1001 from same IP:                                        │
         │  Redis: count: 1001/1000 → RATE_LIMITED!                          │
         │  Envoy returns: 429 Too Many Requests  ❌                          │
         │  Retry-After: 60s header added                                     │
         │                                                                    │
         │  GLOBAL vs LOCAL comparison:                                       │
         │  Local:  each pod has its own counter (3 pods = 300 req/s total)  │
         │  Global: ALL pods share ONE counter (3 pods = 1000 req/min TOTAL) │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - When do I ACTUALLY need global limiting? Decision note:
           • the limit describes a CLIENT ("each IP: 1000 req/min",
             "free tier: 100 calls/day") → it must hold across ALL
             pods at once → GLOBAL is the only correct answer
           • the limit protects one POD's capacity ("a Django worker
             melts past 100 req/s") → LOCAL is enough — and simpler
           • HPA changes pod count → LOCAL totals drift silently
             (3 pods = 300 req/s; autoscaled to 6 pods = 600 req/s)
             → if the business number must stay fixed, go GLOBAL
           • can't run Redis + an extra deployment? → stay LOCAL

         [GLOBAL vs LOCAL — quick decision table for anihpj]
         ┌────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┐
         │ Situation                      │ Pick                      │
         ├────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┤
         │ Protect Django pods from melt  │ LOCAL  (per-pod bucket)   │
         │ "1000 req/min per source IP"   │ GLOBAL (shared counter)   │
         │ Free vs paid API-key quotas    │ GLOBAL (per-key counter)  │
         │ Quick guardrail, zero infra    │ LOCAL                     │
         │ Exact org-wide request budget  │ GLOBAL                    │
         └────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┘

         - Redis sizing: each active limit key (one per unique IP /
           user / API key in the current window) is a tiny counter
           with a TTL — budget ~100 bytes per key; 1,000,000 live
           client IPs ≈ ~100 MB, so one small Redis (256 MB) covers
           anihpj with headroom; also budget the ~1-5ms gRPC check
           per request into your p99 (234ms today) before enabling

         🧠 ANALOGY. Local vs. global rate limiting is like a bank's
            ATMs. A LOCAL limit is each ATM keeping its own $300 cash
            drawer — fast, but three ATMs quietly add up to $900 of
            exposure the bank never sees as one number. A GLOBAL limit
            is one shared ledger every ATM checks before it dispenses a
            dollar — a phone call to the vault adds a beat of latency,
            but the $1000 daily cap holds no matter how many ATMs
            (jobpost-api pods) are open. anihpj's Redis-backed RLS IS
            that vault.

    15.3 Traffic Shaping — Controlling Latency
         - Add deliberate delays to slow down specific clients or paths
         - Use to enforce SLAs: "background batch jobs get max 10 req/s"
         - vs regular user traffic gets full speed

         [TRAFFIC SHAPING — priority lanes for anihpj requests]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  PROBLEM: Background job scraper hitting /jobs/ exhausts resources │
         │                                                                    │
         │  SOLUTION: Distinguish traffic by header, apply different limits   │
         │                                                                    │
         │  Regular user request:         Batch/scraper request:             │
         │  Header: x-client: browser     Header: x-client: batch-job        │
         │          │                             │                           │
         │          ▼                             ▼                           │
         │  ┌──────────────┐           ┌──────────────────────┐              │
         │  │ No rate limit │           │ EnvoyFilter: add 100ms│             │
         │  │ full speed   │           │ delay per request    │             │
         │  │ 0ms overhead │           │ + max 10 req/s       │             │
         │  └──────────────┘           └──────────────────────┘              │
         │                                                                    │
         │  Result: batch jobs work but can't starve real users ✅            │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - How the 100ms brake is actually built: match the header in
           a VirtualService and reuse fault-injection delay as a
           shaping tool (delay applies BEFORE the request hits Django)

         🔧 Under the hood: the 100ms fixedDelay doesn't block a worker
            thread to wait it out — Envoy's fault filter parks the
            request as a timer callback on its event loop and resumes
            it when the timer fires, so ten held-open batch-job
            requests cost ten timers, not ten blocked threads. That's
            the opposite of the risk 15.5's WASM vs LUA table flags for
            a bad Lua script, which CAN stall a worker thread — a
            declarative fault.delay never does.

         [SHAPING YAML — slow lane for batch traffic (VirtualService)]
         ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1                            │
         │ kind: VirtualService                                          │
         │ metadata:                                                     │
         │   name: jobpost-api-shaping                                   │
         │   namespace: anihpj                                           │
         │ spec:                                                         │
         │   hosts: ["jobpost-api"]                                      │
         │   http:                                                       │
         │   - match:                          # LANE 1: the slow lane   │
         │     - headers:                                                │
         │         x-client:                                             │
         │           exact: batch-job          # ← scrapers / batch jobs │
         │     fault:                                                    │
         │       delay:                                                  │
         │         percentage: {value: 100}                              │
         │         fixedDelay: 100ms           # ← the 100ms brake       │
         │     route:                                                    │
         │     - destination: {host: jobpost-api}                        │
         │   - route:                          # LANE 2: everyone else   │
         │     - destination: {host: jobpost-api}    # full speed, 0ms   │
         └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - Pair the slow lane with a local rate limit EnvoyFilter that
           matches the same header to enforce the "max 10 req/s" half

    15.4  Deep Dive — Token Bucket Algorithm Explained
         - DEFINITION: a token bucket is a jar of "permission slips"
           (tokens); every request must grab one token to pass — an
           empty jar means Envoy answers 429 on the spot and Django is
           never called
         - Why it matters: the three knobs (maxTokens, tokensPerFill,
           fillInterval) are the ONLY rate-limit math the exam tests —
           misread fillInterval: 60s as 1s and your "100 req/s" limit
           silently becomes 100 req/MINUTE
         - How it works:
           • fillInterval fires like a metronome → adds tokensPerFill
             tokens, capped at maxTokens (the bucket never overflows)
           • each arriving request consumes exactly 1 token → forwarded
           • bucket empty → instant 429 Too Many Requests, ~0ms cost
         - The two derived numbers to memorize:
           • sustained rate = tokensPerFill ÷ fillInterval
             → 100 ÷ 1s = 100 req/s for each jobpost-api pod
           • burst ceiling = maxTokens → a full, idle bucket can drain
             all at once, absorbing a one-off spike of that size

         [TOKEN BUCKET — millisecond walkthrough at 100 tok/s]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ CONFIG: maxTokens: 100  tokensPerFill: 100  fillInterval: 1s   │
         │                                                                │
         │ T=0ms:      bucket FULL   [██████████] 100/100 tokens          │
         │ T=0-300ms:  burst — 100 requests land, each takes 1 token      │
         │ T=300ms:    bucket EMPTY  [░░░░░░░░░░]   0/100                 │
         │ T=310ms:    request #101 → no token → 429 (Envoy rejects)      │
         │ T=310-999:  every further request → 429, Django untouched      │
         │ T=1000ms:   refill tick: +100 tokens, capped at 100 → FULL     │
         │ T=1001ms:   traffic flows again ✓                              │
         │                                                                │
         │ BURST TUNING (same 100 req/s sustained, different spikes):     │
         │   maxTokens: 100, tokensPerFill: 100 → burst 100, steady 100/s │
         │   maxTokens: 300, tokensPerFill: 100 → burst 300 after a few   │
         │     quiet seconds (bucket saves up), still 100/s average       │
         │   rule: maxTokens = tokensPerFill  → uniform traffic           │
         │         maxTokens > tokensPerFill  → spiky browser traffic     │
         │                                                                │
         │ LOCAL vs GLOBAL MATH (identical YAML, different totals):       │
         │   LOCAL on 3 jobpost-api pods: 3 × 100 = 300 req/s effective   │
         │   HPA scales to 6 pods → silently becomes 600 req/s!           │
         │   GLOBAL: 100 req/s TOTAL, no matter how many pods exist       │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    15.5  Deep Dive — Extending Envoy: WasmPlugin vs Lua EnvoyFilter
         - DEFINITION: when no built-in CRD (VirtualService,
           AuthorizationPolicy, Telemetry) can express your logic, Istio
           lets you run YOUR OWN CODE inside the sidecar — through
           exactly two doors:
           • WasmPlugin CRD (extensions.istio.io/v1alpha1) — loads a
             compiled WebAssembly module into Envoy's sandboxed VM
           • Lua script via EnvoyFilter — injects a small interpreted
             function straight into the HTTP filter chain
         - Why it matters: custom auth token formats, bespoke request
           tagging, odd legacy protocols — real meshes hit these; the
           exam expects you to know WHICH mechanism fits and what each
           one risks
         - How they ship: istiod distributes both; the Wasm module is
           pulled from an OCI registry by istio-agent (like a container
           image), while the Lua source travels inline inside the
           EnvoyFilter YAML itself
         - ⚠️ Extensions run on EVERY matching request — exhaust the
           built-in CRDs first; custom code is yours to debug at 3am

         [WASMPLUGIN — annotated YAML (the REAL extension CRD)]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ apiVersion: extensions.istio.io/v1alpha1    # ← WasmPlugin's home  │
         │ kind: WasmPlugin                                                   │
         │ metadata:                                                          │
         │   name: jobpost-header-guard                                       │
         │   namespace: anihpj              # plugin scoped to anihpj ns      │
         │ spec:                                                              │
         │   selector:                                                        │
         │     matchLabels:                                                   │
         │       app: jobpost-api           # ← attach to these sidecars      │
         │   url: oci://registry.anihpj.dev/wasm/header-guard:v1.2.0          │
         │                                  # ← module pulled like an image   │
         │   sha256: 4f2a91c0...            # ← pin the binary (supply chain) │
         │   imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent                                    │
         │   phase: AUTHN                   # ← where in the filter chain:    │
         │                                  #   AUTHN = before Istio authn    │
         │                                  #   AUTHZ = before Istio authz    │
         │                                  #   STATS = after authz (metrics) │
         │   priority: 10                   # higher runs earlier in a phase  │
         │   failStrategy: FAIL_CLOSE       # plugin crash → block traffic    │
         │                                  # (FAIL_OPEN = let traffic pass)  │
         │   pluginConfig:                  # ← handed to the module as JSON  │
         │     header: x-anihpj-guard                                         │
         │     value: "checked"                                               │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [LUA ENVOYFILTER — inline script tagging anihpj requests]
         ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3                          │
         │ kind: EnvoyFilter                                                 │
         │ metadata:                                                         │
         │   name: jobpost-lua-tag                                           │
         │   namespace: anihpj                                               │
         │ spec:                                                             │
         │   workloadSelector:                                               │
         │     labels:                                                       │
         │       app: jobpost-api                                            │
         │   configPatches:                                                  │
         │   - applyTo: HTTP_FILTER                                          │
         │     match:                                                        │
         │       context: SIDECAR_INBOUND                                    │
         │       listener:                                                   │
         │         filterChain:                                              │
         │           filter:                                                 │
         │             name: envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager   │
         │             subFilter:                                            │
         │               name: envoy.filters.http.router                     │
         │     patch:                                                        │
         │       operation: INSERT_BEFORE      # run before the router       │
         │       value:                                                      │
         │         name: envoy.lua                                           │
         │         typed_config:                                             │
         │           # NOTE: "@type" is ONE long line in the real file       │
         │           "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions           │
         │                    .filters.http.lua.v3.Lua                       │
         │           inline_code: |            # ← the WHOLE program is here │
         │             function envoy_on_request(handle)                     │
         │               handle:headers():add("x-anihpj-lua", "seen")        │
         │             end                                                   │
         │             function envoy_on_response(handle)                    │
         │               handle:headers():add("x-served-by", "anihpj-mesh")  │
         │             end                                                   │
         └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [WASM vs LUA — choosing your Envoy extension mechanism]
         ┌─────────────┬───────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┐
         │ Dimension   │ WasmPlugin (Wasm module)  │ Lua EnvoyFilter          │
         ├─────────────┼───────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┤
         │ Language    │ Rust, Go, C++, Assembly-  │ Lua only, inline in      │
         │             │ Script → compiled .wasm   │ the YAML resource        │
         ├─────────────┼───────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┤
         │ Safety      │ sandboxed VM — a crash is │ runs in Envoy's own      │
         │             │ contained; failStrategy   │ process — a bad script   │
         │             │ FAIL_CLOSE / FAIL_OPEN    │ stalls worker threads    │
         ├─────────────┼───────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┤
         │ Performance │ near-native; small VM     │ interpreted; fine for    │
         │             │ overhead per request      │ tiny header tweaks       │
         ├─────────────┼───────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┤
         │ Hot-reload  │ push new oci:// tag +     │ edit inline_code →       │
         │             │ sha256 → agent re-pulls,  │ istiod pushes new        │
         │             │ no pod restart            │ config, no restart       │
         ├─────────────┼───────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┤
         │ Best for    │ real logic: tests, CI/CD, │ one-line tweaks and      │
         │             │ versions, reuse across    │ temporary workarounds    │
         │             │ teams and clusters        │ you may delete soon      │
         └─────────────┴───────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┘

         - Rule of thumb for anihpj: Lua for a one-line header tweak
           you might delete next sprint; WasmPlugin for anything with
           real logic, tests, or versions — or that must NOT be able
           to crash the proxy (failStrategy: FAIL_CLOSE contains it)

         [VERIFY — is the Wasm module actually loaded?]
         ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ $ kubectl get wasmplugins -n anihpj                         │
         │ NAME                   AGE                                  │
         │ jobpost-header-guard   2m           ← CRD accepted          │
         │                                                             │
         │ $ istioctl proxy-config listener deploy/jobpost-api \       │
         │     -n anihpj -o json | grep -i wasm                        │
         │ "name": "envoy.filters.http.wasm"   ← module live in Envoy  │
         │                                                             │
         │ $ curl -sI http://jobpost-api:8000/jobs/ | grep x-anihpj    │
         │ x-anihpj-guard: checked             ← plugin ran on request │
         └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘


    15.6  Deep Dive — EnvoyFilter's Patch Grammar: applyTo, Context, and Operation
         - DEFINITION: every configPatches entry in an EnvoyFilter is exactly
           one triple — WHERE to patch (applyTo), WHEN it applies
           (match.context), and HOW to edit it (patch.operation) — plus a
           value: payload; nothing about EnvoyFilter is more complicated
           than reading this triple correctly

         📖 KEY TERM — THE PATCH TRIPLE: applyTo = WHERE (HTTP_FILTER,
            CLUSTER...), match.context = WHEN (SIDECAR_INBOUND,
            SIDECAR_OUTBOUND, GATEWAY), patch.operation = HOW
            (INSERT_BEFORE, MERGE...). Every EnvoyFilter in this chapter
            is just this triple wearing a different value: payload.
         - Why it matters: 15.1's local-ratelimit filter and 15.5's Lua
           tagger both use the IDENTICAL triple (HTTP_FILTER +
           SIDECAR_INBOUND + INSERT_BEFORE) — the exam swaps ONE of these
           three knobs per question to test whether you understand what
           each knob controls, not just that "EnvoyFilter does something"
         - How it works — the WHERE (applyTo picks the xDS resource type
           Envoy is about to receive):

         [THE PATCH TRIPLE — mapping ch15's own two filters to the triple]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │THE PATCH TRIPLE — every EnvoyFilter patch = WHERE + WHEN + HOW     │
         │                                                                    │
         │15.1 local rate limiter (from earlier in this chapter):             │
         │  WHERE (applyTo):   HTTP_FILTER      → HTTP filter chain in the HCM│
         │  WHEN  (context):   SIDECAR_INBOUND  → only traffic inbound to pod │
         │  HOW   (operation): INSERT_BEFORE    → slot in just before router  │
         │                                                                    │
         │15.5 Lua request tagger (from earlier in this chapter):             │
         │  WHERE (applyTo):   HTTP_FILTER      → same target as above        │
         │  WHEN  (context):   SIDECAR_INBOUND  → same direction: inbound     │
         │  HOW   (operation): INSERT_BEFORE    → same verb: before router    │
         │                                                                    │
         │Same triple, different payload (value:) — that IS EnvoyFilter: the  │
         │triple finds the slot, value: fills it in with your custom filter.  │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [APPLYTO — the WHERE, full enum from the EnvoyFilter reference]
         ┌─────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ Value               │ What it patches (official summary)           │
         ├─────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ LISTENER            │ a listener (add or replace one)              │
         │ FILTER_CHAIN        │ a filter chain inside a listener             │
         │ NETWORK_FILTER      │ an L4 filter, e.g. TCP proxy                 │
         │ HTTP_FILTER         │ an HTTP filter inside the HCM's chain        │
         │ ROUTE_CONFIGURATION │ the RDS route config (MERGE-only op)         │
         │ VIRTUAL_HOST        │ a virtual host in a route config             │
         │ HTTP_ROUTE          │ one route inside a matched virtual host      │
         │ CLUSTER             │ a CDS cluster; also used to ADD new ones     │
         │ EXTENSION_CONFIG    │ a named ECDS extension-config resource       │
         │ LISTENER_FILTER     │ a listener filter (runs pre filter chain)    │
         │ BOOTSTRAP           │ DEPRECATED — patches bootstrap directly      │
         └─────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - the WHEN (match.context restricts by proxy type / traffic
           direction) and the HOW (patch.operation picks the edit verb):

         [PATCHCONTEXT — the WHEN]
         ┌───────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ Value             │ Matches traffic on                             │
         ├───────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ ANY               │ every context: inbound, outbound, gateway      │
         │ SIDECAR_INBOUND   │ a sidecar's inbound listener only              │
         │ SIDECAR_OUTBOUND  │ a sidecar's outbound listener only             │
         │ GATEWAY           │ an ingress/egress Gateway proxy only           │
         └───────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [PATCH.OPERATION — the HOW]
         ┌────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ Value          │ What it does                                      │
         ├────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ ADD            │ append to the end of a list                       │
         │ REMOVE         │ delete the matched object                         │
         │ INSERT_BEFORE  │ insert immediately before the matched filter      │
         │ INSERT_AFTER   │ insert immediately after the matched filter       │
         │ INSERT_FIRST   │ insert as the very first filter in the list       │
         │ REPLACE        │ swap a named filter's contents (HTTP/NETWORK      │
         │                │ filter only)                                      │
         │ MERGE          │ deep-merge fields into the existing object        │
         └────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - Two exam traps baked into this grammar: REPLACE is legal ONLY on
           HTTP_FILTER and NETWORK_FILTER (it swaps a NAMED filter's
           contents wholesale); ROUTE_CONFIGURATION accepts ONLY MERGE —
           pick REPLACE or an INSERT_* there and Istio rejects the config
         - Full governance treatment — including WHICH patch wins when two
           EnvoyFilters both match the same workload, and istio.io's
           official "use with care" warning — is in 15.9

    15.7  The Global Rate Limiting EnvoyFilter — Wiring Up envoy.filters.http.ratelimit
         - 15.2 covered the ARCHITECTURE of global rate limiting; this
           section shows the actual EnvoyFilter YAML that wires
           envoy.filters.http.ratelimit into jobpost-api's chain — the
           exam can and does ask you to spot a broken field name in
           exactly this YAML
         - Why it matters: global rate limiting always needs TWO EnvoyFilter
           patches, not one — an HTTP_FILTER patch that inserts the filter
           into the chain, and a VIRTUAL_HOST (or HTTP_ROUTE) patch that
           attaches rate_limits actions telling Envoy WHAT to send the RLS
           server as a "descriptor" (source IP? a header? both?)
         - How it works — patch #1, insert the filter:

         [GLOBAL RATELIMIT — patch 1 of 2: insert envoy.filters.http.ratelimit]
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3                                            │
         │kind: EnvoyFilter                                                                   │
         │metadata:                                                                           │
         │  name: jobpost-global-ratelimit-filter                                             │
         │  namespace: anihpj                                                                 │
         │spec:                                                                               │
         │  workloadSelector:                                                                 │
         │    labels:                                                                         │
         │      app: jobpost-api        → patched onto jobpost-api's sidecar only             │
         │  configPatches:                                                                    │
         │  - applyTo: HTTP_FILTER        # add the ratelimit filter to the HTTP chain        │
         │    match:                                                                          │
         │      context: SIDECAR_INBOUND                                                      │
         │      listener:                                                                     │
         │        filterChain:                                                                │
         │          filter:                                                                   │
         │            name: envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager                     │
         │    patch:                                                                          │
         │      operation: INSERT_BEFORE   # ahead of the router, same as local limit         │
         │      value:                                                                        │
         │        name: envoy.filters.http.ratelimit   ← the GLOBAL filter name               │
         │        typed_config:                                                               │
         │          "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters                     │
         │                    .http.ratelimit.v3.RateLimit                                    │
         │          domain: anihpj-jobpost          ← namespaces the descriptors              │
         │          failure_mode_deny: true         # RLS unreachable → reject                │
         │                                           # (fail-closed; false=fail-open)         │
         │          timeout: 0.25s                  # budget inside your p99 latency          │
         │          rate_limit_service:                                                       │
         │            grpc_service:                                                           │
         │              envoy_grpc:                                                           │
         │                cluster_name: outbound|8081||ratelimit.anihpj.svc.cluster.local     │
         │            transport_api_version: V3                                               │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - patch #2: what actually gets rate-limited — the actions build
           the descriptor Envoy sends to the RLS server on every request:

         [GLOBAL RATELIMIT — patch 2 of 2: attach rate_limits actions]
         ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3                                       │
         │kind: EnvoyFilter                                                              │
         │metadata:                                                                      │
         │  name: jobpost-global-ratelimit-route                                         │
         │  namespace: anihpj                                                            │
         │spec:                                                                          │
         │  workloadSelector:                                                            │
         │    labels: {app: jobpost-api}                                                 │
         │  configPatches:                                                               │
         │  - applyTo: VIRTUAL_HOST        # attach the rate_limits ACTION here          │
         │    match:                                                                     │
         │      context: SIDECAR_INBOUND                                                 │
         │      routeConfiguration:                                                      │
         │        vhost:                                                                 │
         │          name: "jobpost-api.anihpj.svc.cluster.local:8000"                    │
         │          route: {name: default}                                               │
         │    patch:                                                                     │
         │      operation: MERGE            # VIRTUAL_HOST only supports MERGE           │
         │      value:                                                                   │
         │        rate_limits:                                                           │
         │        - actions:                # each action builds one descriptor          │
         │          - remote_address: {}    # key = the client's source IP               │
         │          - request_headers:                                                   │
         │              header_name: "x-api-key"                                         │
         │              descriptor_key: "API_KEY"  ← per-key quota, not just IP          │
         └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - the RLS server's OWN config — Istio does not ship a rate-limit
           server; this is server-side config for whatever gRPC RLS
           implementation you deploy (e.g. envoyproxy/ratelimit), NOT an
           Istio CRD:

         [RLS SERVER CONFIG — domain/descriptors, mounted into the RLS deployment]
         ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │# ratelimit-server configuration (mounted into the RLS deployment as a         │
         │# ConfigMap — this is server-side config, NOT an Istio CRD)                    │
         │                                                                               │
         │domain: anihpj-jobpost         # must match the EnvoyFilter's domain: above    │
         │descriptors:                                                                   │
         │- key: remote_address                 # matches the remote_address action      │
         │  rate_limit:                                                                  │
         │    unit: minute                                                               │
         │    requests_per_unit: 1000            # 1000 req/min PER SOURCE IP            │
         │- key: API_KEY                        # matches the request_headers action     │
         │  rate_limit:                                                                  │
         │    unit: day                                                                  │
         │    requests_per_unit: 100000          # free-tier daily quota per key         │
         └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - failure_mode_deny is the field to watch on the exam: true = RLS
           unreachable → reject traffic (fail-closed, safe but can cause
           an outage if the RLS pod dies); false = fail-open (traffic
           flows unlimited if RLS is down) — anihpj's choice depends on
           whether the limit protects a paying customer's quota
           (fail-closed) or is just a soft guardrail (fail-open)

         [LOCAL vs GLOBAL EnvoyFilter — the two filters side by side]
         ┌───────────────┬───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┐
         │ Dimension     │ LOCAL (15.1)                  │ GLOBAL (this section)         │
         ├───────────────┼───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┤
         │ Filter name   │ ...http.local_ratelimit       │ ...http.ratelimit             │
         │ State         │ in-process token bucket       │ external RLS + Redis/store    │
         │ applyTo used  │ HTTP_FILTER only              │ HTTP_FILTER + VIRTUAL_HOST    │
         │ Extra infra   │ none                          │ RLS deployment + backing store│
         │ Scope         │ per pod                       │ whole mesh, one counter       │
         │ Extra hop     │ ~0ms (in-process)             │ ~1-5ms gRPC check per request │
         └───────────────┴───────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┘

    15.8  Deep Dive — WasmPlugin's Full CRD Field Reference & Module Distribution
         - DEFINITION: 15.5 introduced WasmPlugin with the fields you'll
           touch most (selector, url, sha256, phase, priority,
           failStrategy, pluginConfig); this section completes the picture
           with every remaining field the CRD defines, plus exactly how a
           Wasm module physically gets from your laptop into Envoy's
           sandboxed VM
         - Why it matters: the exam's WasmPlugin questions increasingly
           probe the fields 15.5 didn't cover — targetRefs (Gateway
           API-style targeting), the url scheme defaulting rules, and the
           imagePullPolicy/sha256 interaction — because these are the
           fields people get wrong in real clusters

         [WASMPLUGIN — the complete field reference]
         ┌──────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ Field            │ What it does (official reference)                                     │
         ├──────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ selector         │ WorkloadSelector: label-match which pods get the plugin               │
         │ targetRefs       │ Gateway-API-style alternative to selector; targets a                  │
         │                  │ named Gateway/ServiceEntry-like resource instead of labels            │
         │ url              │ Wasm module or OCI image location; no scheme given                    │
         │                  │ defaults to oci://; also supports file:// and http(s)://              │
         │ sha256           │ checksum verifying the Wasm module/OCI image (supply chain)           │
         │ imagePullPolicy  │ IfNotPresent or Always; unspecified = IfNotPresent, BUT a             │
         │                  │ :latest tag forces Always; sha256 set forces IfNotPresent             │
         │ imagePullSecret  │ credentials (Secret name) for pulling from a private OCI              │
         │                  │ registry                                                              │
         │ pluginConfig     │ arbitrary Struct (JSON) handed to the module at load time             │
         │ pluginName       │ name used inside Envoy config; was called rootID before               │
         │ phase            │ PluginPhase: UNSPECIFIED_PHASE, AUTHN, AUTHZ, or STATS                │
         │ priority         │ int32; same-phase plugins run in DESCENDING priority order            │
         │ failStrategy     │ FAIL_CLOSE (5xx on crash), FAIL_OPEN (bypass plugin), or              │
         │                  │ FAIL_RELOAD (spin up a fresh instance per request)                    │
         │ vmConfig         │ Wasm VM env vars / runtime settings (e.g. v8 vs wasmtime)             │
         │ match            │ TrafficSelector[]; restricts which requests reach the plugin          │
         │ type             │ PluginType of the Wasm extension (defaults to HTTP)                   │
         └──────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - targetRefs vs selector: pick exactly ONE. selector label-matches
           ordinary sidecar workloads (jobpost-api); targetRefs is the
           Gateway-API-style pointer used when the plugin belongs to a
           Gateway or other named resource, not a labeled Pod:

         [WASMPLUGIN — targetRefs example, an alternative to selector]
         ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │apiVersion: extensions.istio.io/v1alpha1                                     │
         │kind: WasmPlugin                                                             │
         │metadata:                                                                    │
         │  name: anihpj-gateway-header-guard                                          │
         │  namespace: anihpj                                                          │
         │spec:                                                                        │
         │  targetRefs:                    # ← Gateway-API style, an alt to selector   │
         │  - kind: Gateway                # ← attach straight to a named Gateway      │
         │    group: gateway.networking.k8s.io                                         │
         │    name: anihpj-ingress                                                     │
         │  url: oci://registry.anihpj.dev/wasm/header-guard:v1.2.0                    │
         │  sha256: 4f2a91c0...                                                        │
         │  phase: AUTHN                                                               │
         │  pluginConfig:                                                              │
         │    header: x-anihpj-guard                                                   │
         │    value: "checked"                                                         │
         │                                                                             │
         │NOTE: use targetRefs when the plugin belongs to a Gateway/waypoint           │
         │resource, not a labeled workload; use selector (15.5) for ordinary           │
         │sidecars like jobpost-api. Only one of selector/targetRefs is set.           │
         └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - Wasm module distribution — this is OCI-native: the SAME
           container registry and the SAME pull-policy mental model as a
           Deployment's image:, except istio-agent (not Envoy itself) is
           what fetches it:

         [WASM MODULE DISTRIBUTION — push once, reference everywhere]
         ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │WASM MODULE DISTRIBUTION — push once, reference everywhere             │
         │                                                                       │
         │1. Build   header-guard.wasm  (Rust/Go/C++/AssemblyScript → compiled)  │
         │                                                                       │
         │2. Push to an OCI registry → SAME registry you already use for         │
         │   container images:                                                   │
         │   $ oras push registry.anihpj.dev/wasm/header-guard:v1.2.0            │
         │       header-guard.wasm:application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar        │
         │                                                                       │
         │3. Reference it from WasmPlugin.spec.url:                              │
         │     url: oci://registry.anihpj.dev/wasm/header-guard:v1.2.0           │
         │     sha256: 4f2a91c0...        # pin it → forces IfNotPresent pulls   │
         │                                                                       │
         │4. istio-agent on each matched pod pulls the OCI artifact like a       │
         │   container image, verifies sha256, loads it into the Wasm VM         │
         │                                                                       │
         │5. Roll out a new version: bump the tag + sha256, kubectl apply →      │
         │   istio-agent re-pulls, NO pod restart, NO proxy restart needed       │
         └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - imagePullPolicy's hidden rule (a genuine exam trap): unspecified
           defaults to IfNotPresent — UNLESS the url tag is literally
           :latest, in which case Istio silently switches to Always; and
           if you set sha256 at all, Istio forces IfNotPresent regardless
           of what imagePullPolicy says, because a pinned digest never
           needs re-pulling

    15.9  EnvoyFilter Ordering & Governance — priority, Multi-Filter Precedence, and "Use With Care"
         - DEFINITION: EnvoyFilter has its OWN top-level spec.priority:
           int32 field (separate from WasmPlugin's priority) that,
           together with namespace scope and creation time, decides which
           patch wins when two or more EnvoyFilters touch the same workload
         - Why it matters: anihpj's platform team and an app team could
           both ship an EnvoyFilter patching jobpost-api's HTTP_FILTER
           chain (say, 15.1's local-ratelimit filter and 15.5's Lua
           tagger) — istiod does NOT reject the collision, it silently
           applies both in a defined order; the exam expects you to
           compute that order

         [ENVOYFILTER RESOLUTION ORDER — when multiple filters match one workload]
         ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │MULTIPLE EnvoyFilters MATCHING THE SAME WORKLOAD — resolution order      │
         │                                                                         │
         │STEP 1 — namespace scope (broadest first):                               │
         │  all EnvoyFilters in the config ROOT namespace (usually istio-system)   │
         │  applied first, THEN all matching EnvoyFilters in the workload's OWN    │
         │  namespace (e.g. anihpj)                                                │
         │                                                                         │
         │STEP 2 — within the same namespace scope, patch sets sort by:            │
         │  1. priority          ← spec.priority (int32); LOWEST value first       │
         │  2. creation time      ← older EnvoyFilter objects applied first        │
         │  3. fully-qualified name ← final tiebreaker, alphabetical               │
         │                                                                         │
         │anihpj example: filter-local-ratelimit (priority unset=0) and            │
         │filter-lua-tag (priority: 5) both patch jobpost-api's HTTP_FILTER        │
         │chain → the priority:0 filter's patch set is evaluated first             │
         └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - official guidance on why this is risky in the first place —
           quoted verbatim from istio.io's EnvoyFilter reference page:

         [WHY EnvoyFilter IS A LAST RESORT — direct from the docs]
         ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │WHY THE EXAM TREATS EnvoyFilter AS A LAST RESORT — verbatim from istio.io: │
         │                                                                           │
         │"This feature must be used with care, as incorrect configurations          │
         │could potentially destabilize the entire mesh."                            │
         │                                                                           │
         │"The behavior is undefined if multiple EnvoyFilter configurations          │
         │conflict with each other."                                                 │
         │                                                                           │
         │"Some aspects of this API are deeply tied to the internal                  │
         │implementation ... any envoy configuration provided through this           │
         │mechanism should be carefully monitored across Istio proxy version         │
         │upgrades."                                                                 │
         │                                                                           │
         │Translation for anihpj: reach for VirtualService / AuthorizationPolicy     │
         │/ Telemetry FIRST; EnvoyFilter is the escape hatch, not the front door     │
         └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         [ANIHPJ GOVERNANCE CHECKLIST — practical mitigations, not just theory]
         ┌──────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ Practice                     │ Why (anihpj-specific rationale)                 │
         ├──────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ Always set workloadSelector  │ unscoped EnvoyFilters hit every sidecar in      │
         │   or targetRefs              │ the namespace, not just jobpost-api             │
         │ Set spec.priority explicitly │ don't rely on creation-time tiebreaks that      │
         │                              │ silently reorder after a re-apply/CI re-run     │
         │ Name filters descriptively   │ fully-qualified name is the LAST tiebreaker     │
         │                              │ and shows up in istioctl analyze output         │
         │ Keep one Git-tracked YAML    │ undefined behavior on conflicts means two       │
         │   per concern                │ teams editing the same patch is a real outage   │
         │ Re-validate after every      │ EnvoyFilter is tied to Envoy's internal xDS     │
         │   Istio minor upgrade        │ shape, which can change between releases        │
         │ Prefer WasmPlugin/native     │ exhaust VirtualService, AuthorizationPolicy,    │
         │   CRDs before EnvoyFilter    │ Telemetry, WasmPlugin — in that order           │
         └──────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         - anihpj rule of thumb closing this chapter: EnvoyFilter and
           WasmPlugin are both "you write the logic" escape hatches — but
           EnvoyFilter edits Envoy's raw xDS config with NO stability
           guarantee across Istio versions, while WasmPlugin runs your
           code inside a sandboxed VM with a versioned, documented CRD
           surface; when either mechanism CAN solve the problem, WasmPlugin
           is the one that survives your next Istio upgrade unscathed

    [UNDER THE HOOD 🔧 — LOCAL + GLOBAL BOTH LIVE: WHO CHECKS FIRST?]
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ REQUEST-BY-REQUEST WALKTHROUGH — local + global ratelimit both live      │
         │                                                                          │
         │ SETUP: the platform team ships 15.1's jobpost-api-local-ratelimit (100   │
         │ tok/s per pod, no priority set). The app team separately ships 15.7's    │
         │ two-patch global filter, jobpost-global-ratelimit-filter (1000 req/min   │
         │ per IP via RLS+Redis, no priority set either). Both patch the SAME       │
         │ SIDECAR_INBOUND HTTP_FILTER chain with INSERT_BEFORE the router — a      │
         │ collision 15.9 says istiod will NOT reject.                              │
         │                                                                          │
         │ STEP 1  Resolve WHICH patch compiles into the chain first (15.9's rule): │
         │         same namespace (anihpj), same priority (both default to 0) →     │
         │         tiebreak = alphabetical name. "jobpost-api-local..." sorts       │
         │         before "jobpost-global..." ('a' < 'g') → LOCAL compiles first    │
         │                                                                          │
         │ STEP 2  Envoy always runs HTTP filters in chain order, so every request  │
         │         hits envoy.filters.http.local_ratelimit FIRST:                   │
         │           bucket EMPTY → instant 429, RLS/Redis NEVER contacted (free)   │
         │           bucket OK    → 1 token consumed → falls through to STEP 3      │
         │                                                                          │
         │ STEP 3  envoy.filters.http.ratelimit (global) runs SECOND:               │
         │           gRPC check to RLS (~1-5ms) → Redis counter for source IP       │
         │           over 1000/min  → 429 + Retry-After: 60s                        │
         │           under 1000/min → forwarded to Django (both gates passed)       │
         │                                                                          │
         │ THE ACCIDENT: this cheap-check-first order exists ONLY because           │
         │ "jobpost-api-local-ratelimit" happens to sort before "jobpost-global-    │
         │ ratelimit-filter". Rename or re-create the global filter as, say,        │
         │ "aaa-global-ratelimit", and the order FLIPS — every request now pays     │
         │ the RLS/Redis round trip BEFORE the free local check, wasting RLS        │
         │ capacity exactly when jobpost-api is already under the heaviest load.    │
         │                                                                          │
         │ THE FIX: never rely on the accident — set spec.priority explicitly       │
         │ (local: priority 0, global: priority 10 — LOWEST runs first, per 15.9)   │
         │ so the free check always guards the expensive one, no matter what        │
         │ either filter is named or which team applies their YAML first.           │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    [SPEED TIPS]
         ⚡ Default to LOCAL first — zero extra infra, and it answers "protect
            one pod" questions instantly; reach for GLOBAL only when the
            requirement names a client (an IP, a user, an API key) across ALL
            pods at once
         ⚡ Read fillInterval before anything else in a token-bucket YAML —
            fillInterval: 60s disguised as 1s is this chapter's single most
            common exam trap ("100 req/s" silently becomes "100 req/min")
         ⚡ Before writing a new EnvoyFilter, check whether VirtualService,
            AuthorizationPolicy, Telemetry, or WasmPlugin already solves it —
            EnvoyFilter is istio.io's own "last resort," and every extra one
            you ship is another unscoped blast radius to review later
         ⚡ Always set workloadSelector (or targetRefs) AND spec.priority on
            every EnvoyFilter/WasmPlugin — skipping either leaves you exposed
            to 15.9's silent namespace-wide match or an alphabetical-tiebreak
            accident like the one walked through above
         ⚡ Prefer WasmPlugin over a Lua EnvoyFilter the moment the logic gets
            tests, versions, or a second team touching it — sha256-pinned OCI
            images roll forward/back with zero pod restarts; Lua's inline_code
            has no such safety net
         ⚡ Map failure_mode_deny straight to the business stake: true
            (fail-closed) protects a paying customer's quota at the cost of an
            outage if RLS dies; false (fail-open) never blocks legitimate
            traffic but lets abuse through while RLS is down

    [COMMANDS CHEAT-CARD]
         ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ Command                                                     │ What it proves / does                                                  │
         ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
         │ kubectl apply -f <file>.yaml -n anihpj                      │ Ship or update an EnvoyFilter / WasmPlugin — zero pod restarts         │
         │ kubectl get envoyfilters -n anihpj                          │ List every EnvoyFilter patching this namespace (spot 15.9 collisions)  │
         │ kubectl describe envoyfilter <name> -n anihpj               │ Confirm workloadSelector + priority match what you intended            │
         │ istioctl proxy-config listener deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj │ Dump the live listener config Envoy is actually running                │
         │   ... -o json | grep -i ratelimit                           │ Prove LOCAL and/or GLOBAL ratelimit filter is compiled into the chain  │
         │   ... -o json | grep -i wasm                                │ Prove the Wasm module actually loaded into Envoy's sandboxed VM        │
         │ kubectl get wasmplugins -n anihpj                           │ Confirm istiod accepted the WasmPlugin CRD                             │
         │ curl -sI http://jobpost-api:8000/jobs/ | grep x-anihpj      │ Confirm a WasmPlugin/Lua filter actually ran on a real request         │
         │ for i in $(seq 1 150); do curl ...; done | sort | uniq -c   │ Trip a limiter for real — count 200s vs 429s directly                  │
         │ istioctl analyze -n anihpj                                  │ Catch EnvoyFilter/WasmPlugin misconfigs before they hit a live sidecar │
         │ kubectl delete envoyfilter <name> -n anihpj                 │ Emergency undo — the limit disappears instantly, no restart needed     │
         └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    [PRACTICE DRILL 🧪 — 8 minutes]
         🧪 Cap jobpost-api at 100 req/s per pod, right now:
         1. (2 min) Copy 15.1's EnvoyFilter into local-ratelimit.yaml: set
            workloadSelector labels app: jobpost-api, maxTokens: 100,
            tokensPerFill: 100, fillInterval: 1s
         2. (1 min) kubectl apply -f local-ratelimit.yaml -n anihpj
         3. (2 min) Verify it's live: istioctl proxy-config listener
            deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj -o json | grep local_ratelimit
         4. (2 min) Trip it: fire 150 quick requests at jobpost-api's /jobs/
            endpoint and tally status codes with sort | uniq -c — confirm
            roughly 100 200s and 50 429s
         5. (1 min) Clean up: kubectl delete envoyfilter
            jobpost-api-local-ratelimit -n anihpj and confirm the limit
            disappears instantly, no pod restart

         │         fillInterval — the same three knobs behind every limiter above     │
         │                                     │                                      │
         │                                     ▼                                      │
         │   15.5, 15.8  WHEN NO CRD IS ENOUGH  WasmPlugin (sandboxed, OCI-shipped,   │
         │               versioned) vs Lua EnvoyFilter (inline, fast, riskier)        │
         │                                     │                                      │
         │                                     ▼                                      │
         │   15.6  THE GRAMMAR  every EnvoyFilter patch = applyTo (WHERE) +           │
         │         context (WHEN) + operation (HOW) — one triple, every filter        │
         │         above uses it                                                      │
         │                                     │                                      │
         │                                     ▼                                      │
         │   15.7  WIRED FOR REAL  envoy.filters.http.ratelimit needs 2 patches:      │
         │         HTTP_FILTER to insert it, VIRTUAL_HOST to attach its actions       │
         │                                     │                                      │
         │                                     ▼                                      │
         │   15.9  GOVERNED  priority → creation time → name decides who wins         │
         │         when EnvoyFilters collide; istio.io calls this "use with care"     │
         │                                     │                                      │
         │                                     ▼                                      │
         │   RESULT  jobpost-api survives a retry storm, a scraper, and a gap in      │
         │           Istio's own CRDs — without one line of Django code touched       │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         In one paragraph: Chapter 15 starts where Chapter 14 leaves off — a
         jobpost-api that is finally live and healthy — and asks what stops a
         single caller from ruining that. 15.1-15.3 give you the three levers
         (local, global, shaping); 15.4 supplies the math that makes all
         three predictable; 15.5 and 15.8 open a second door for anything
         none of Istio's CRDs cover, weighing a sandboxed WasmPlugin against
         a quicker but riskier Lua EnvoyFilter; 15.6 hands you the grammar
         every EnvoyFilter patch is built from; 15.7 uses that grammar to
         wire up global rate limiting for real; and 15.9 closes the chapter
         with the discipline to run more than one EnvoyFilter safely —
         because, as istio.io itself warns, this is a mechanism that must be
         used with care.

Chapter 16: Multi-Cluster and Advanced Scenarios
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Chapter 16 of 14-16 (Part 8)  ·  Difficulty: 🔴 Advanced  ·  Extends Traffic Management (35%) + Install/Upgrade/Config (20%) — not its own graded domain

    WHY THIS MATTERS
    anihpj no longer fits inside one cluster or one interception model.
    EU jobseekers hitting jobpost-api from Frankfurt and US jobseekers
    hitting the same API from Virginia both expect sub-100ms responses,
    and pinning either region to a single cluster means someone's
    request crosses an ocean on every call. At the same time, seven
    sidecar-injected services times every replica is real memory the
    platform team pays for on every node, and low-traffic services like
    notification-service and location-service burn a full Envoy sidecar
    just to say "mTLS, please" a handful of times a minute. Layered on
    top of both problems, anihpj's original Postgres instance was never
    containerized — it still runs as a VM with real disks attached,
    sitting just outside the mesh's mTLS boundary until it gets a
    WorkloadEntry and joins like any other workload. Chapter 16 is where
    anihpj's mesh stops being "one cluster, one interception model,
    containers only" and becomes whatever shape the business actually
    needs: multiple clusters bridged by a shared root of trust, sidecar
    and sidecar-free namespaces coexisting under one mesh, and a legacy
    VM treated as a first-class citizen.

    LEARNING OBJECTIVES
      ✅ Explain Multi-Primary vs Primary-Remote control planes and
         single- vs multi-network topologies, and pick the right
         combination for anihpj's actual EU/US split
      ✅ Bring the legacy PostgreSQL VM into the anihpj mesh with
         WorkloadEntry, WorkloadGroup, and a MESH_INTERNAL ServiceEntry,
         and trace the CSR flow that earns it a SPIFFE certificate
      ✅ Describe how ztunnel and the optional waypoint proxy split L4
         and L7 responsibility in ambient mesh, and calculate anihpj's
         memory savings versus all-sidecar
      ✅ Trace an HBONE tunnel end-to-end and state which port (15008)
         and which identity (the source pod's SPIFFE, never the node's)
         it carries
      ✅ Walk any anihpj service through the sidecar-vs-ambient decision
         tree and justify the resulting mode from its actual L7 and
         in-pod requirements
      ✅ Enable ambient mode for a namespace and scope a waypoint to it
         with istioctl waypoint apply/generate/list/status/delete and
         istio.io/use-waypoint labels
      ✅ Diagnose the two most common multi-cluster failures — a missing
         shared root CA and a missing or misconfigured east-west gateway
         — from symptoms alone

    EXAM/ICA RELEVANCE
    Chapter 16 has no dedicated ICA domain of its own — all of Part 8
    (Chapters 14-16) extends Traffic Management (35%) and Installation,
    Upgrade & Configuration (20%) to production scale rather than
    opening a new graded topic. Multi-cluster questions (16.1, 16.7) are
    graded as advanced Traffic Management: locality-weighted routing and
    failover reuse the same VirtualService/DestinationRule primitives
    from Chapters 6-7, just spanning a cluster boundary. Ambient-mode
    questions (16.3-16.6) fall under Installation's official "Sidecar or
    Ambient Mode" objective (see 4.11) — expect the exam to test WHEN
    you reach for ambient, not only how to enable it. VM-workload
    questions (16.2, 16.8) sit under "Connecting In-Mesh Workloads to
    External Workloads and Services," specifically its external-to-
    in-mesh direction (the reverse direction, ServiceEntry, is Chapter
    8). Treat this chapter as the hardest-mode replay of skills you
    already own, not a new syllabus.

    [CHAPTER 16 SECTION MAP — how the nine sections group together]
    ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
